adoption.heading: 2026-11-23: Master plan revision adopted as the frontier

thesis: Yamakan is the production system of record for AI filmmaking: every shot stays a revisable, attributable object with a stated cost in time and data, inside one local project that the creator owns — whichever model, renderer or agent produced it.
commonContract: Step 0 of every card: verify live `main` and reproduce the gap the card describes. If the gap is already closed, record ALREADY_SATISFIED with evidence for that part and do only what remains.

No new store, scheduler, project format or authority. The canonical project and timeline, original media, old receipts and each writer's history are preserved; a stored format moves only by an additive version step that still reads every older version.

Existing scopes and the human-only rule are kept, every command input stays strict, bounded and path-free, every mutation keeps a receipt or refuses a request id, and `tests/parity.test.ts` holds for REST and MCP.

Nothing is imported without provenance and licence closure: `npm run provenance:check` and `npm run brand:check` pass, and a new file under a donor root is declared in `docs/provenance/import-policy.json`.
`npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check` and `npm test` pass; `npm run test:studio` when Studio code is touched and `npm run test:e2e` when browser interface code is touched.

Real end-to-end qualification leaves evidence under `docs/evidence/` with the head SHA and the host. A missing tool or a skipped step is recorded BLOCKED, never PASS. Each qualify script records free disk, free memory, power state and load first, and ends BLOCKED below its stated need. An unmeasured need is written as unmeasured.

Models and providers stay off. No spend and no download happens unless the card's gate and a recorded founder decision allow it. The frozen resource policy and qualification policy are not changed by a card.
Each pull request gets a fresh independent review, CI on its exact head and a normal merge. No force-push, and no merge of a pull request whose checks did not run.

stages.name: Truth and frontier
stages.purpose: Make the record match the code: adopt the revision, date the stale documents, wire the plan check, settle one consent rule, and widen Windows CI.
stages.exit: MPR-001 recorded; MPR-002, MPR-003 and MPR-010 verified; MPR-804 verified or recorded blocked on FD-8.

stages.name: The Revisable Shot
stages.purpose: The shortest path to the thesis: every take carries its request as a hashed record, a generation lands on the shot it was made for, a take can be revised from its own record, and the shot's history can be read. Needs no new model, provider or hardware.
stages.exit: MPR-101 to MPR-107 verified: one shot is generated or rendered onto its shot, revised from its own record, compared and replaced, and its history read, on the founder host with the stand-in route. Measure: in that demonstration nothing outside the revised shot changes (project collateral change, M6p in document 10, is zero). Observation: at least three working editors or creative leads invited by the founder run the demonstration on the founder host and their remarks are recorded; if this is not arranged it is recorded BLOCKED, never PASS.

stages.name: Governed execution
stages.purpose: Default-deny gates for egress, spend and download; a model catalog with three-state capability cells, preflight and typed failures; an honest agent surface with waits, approvals, budgets and an audit feed.
stages.exit: Every card of the stage verified: nothing leaves the computer, spends or downloads without a recorded approval; the catalog, capability report, preflight and typed failures are the only source of model facts; an agent can wait, ask, be budgeted and be audited. Measure: zero unapproved spend, egress or download across the stage's qualification runs (M9 in document 10).

stages.name: Editor depth and interchange
stages.purpose: Put the existing command-only editing into the browser, add first run and the continuity journey, register the production pipeline in the Director, and write a provenance manifest beside every export.
stages.exit: Every card of the stage verified: the editing commands named in the cards are reachable in the browser, the continuity journey passes, the Director shows the production pipeline, and every export has a manifest. Measure: export reliability (M11) and lineage completeness (M13), as document 10 defines them, are both 100% on the stage's qualification runs.

stages.name: Consistency and control
stages.purpose: Entities with approved anchors, per-shot reference delivery reports, one camera and render record per shot, and a consistency measurement harness.
stages.exit: MPR-401, MPR-402, MPR-403 and MPR-405 verified; MPR-404 stays deferred until its trigger is claimed.

stages.name: Qualification and benchmark
stages.purpose: Pre-register the workflow benchmark, run the Yamakan-only baseline and the supervised-agent measure, and only then decide the competitor arm.
stages.exit: MPR-801, MPR-802 and MPR-805 verified, with every comparison still NOT TESTED unless MPR-803 ran after FD-6.

stages.name: Gated expansions
stages.purpose: Cards that stay shut until a founder decision is recorded: local weights, a hosted provider, the credential vault and operating-system user presence.
stages.exit: No exit: each card opens only when its founder decision is recorded, and closes on its own qualification.

tracks.name: Truth and frontier
tracks.purpose: Make the written record match the code and put the plan under a check that CI runs.

tracks.name: The revisable shot
tracks.purpose: Every take keeps its request; a generation lands on its shot; a take can be revised from its own record; the history of a shot can be read.

tracks.name: Model system
tracks.purpose: One catalog, honest capability cells, preflight, default-deny gates, typed failures, licence gates, and the gated qualification of local and hosted routes.

tracks.name: Director
tracks.purpose: A planner and proposer over typed commands: a registered production pipeline, a plan view, hash-bound edit proposals and a reasoned route order. Yamakan ships no language model.

tracks.name: Consistency and camera
tracks.purpose: Reference management that says what a route will receive, one camera and render record per shot, and a harness that measures consistency instead of asserting it.

tracks.name: Agentic production
tracks.purpose: An honest tool list, waits and events, approvals that survive a restart, budgets, an audit feed, and a fair Blender queue, all inside the existing job and permission authorities.

tracks.name: Editor and experience
tracks.purpose: Put the editing commands that already exist into the browser, add first run and a continuity journey, and prepare the Arabic review.

tracks.name: Portability and interchange
tracks.purpose: A provenance manifest beside every export and lineage that survives OpenTimelineIO.

tracks.name: Benchmark and qualification
tracks.purpose: Pre-registered measurement of the thesis, Windows CI, and the supervised-agent measure; a comparison is stated only after it was run.

states.meaning: No unmet dependency. Work may start once MPR-001 is merged and the founder's quoted words authorise building this card; a card that creates a listed new file also waits for MPR-003, because the package check refuses the file until then.
At least one dependency is not verified yet.
Waits for something outside engineering, named on the card (a founder decision, a person, a tool or a machine).
Deliberately not scheduled; kept so the reason and the reopening condition are on record.
Built, or being built, and not yet verified. The pull request that builds a card sets it when it creates one of the card's listed new files.
Complete: every listed new file exists and `evidence` names the merge commit. The implementation lead sets it in a reviewed pull request.

founderDecisions.question: Four answers: (a) adopt this revision as the current plan; (b) close draft PRs #85 and #86 as superseded evidence; (c) merge the planning pull request; (d) build the cards in the order of FD-11, each behind its own gates?
founderDecisions.default: The System Supremacy programme stays the only authority; this package stays a proposal.
founderDecisions.note: MPR-001 records the answer, and cannot start before the planning pull request is merged on the founder's explicit word. Adoption alone authorises neither that merge nor building the cards. No card is built before FD-1 is recorded; that rule is carried by the meaning of the states and is not written as a dependency on each card.

founderDecisions.question: May the full generation request, prompt included, be stored in the project and travel with backups and, when the person chooses, with exports?
founderDecisions.recommended: Yes in the project and backups; opt-in for exports.
founderDecisions.default: No prompt in the take record. The generation ledger, the shot notes and backups keep the full prompts they keep today; revising from a take cannot refill the prompt.

founderDecisions.question: Is the Kaggle route a product feature or a founder-only experiment?
founderDecisions.recommended: A product feature marked experimental, after containment and a reading of Kaggle's terms.
founderDecisions.note: The containment, gate and failure cards are needed whichever way this goes; the listed cards change what they deliver. Optional real-route observations in other cards are recorded BLOCKED without it.

founderDecisions.question: May small, permissively licensed weights be downloaded for local captions, voice and image, for qualification first?
founderDecisions.recommended: Yes for captions and voice on this PC, for qualification only; image later.
founderDecisions.default: No weights on the PC, as today.

founderDecisions.question: May a legal review of customer-credential hosted providers start?
founderDecisions.recommended: Yes, review only; no provider code that talks to a real service.
founderDecisions.default: No hosted provider work beyond the loopback fake.

founderDecisions.question: May the benchmark's competitor arm be paid for and volunteer raters recruited?
founderDecisions.recommended: Decide after the Yamakan-only baseline exists.
founderDecisions.default: No competitor arm; every comparison stays NOT TESTED.

founderDecisions.question: May the revision-cost protocol be published as an open benchmark description?
Run the full test suite on Windows in CI?
founderDecisions.default: One narrow Windows job, as today.

founderDecisions.question: Require operating-system user presence for human-only commands?
founderDecisions.recommended: Yes, as an option the person can turn on; keep the launch secret.

founderDecisions.question: Remove the personal Kaggle account id from committed notebook metadata?
Order of work: finish the in-flight Blender pull requests, then Stage 1 before any new feature stream?
founderDecisions.default: The implementation owner continues the current streams.
founderDecisions.note: Decides the order of every card, so it is not repeated on each card.

tasks.title: Record plan adoption, point specs/CURRENT.md at the new frontier, settle PRs #85/#86

`docs/FOUNDER_DECISION_RECORD.md` holds dated sections in date order; the last is '2026-11-10: Blender integration, and YouMind OpenLab as its extension'. Entries use the bullets 'Source and form', 'Planning reference', 'Authorized scope', 'Still not authorized', 'Effect' and state that the instruction was given in chat with no signed approval and no founder GitHub review.

The '2026-10-25: Ultimate Master Plan autonomous execution' entry of `docs/FOUNDER_DECISION_RECORD.md` lists, under 'Still not authorized', merging or discarding planning PRs #85/#86 without a deliberate reconciliation decision. No later entry lifts that. FD-1 is that decision.

PR #85 (branch research/competitive-video-rea-2026-10-22, head 7472a14) and PR #86 (branch research/ultimate-master-plan-2026-10-23, head caec7d9c225d430e1a42f8af8fd8eebc17c5317d) are recorded as intact drafts by `specs/CURRENT.md` ('85/86 intact') and by the `rule` and `sourceSha` fields of `docs/research/YAMAKAN_SYSTEM_SUPREMACY_REA/LEGACY_RECONCILIATION.json`. At main 7b1ca46ce20efaa603be12b51d57aee04a3f5f72 the planning package is not tracked: `git status --short` in the planning worktree shows the package directory as untracked. This card can start only after the planning pull request is merged.

Precedent for the shape of this change: merge 4a96b02 (PR #31, branch named docs/founder-start-authorization) and merge 364e041 (PR #159, branch named docs/record-opus-handoff) each recorded a founder authorisation and repointed `specs/CURRENT.md` in a documentation pull request (PR #31 changed 3 files; PR #159 changed 14) (`git log --merges`). PR #159 also changed the header of `docs/research/YAMAKAN_SYSTEM_SUPREMACY_REA/TASK_REGISTRY.json` (`git log --first-parent` on that file); this card leaves the matching header change of the new registry to MPR-003.

Read, and run in the planning worktree at 7b1ca46: the package's own check `docs/research/YAMAKAN_MASTER_PLAN_REVISION_2026_11/tools/validate-addendum.mjs` requires the registry header to say `status` `PROPOSED_NOT_AUTHORIZED` and `implementationAuthorized` false, and requires the line 'Status: PROPOSED — planning only. Not authority until founder review.' near the top of every package document. So this card edits no package file; MPR-003 changes the check, the header and the status lines together. The check may still change before the planning pull request merges.
interfaces: No command, schema, type or script changes

`specs/CURRENT.md` gains one new second-level section placed directly under the title, headed 'Master plan revision adopted (<date of the founder's instruction>)', and every existing section stays below it, unchanged

`docs/FOUNDER_DECISION_RECORD.md` gains one new second-level section appended at the end, headed '<date of the instruction>: Master plan revision adopted as the frontier', with the bullets 'Source and form', 'Planning reference', 'Authorized scope', 'Pull requests #85 and #86', 'Still not authorized', 'Effect'

implementationSequence: Verify live main: confirm the planning package directory `docs/research/YAMAKAN_MASTER_PLAN_REVISION_2026_11` is tracked on main, that the first section of `specs/CURRENT.md` is still 'Implementation under founder handoff (2026-11-04)', and that `docs/FOUNDER_DECISION_RECORD.md` has no entry adopting the revision. With no instruction, change nothing and leave the card EXTERNAL_BLOCKED. If the founder adopts the revision but says nothing about #85/#86, record the adoption and write under 'Pull requests #85 and #86' that the disposition is not decided and both stay open and untouched. Prove the change before review: `git diff --numstat origin/main -- docs/FOUNDER_DECISION_RECORD.md` shows 0 deleted lines; `git diff --name-only origin/main` lists exactly the two target files; every relative link in the two new sections resolves to a file tracked on main and every anchor matches a heading of the target file.

Confirm with `gh pr view` and with `git ls-remote --heads origin <branch>` that each branch still points at its recorded commit.

Verify main after the merge (re-run the link check at the merge commit) and have the implementation lead add the merge to ledger 12 in the next ledger update, as the System Supremacy handoff document requires; the ledger is not edited in this pull request.

`docs/FOUNDER_DECISION_RECORD.md` ends with one new section that quotes the founder verbatim; the diff of that file has additions only.

Link check over the two new sections: each relative path passes `git ls-files --error-unmatch <path>` and each anchor equals the GitHub slug of a heading in the target file; paste the command and its output in the pull request.
`npm run brand:check` and `npm run provenance:check` pass; exact-head CI (the `qualify` job of `.github/workflows/qualify.yml`) is green. No test file is added because no behaviour changes.

A diff that deletes or rewrites any existing line of `docs/FOUNDER_DECISION_RECORD.md` is refused in review (the additions-only check fails).

The proof is the post-merge check on main at the merge commit: the link check output and the `gh pr view 85` and `gh pr view 86` outputs, quoted in the pull request and in the next ledger update. A check that could not be run (for example `gh` not signed in) is reported as BLOCKED, not as passed.

The new section of `specs/CURRENT.md` is at most 12 lines and the record entry at most 8 bullets, so the frontier can be read in one screen.

`docs/PLAN_FREEZE_MANIFEST.md` and every other file it hashes are not edited; no hash is recomputed.
The System Supremacy registry, its ledger and its handoff document are not edited; this card does not complete SS-019, which still owns the final frontier and release evidence packet.
No file of the planning package is edited: its registry header and status lines keep the proposed form, so the package check keeps passing between this merge and MPR-003.
The planner never performs this card; it is done by the implementation owner after the founder's instruction.
definitionOfDone: Merged by a normal merge with a fresh independent review and exact-head CI; main verified after the merge.
The pull request author is the implementation owner and the description quotes the founder's instruction.
GitHub state of #85 and #86 matches the record, with both branches retained.
Ledger 12 carries the merge in the lead's next ledger update.
risks: The instruction may be partial or ambiguous. Mitigation: record only what was written, mark the rest 'not decided', and keep the card open for the missing half.

A reviewer may read the freeze manifest as forbidding any change to the founder record, whose hash already differs on main. Mitigation: cite the additions-only history since the freeze commit in the pull request; do not edit or re-hash the manifest.
The recorded head commits of #85/#86 may be out of date, because they can move after 2026-11-22, when their live state was last read. Mitigation: step 2 reads the live state and stops on a mismatch.
Closing a pull request is outward-facing. Mitigation: it is done only on the founder's instruction, branches are kept, and a closed pull request can be reopened.

Founder statements dated after the record's last entry are cited elsewhere (the ledger cites decisions made after 2026-11-10; by reading) but have no entry. Mitigation: this card does not backfill them from memory; it flags the gap to the founder.
blockingExternalRequirements: FD-1: the founder's instruction in chat adopting the revision as the frontier and stating the disposition of draft PRs #85 and #86.
The planning pull request that carries `docs/research/YAMAKAN_MASTER_PLAN_REVISION_2026_11` must be merged to main first, which itself needs the founder's instruction.
tasks.rollback: Back out with a follow-up documentation pull request that removes the new top section of `specs/CURRENT.md` and appends a dated reversal entry to `docs/FOUNDER_DECISION_RECORD.md`; the adoption entry itself is never deleted. Reopen #85 and #86 on GitHub if they were closed; their branches were never deleted. No project data is involved.

tasks.title: Decide and close the pinned-take path past consent revocation at the commit point
tasks.objective: When a person revokes consent, a take made with that person's references does not return to the timeline through undo, redo, placing or restore; the open consent finding in ledger 12 is closed with a test as evidence, whichever way the rule is decided.
currentBaseline: Ledger 12 (`docs/research/YAMAKAN_SYSTEM_SUPREMACY_REA/12_EXECUTION_AND_CONTINUATION_LEDGER.md`) lists an open finding marked 'by reading, not run': a take with reference pins and no continuity references could return through undo after its consent is revoked, and it says the case should be run first.

That ledger line is stale. PR #179 (commit 84415da, merge 19613c1) has since run the case and kept the behaviour on purpose: the test 'a take with only a pinned pack can return after revocation, as any project media can' in `tests/story-packs.test.ts` saves a pack and a story, assembles, removes the clip, calls `yamakan.consent.revoke`, and then asserts that `yamakan.project.undo` brings the clip back and that a later `clip.add` of the same media is accepted. So the gap reproduces today by design; closing it is a change of a documented rule, not a repair of an unknown fault.

`docs/OPERATIONAL_CONTRACTS.md` states the present rule in three passages: redo of an assembly does not check a pinned pack's consents again; after revocation a take with only a pinned pack, and other media, can still be placed; undo and redo run the commit point's check on newly presented media, but a take with only a pinned pack is not gated there. The receipt `docs/evidence/ultimate/consent-gate.md` lists it under 'What is left open' with the reason that a pin does not show the take depicts that person.

By reading, not run: the commit point is `assertPlacementConsent(c, before, after)` in `core/continuity.ts`, called once from `core/store.ts` for every operation except `project.create`. It works out the newly presented media hashes, calls `assertLinkedMediaNotRevoked`, then scans this project's story versions and, for each take, checks only `lineage.continuity` and only when `lineage.outputHash` is among the placed hashes. It reads neither `shot.referencePacks` nor `lineage.inputs`, and a take with no lineage is never matched.

By reading, not run: pack pins are checked only when `yamakan.story.save`, `yamakan.story.assemble` or `yamakan.take.apply` run, through `verifyStory`, `verifyPin` and `verifyConsents` in `core/story.ts`. Direct `clip.add` and `clip.replaceMedia` operations, `yamakan.project.undo`, `yamakan.project.redo` and `yamakan.project.restore` do not pass through them.

By reading, not run: a second form of the same gap exists. `addMadeVideo` in `src/create/create-story.ts` writes a take with empty `referencePacks` and a lineage that has `outputHash` and `inputs` but no continuity, so a take made from a consented reference picture is not matched at the commit point either.

The commands involved do not change: `yamakan.project.undo` and `yamakan.project.redo` take the strict input `{projectId, expectedRevision}` under scope `project:write`; `yamakan.consent.revoke` is human-only under scope `consent:revoke`. `tests/continuity-consent.test.ts` covers takes that carry continuity references and passes today (read, not run by this card's author).
`npm run qualify:consent-gate` (`scripts/qualify-consent-gate.mjs`) drives a real browser and is not part of CI; its last receipt predates this card.
interfaces: No new command, scope, table, schema, document format or setting

`assertPlacementConsent(c, before, after)` in `core/continuity.ts` keeps its signature and its single call site in `core/store.ts`; only the set of takes it matches and the media it passes to the revocation check grow
`assertLinkedMediaNotRevoked(db, hashes, recovering)` and the module-private `linksOf` are reused unchanged

Refusal: error code `VALIDATION`, the message `assertLinkedMediaNotRevoked` already throws, unchanged (it begins 'This person's consent was revoked'; on a restore over an unreadable head it begins 'This revision shows media whose person's consent was revoked'); the head revision does not move and no receipt is written for the refused commit
Way back, unchanged: a pack version saved with a newer consent for that media through `yamakan.pack.save`, then `yamakan.story.save`
`yamakan.project.undo`, `yamakan.project.redo`, `yamakan.project.restore` and `yamakan.project.applyBatch` keep their inputs, scopes and receipts

sourceReuse: `assertPlacementConsent`, `assertLinkedMediaNotRevoked`, `linksOf` and its `packLinks` cache in `core/continuity.ts`.

Record the decision before the code. In the existing loop over this project's story versions, match a take to a newly presented medium by `lineage.outputHash`, or, when the take has no lineage, by `take.assetId` resolved to its hash in the after-state's assets. For each matched take collect the `assetHash` of every `lineage.inputs` entry and, for every pack version its shot pins, the consent-linked hashes returned by `linksOf`; pass the collected hashes to the existing `assertLinkedMediaNotRevoked` with the same `recovering` value the function already uses. Keep the continuity branch as it is. Add no table, no column and no new call site.

tasks.title: Record every take's generation or render request as an immutable, hashed take record
tasks.evidence: Merged as 6b9fb8e (PR #291), c7c9929 (PR #292) and 399172af3a33b1f23398f2b9988cef8ee0687830 (PR #296, FD-2); qualify:revisable-shot and qualify:create-durable passed at 2fc6472 on GitHub's Linux machine (run 45215659043); the Blender arm is BLOCKED; docs/evidence/ultimate/MPR-101-take-record.md
tasks.objective: Every generated or rendered take carries a complete, immutable record of how it was made, so a person can see it, repeat it and revise it later. The story document stays small because the take points to its record by hash.
currentBaseline: `core/story.ts`: `TakeLineageSchema` is `{label?, outputHash, inputs (at most 8), continuity? (at most 8)}`, `TakeSchema` is `{id, assetId, sourceStartTicks, lineage?}` and `StoryDocumentSchema` has `formatVersion: z.literal(1)`. No field holds a request.

`src/create/create-story.ts` `addMadeVideo` writes seed, steps and model into the free-text `lineage.label` and the prompt (cut to 2,000 characters) into the shot's `notes`, and makes one new shot per made video in the story titled 'Made in Create' (`CREATE_STORY_TITLE`).

`core/engines/generation.ts`: the ledger row type `GenerationRecord` (the JSON payload of a `jobs` row of kind `remote-generation`; `core/jobs.ts` `REMOTE_GENERATION`, `generationLedger`) holds recipe, prompt, seed, width, height, durationFrames, firstFrameAssetId, inputs, `startedAt`, state and `imported {assetId, lineage}`. It has no finish time, no usage figure and no link to a story, shot or take. `GenerationLineage` keeps `promptHash` only.

`core/document-ref.ts`: `DocumentKind` is `studio | cinemaScene | story | referencePack | captions | lut | promptPresets` and `DOCUMENT_SCHEMA_VERSIONS` maps every kind to 1. `core/documents.ts` `validateDocument(kind, schemaVersion, raw)` refuses any other version. The command `yamakan.document.capability` returns only `{available, turnedOff}`.

`core/store.ts`: table `creative_documents(hash, kind, schema_version, asset_ids, bytes, byte_length, object_digests)` accepts any kind name of 1 to 32 letters since `SCHEMA_V14`; table `story_document_versions(project_id, document_id, content_hash, revision)` records the versions a project held, and every reader filters by kind (`core/continuity.ts`, the store's `held` check). `core/canonical.ts` caps a project's `documents` array at 32.

Readers that accept only story version 1: `readStory`, `yamakan.story.assemble` and `yamakan.take.apply` in `core/command/registry.ts`, `renderStoryShot` in `core/director/cinema-pipeline.ts`, the story loop of `assertPlacementConsent` in `core/continuity.ts` (it reports a story it cannot parse as damaged), and `yamakan.story.save`, which commits with a hard-coded `schemaVersion: 1`. The browser type `CreateStory` in `src/create/create-story.ts` has `formatVersion: 1`.

Blender: the render job payload `BlenderPayload` (`core/jobs.ts`, format `blender/1`) holds `scene`, `name` and an optional plate pin; on success the job stores `artifact` as `asset:<assetId>`. The `jobs` and `attempts` tables have no time column, and nothing links the job to a story shot or take.
`yamakan.project.export` returns the canonical project with document references only (no document bytes). `command_receipts` keeps `request_digest`, not the request.
interfaces: New document kind `takeRecord` in `DocumentKind` (`core/document-ref.ts`); document format `yamakan.take-record`, `formatVersion` 1. New file `core/take-record.ts` exports `TakeRecordSchema`, type `TakeRecord`, `TAKE_RECORD_LIMITS = { recordBytes: 40 * 1024, inputs: 8, changedFields: 16, recordsPerSave: 8 }`, `recordHashOf(record)` (SHA-256 of the canonical JSON), `buildGenerationRecord`, `buildRenderRecord`, `buildDeclaredRecord` and the switch `RECORD_HOLDS_PROMPT`. The name is `TakeRecord` because `GenerationRecord` already names the ledger row.

`TakeRecord` fields (strict object, every string bounded, no host path): `format`; `formatVersion`; `origin` (`generation` | `render` | `declared`); `route` (`kaggle` | `comfyui` | `blender` | `receiptFile`, a closed list); `source` (`{generationId}` | `{jobId}` | null); `recipe` (`{id (at most 80 characters), hash}` | null); `model` (`{id (at most 200), revision (at most 80) | null, manifestHash | null, licence (at most 80) | null}` | null); `operation` (an `Operation` name of `core/engines/contract-v2.ts`, or `render`); `request`; `inputs` (at most 8 of `{assetId, assetHash, role}`, role one of `firstFrame`, `lastFrame`, `source`, `mask`, `audio`, `plate`, and, since MPR-202 by OA-15, `reference`); `output {sha256}`; `timings {startedAt, endedAt, importedAt}` (epoch milliseconds or null); `usage {wallMs, quotaSeconds}` (null means not reported); `derivedFromTakeId` (id or null) with `derivedFromRecordHash` (hash or null; the base take's record, so the chain survives the removal of the base take); `changedFields` (at most 16 names from the closed list `REVISION_FIELDS` = `recipe`, `model`, `prompt`, `seed`, `width`, `height`, `durationFrames`, `fps`, `steps`, `firstFrame`, `inputs`, exported from `core/take-record.ts`; always empty until MPR-103 writes it). By OA-5 and OA-16, accepted on 2026-11-23, also: `revisionNote` (1 to 500 characters, only beside a `derivedFromTakeId`, or null; null until MPR-103 writes it) and `reported`, what the run said of itself, only on a generation's record, or null: `{model {id (at most 200), version (at most 80) | null} | null, seed | null, runtime {python | null, torch | null, packages (at most 32 of at most 80) | null} | null}`, each of the form of such a name or not known. A Kaggle run's are its script's own: the packages it asks for, its model and the seed it was sent.

`request` of a generation or declared record: `{kind: 'generation', prompt? (at most `ENGINE_V2_LIMITS.promptChars`, 4,000), promptHash | null, seed | null, width | null, height | null, durationFrames | null, fps | null, steps | null}`. `request` of a render record: `{kind: 'render', blenderVersion (from `BLENDER_PIN.version`), sceneFormat, sceneHash (SHA-256 of the canonical scene of the job payload), width, height, fps, frames, samples, camera {focalLengthMm, sensorWidthMm}, moves {orbitDegrees, dolly?, panDegrees?, shake?}, lighting?, view?, direction? (at most 4 kind and choice pairs)}`. The scene itself is not copied into the record.

Story format version 2 (`core/story.ts`): `TakeSchema` gains optional `recordHash` (64 lower-case hex characters). Version 2 also defines the optional `brief`, scene `sceneText` and shot `intent` fields and the `STORY_LIMITS.textBytes` budget exactly as MPR-106 `interfaces` states them (schema and validation only; nothing writes them in this card). Exports: `StoryDocumentV1Schema`, `StoryDocumentSchema` (version 2, the form written), `StoredStorySchema` (either version) and the pure `upgradeStory(stored)`.

`core/document-ref.ts`: new `DOCUMENT_READ_VERSIONS: Readonly<Record<DocumentKind, readonly number[]>>` (`story: [1, 2]`, `takeRecord: [1]`, every other kind `[1]`). `DOCUMENT_SCHEMA_VERSIONS` stays the version written (`story: 2`, `takeRecord: 1`). `validateDocument` checks membership in the read set and picks the story schema by version.

`yamakan.story.save` (scope `project:write`, mutation, not human-only, receipt kept, compare-and-swap on `expectedRevision` and `expectedContentHash`: all unchanged) accepts a version 1 or version 2 body, stores version 2, and gains optional strict `records` (at most 8): each `{takeId, from}` where `from` is `{generationId}`, `{jobId}` or `{declared: {model (at most 200), revision? (at most 80), prompt (at most 4,000), seed, steps?, licence? (at most 80)}}`. The service builds each record from its own ledger or job row, writes `recordHash` on the named take and commits story and records in one transaction. The result gains `records: [{takeId, recordHash}]`.

New read command `yamakan.take.record` (scope `project:read`, not a mutation, no receipt): strict input `{projectId, documentId, shotId, takeId}`; returns `{recordHash, record}`, or NOT_FOUND 'The take has no generation record.'. `yamakan.take.list` (input unchanged) gains `recordHash` (string or null) on each take.

`yamakan.document.capability` gains `kinds`: for each document kind `{written, read}` (for example `story: {written: 2, read: [1, 2]}`, `takeRecord: {written: 1, read: [1]}`); `available` and `turnedOff` are unchanged. `yamakan.document.commit` refuses kind `takeRecord` with VALIDATION 'A take record is saved with its take.'.

`core/store.ts` `commitDocument` gains a bounded `attachments` argument (at most 8 records) written inside the same transaction and the same `withinDocumentBudget` check: one `creative_documents` row per record (idempotent on its hash) and one `story_document_versions` row `(project_id, the story's document id, recordHash, revision)`, so the existing `held(documentId, contentHash, 'takeRecord')` check answers for records with no SQL schema step.

Ledger row `GenerationRecord` gains optional `endedAt` (set once, at the first terminal state), and by OA-16 optional `reported`, kept when it is first known to have succeeded. `BlenderPayload` gains optional `shot {documentId, shotId}` and `direction`, set by `renderStoryShot`. Rows without these fields read as before.

performanceCriteria: Size arithmetic for the storage choice. Inline: a record is about 1 KiB of fixed fields plus a prompt of up to 4,000 UTF-16 units (about 8,000 bytes of Arabic, 12,000 bytes of CJK), so 1 to 13 KiB (measured since FD-2: a record is at most 35,304 bytes, for a prompt of control characters); 200 shots x 8 takes = 1,600 records = about 1.56 to 20.3 MiB against `STORY_LIMITS.documentBytes` = 262,144 bytes, which is 6 to 80 times the limit; one shot with 8 takes of a 2,000-character Arabic prompt is already about 40 KiB, 15% of the document, and every later story version would keep another copy. By hash: `recordHash` costs about 80 canonical bytes per take, so 1,600 takes cost 128,000 bytes, 49% of the limit. Estimated, not measured; the limits test pins the numbers.

A record is at most 40,960 canonical bytes with at most 8 inputs and 16 changed fields; a save attaches at most 8 records. Worst case for one story: 1,600 x 40 KiB = 62.5 MiB against `DOCUMENT_LIMITS.workspaceDocumentBytes` (4 GiB).
`yamakan.story.save` stays one transaction; the hold checks are indexed point reads, at most 1,600 per save. `yamakan.take.record` reads one row by its hash.

tasks.title: Let a generation target a story shot and append its take on import
tasks.evidence: Merged as aaab5d58250872f5359b1c775e3f6fe8bda2aa44 (PR #299, pinned to 664e9e7); qualify:revisable-shot passed at 29a170a on GitHub's Linux machine (docs/evidence/ultimate/MPR-102-shot-target-receipt.json); main's CI passed; no screen sends a target until MPR-104
tasks.objective: A person can start a generation for a shot that already exists, and bringing the result in adds it to that shot's take stack as a new story version. The timeline changes only when the person later replaces the take.
currentBaseline: `yamakan.generation.start` (`core/command/registry.ts`; scope `project:write`, mutation, human-only, refuses a request id) takes the strict input `{projectId, recipeId, prompt?, seed?, width, height, durationFrames, firstFrameAssetId?, noUnconsentedPerson?}`. It has no way to name a story or a shot.

`core/engines/generation.ts` `createGenerationService`: `start` writes the ledger row with `ledger.begin` before anything is sent and counts `durationFrames` at the project's output frame rate (`framesToTicks(request.durationFrames, rational(num, den))`). The row type `GenerationRecord` has no target field.

`importResult` and `bringIn` (same file) import the one video as a project asset, set `imported {assetId, lineage}` on the row and return it; a repeated call returns the stored `imported`. They make no story change and no timeline change. `yamakan.generation.import` takes `{generationId}` only.

The only path from a generated video to a story today is in the browser: `src/create/CreateWorkspace.tsx` `record()` calls `addMadeVideo` (`src/create/create-story.ts`), which adds a new shot to the story titled 'Made in Create' for every video. No path adds a take to an existing shot.

`core/story.ts` `verifyStory` runs on every story commit and refuses a footage take that does not cover its shot (`Take of shot "<name>" runs past the end of its source.`), a take whose asset is audio, and any shot whose pinned reference pack no longer verifies. `STORY_LIMITS.takesPerShot` is 8.

A story is identified across versions by its stable `documentId` (the project's document reference); each save changes `contentHash`. `core/store.ts` `commitDocument` records the save as a revision with operation `document.commit` and gives no `editStepAuthor` for a story, so every story save ends the project's undo history (`tests/undo-across-documents.test.ts`: 'a story or pack still ends history, so undo cannot bring one back unchecked').
`yamakan.generation.list` hides rows with `dismissed: true`; a start refused before sending is stored as `state: failed, dismissed: true`.
interfaces: `yamakan.generation.start` (scope, human-only rule and request-id refusal unchanged) gains optional strict `target: {documentId, shotId}` (two ids, no path, no text). Without `target` the command behaves exactly as today.

Refusals at start with a target, all raised before `ledger.begin` so nothing is recorded and nothing is sent: NOT_FOUND 'This project has no such story.' (no story document with that id in the project); NOT_FOUND 'The story has no such shot.'; LIMIT_EXCEEDED 'The shot already holds 8 takes; remove one before generating another.' (the number comes from `STORY_LIMITS.takesPerShot`); VALIDATION 'The shot lasts <X> s and this request makes <Y> s; ask for a longer take or shorten the shot.' when `framesToTicks(durationFrames, project rate)` is less than the shot's `durationTicks`.

Ledger row `GenerationRecord` gains optional `target {documentId, shotId}` and optional `take` (the append outcome below). Both live in the row's existing JSON payload: no column and no schema step. A row without them reads as an untargeted generation; `memoryLedger` keeps them in memory like every other field.

`yamakan.generation.import` (input `{generationId}`, scope, human-only rule and request-id refusal unchanged) returns today's `{assetId, lineage}` plus `take`: null when the row has no target; `{appended: true, documentId, shotId, takeId, recordHash, contentHash, revision}`; or `{appended: false, reason, message}` with `reason` one of `story-gone`, `shot-gone`, `shot-full`, `take-too-short`, `story-refused`, `busy`. The asset import itself is unchanged and is never undone by a failed append.

New function `appendGeneratedTake` in `core/takes.ts`: reads the story head by `documentId`, builds the take `{id (new UUID), assetId, sourceStartTicks: 0, lineage: {outputHash, inputs}, recordHash}`, and commits story and take record in one `commitDocument` call through the same verification `yamakan.story.save` uses (`verifyStory`, `verifyStoryContinuity`, MPR-101's record attachment). The shot's `selectedTakeId` is not changed. No timeline operation is issued.
`yamakan.generation.list` and `yamakan.generation.status` gain `target` and `take` (null when absent). Additive; no input change.
Files this card edits that MPR-101 adds (so they are in neither `targets` nor `newFiles`): `core/take-record.ts` (reads `buildGenerationRecord`) and `scripts/qualify-revisable-shot.mjs`.

tasks.title: Add a revision draft read command and record what changed between takes
tasks.objective: A person can open any take, get back the request that made it as an editable draft, change one field and generate a new take whose record says which take it came from and which fields changed. A revision is a new generation from changed inputs; it does not edit the pixels of the earlier take.
currentBaseline: No command returns a take's request. `core/command/registry.ts` has `yamakan.take.list`, `yamakan.take.compare`, `yamakan.take.proposeReplace` (all `project:read`) and `yamakan.take.apply` (`project:write`, mutation, receipt); it has no `yamakan.take.revisionDraft`.

The only place a request can be read back is `yamakan.generation.list`, which returns `prompt` and `seed` for generations a person has not dismissed; a dismissed generation, a take from a receipt file and a take on another shot cannot be reopened as a request.

Create keeps one working draft per project in browser storage (`src/create/CreateWorkspace.tsx`, key `yamakan.create.brief.<projectId>`, type `CreateBrief` in `src/create/create-model.ts`). It is the last thing typed, not the request of a chosen take.

`yamakan.generation.options` reports, per offered model, `recipeId`, `operation`, `model`, `revision`, `licence`, `width`, `height`, `frames`, `fps` and `steps` (from `offeredKaggleRecipes()` in `core/engines/kaggle.ts`) only when the service was told to use the person's Kaggle CLI. `generationOf` in the registry throws CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE 'No local engine is configured for this service.' when no engine is configured.

Nothing records that one take was made from another: `TakeLineageSchema` (`core/story.ts`) holds output and input pins only, and `GenerationRecord` (`core/engines/generation.ts`) has no base-take field.

The replace path exists and is verified (SS-006): `core/takes.ts` `compareTakes` and `proposeReplace`, and `yamakan.take.apply`, which applies the proposal as one `applyOperations` batch (one undo step) and refuses a stale proposal with REVISION_CONFLICT.
interfaces: New read command `yamakan.take.revisionDraft` (scope `project:read`, not a mutation, no receipt; available to agents as every read is). Strict input `{projectId, documentId, shotId, takeId}`.

Its output: `{base: {documentId, shotId, takeId, recordHash, storyContentHash}, draft, complete, startable, checks, reason}`. `draft` is `{recipeId | null, prompt | null, seed | null, width | null, height | null, durationFrames | null, firstFrameAssetId | null}` (the field names of `yamakan.generation.start`) or null. `complete` is true when the draft has every field a start requires. `startable` is true when `complete` and no check is `unavailable`. `checks` is at most 16 of `{field, state, message}` with `field` from `REVISION_FIELDS` or `route` and `state` one of `ok`, `changed`, `unavailable`, `unknown`. `reason` is null or one sentence saying why there is no draft.
The draft never carries `noUnconsentedPerson`: a person states it again for every run, as `core/engines/generation.ts` `start` requires.

Checks against today's offer (and against the MPR-201 catalog once it exists; the output shape does not change): `route` (`unavailable` with the engine's own reason when none is configured; the draft is still returned); `recipe` (`unavailable` 'This model is no longer offered here.' when the recipe id is gone; `changed` 'The model's run script changed since this take; the same request may give a different result.' when the id is offered with another hash); `model` (`changed` when the manifest hash differs); `width`, `height`, `durationFrames` (`changed` with the model's present size and length when they differ); `firstFrame` (`unavailable` 'The still this take started from is no longer in the project.' when the pinned asset is gone or has another hash); `seed` (`unknown` 'This take has no recorded seed; a repeat will differ.' when null); `prompt` (`unknown` when the record holds only a hash and no source for the text is found).

Draft sources by record `origin`: `generation` gives a full draft; `declared` (a receipt file) gives the fields it has with `complete: false`; `render` gives `draft: null` and reason 'This take was rendered with Blender; revise it from its shot direction.'; a take with no record gives `draft: null` and reason 'This take has no generation record.'. When the record holds `promptHash` without text (FD-2 declined), the prompt is taken from the ledger row named by `source.generationId` if that row belongs to this project and its prompt hashes to `promptHash`; otherwise `prompt` is null.

`yamakan.generation.start` (scope `project:write`, mutation, human-only, refuses a request id: unchanged) gains optional `derivedFromTakeId` (an id) and, only beside it, optional `revisionNote` (1 to 500 characters; OA-5, accepted on 2026-11-23). It is valid only together with `target`. Refusals before anything is recorded or sent: VALIDATION 'A revision names the shot it is for.' (no `target`); VALIDATION 'A revision is made for the shot its base take belongs to.' (the take is not in the target shot); VALIDATION 'The base take has no generation request to revise from.' (no record, or a record that is not `request.kind: generation`).

Ledger row `GenerationRecord` gains optional `derivedFrom {takeId, recordHash, revisionNote?}` (written at start, so the base is fixed even if the take is removed later). At import, MPR-102's append passes it to `buildGenerationRecord`, which writes `derivedFromTakeId`, `derivedFromRecordHash` and `changedFields`, and the record's `revisionNote` (OA-5, accepted on 2026-11-23) when the person gave one.

New pure function `diffRequests(base, next)` in `core/take-record.ts` (a file MPR-101 adds): returns the names from `REVISION_FIELDS`, in that order, whose values differ. `recipe` compares id and hash; `model` compares id, revision and manifest hash; `prompt` compares text when both records hold it and `promptHash` otherwise; `firstFrame` compares the hash of the input with role `firstFrame`; `inputs` compares the remaining inputs as a sorted list of role and hash; every other name compares the request field. A field present on one side only counts as changed. An empty list means an exact repeat. The value is computed by the service and is never accepted from a client.

tasks.title: Keep a shot's take replaceable after its clip is split or trimmed
tasks.objective: After a person splits or trims the clip of a shot, the shot's take can still be replaced in one step, with every piece keeping its own place in the take. A clip that cannot be replaced safely is refused with a reason that names the clip.
currentBaseline: `core/takes.ts` `shotClip` refuses whenever `shot.clipIds.length !== 1` with 'The shot is shown by more than one clip on the timeline; replace its takes one clip at a time in the editor.'. The same text is given when the shot has no clip at all, which is the wrong reason.

`core/timeline/operations.ts` `clip.split` inserts the new clip's id after the original in every `shot.clipIds` that holds it, so the shot's clip list stays complete after a split. The first split of a shot's clip therefore ends take replacement for that shot.

`core/takes.ts` `shows(clip, take)` requires `clip.title === null`, the same `assetId` and `clip.sourceStartTicks === take.sourceStartTicks`. `clip.trim` moves `sourceStartTicks`, so a clip trimmed at its start no longer shows any take and `proposeReplace` refuses with 'The shot's clip no longer shows one of this shot's takes; replace it in the editor.'. A clip trimmed only at its end still matches.

`TakeProposalSchema` (`core/takes.ts`) is `format: yamakan.take-proposal`, `formatVersion: z.literal(1)` with `mappings` of exactly one `{clipId, startTicks, durationTicks, from, to}`. A proposal is never stored: `yamakan.take.proposeReplace` computes it and `yamakan.take.apply` recomputes it inside `store.applyOperations` and compares the whole proposal, not only `proposalHash`.

`clip.replaceMedia` (`core/timeline/operations.ts`) already refuses precisely: 'Track is locked.', 'Reset the clip's speed before replacing its take.', 'Relink the clip's unlinked sound before replacing its take.', 'A still take starts at the beginning of its source.', 'The take is shorter than the clip.'. `applyBatch` takes 1 to 64 operations and wraps an error as `Operation N (type): message`.

`clip.remove` and `timeline.rippleDelete` take a removed clip's id out of `shot.clipIds` (a shot can be left with none); `shot.remove` and `scene.remove` leave their clips on the timeline. Nothing reports a clip that shows a take's media but belongs to no shot.

The browser type `TakeProposal` in `src/director/take-review.ts` has `formatVersion: 1`, and `src/director/TakeReview.tsx` shows one mapping (`take-proposal-clip`, `take-proposal-from`, `take-proposal-to`).
interfaces: Offset rule (`core/takes.ts`, replacing `shows`): a clip with `title === null` shows take T at offset `d = clip.sourceStartTicks - T.sourceStartTicks` when `clip.assetId === T.assetId` and `d >= 0`. If a take of the shot matches the clip's in-point exactly, that take is the one shown. Otherwise the clip must match exactly one take of the shot by asset; if two takes use the same asset the clip is refused with 'Two takes of this shot use the same media, so the clip's place in the take cannot be told; replace it in the editor.'.

Mapping rule: for footage, each clip maps to the new take at `newTake.sourceStartTicks + d`, keeping its own timeline start and duration. When the new take is a still, every clip maps to source start 0. When the take now shown is a still and the new take is footage, a clip's offset is the sum of the durations of the shot's earlier clips in timeline order, so the footage runs on across the cuts.

Take-proposal format version 2 (`TakeProposalSchema`): `formatVersion: 2`; `mappings` holds 1 to 64 entries (the `applyBatch` limit) sorted by timeline start and then clip id; each mapping is `{clipId, startTicks, durationTicks, takeOffsetTicks, from, to}`. Clips that already show the requested take at their offset are left out; if none is left the existing refusal 'The shot already shows this take.' is given. More than 64 clips is LIMIT_EXCEEDED 'The shot is shown by more than 64 clips; replace its takes in the editor.'.

`yamakan.take.proposeReplace` (scope `project:read`, not a mutation; input unchanged) returns a version 2 proposal. `yamakan.take.apply` (scope `project:write`, mutation, not human-only, receipt kept; unchanged) accepts a version 2 proposal and applies all mappings as one `applyOperations` batch, which is one revision and one undo step. A proposal with `formatVersion: 1` is refused with REVISION_CONFLICT 'This proposal was made by an older page; propose it again.' so an open page takes its existing stale path.

Refusals name the clip: `Clip <i> of <n> of this shot: <reason>`, where the reason is the text `clip.replaceMedia` gives (retimed clip, unlinked sound, locked track, take shorter than the clip). A shot with no clip is refused with 'The shot has no clip on the timeline; assemble it again or attach a clip.'. Today's handling of a title-card clip is kept when it is the shot's only clip; a title card that was split is refused with 'The shot's title card was split; replace its clips in the editor.'.

`yamakan.take.list` (input unchanged) gains, per shot, `timeline.clips`: at most 64 of `{clipId, startTicks, durationTicks, assetId, sourceStartTicks, takeId, takeOffsetTicks}`. The existing single-clip fields of `timeline` keep describing the first clip, and `currentTakeId` is the take all clips show or null when they disagree, so the present `takeRows` reader keeps working.

`yamakan.take.list` gains `orphans` (at most 64) and `orphanTotal`: each orphan is a clip on a video track with `title === null` whose asset is a take's asset in this story and whose id is in no shot's `clipIds`, given as `{clipId, startTicks, durationTicks, assetId, candidates}` with at most 4 candidate `{shotId, takeId}`. No new mutation: a person re-attaches a clip with the existing `shot.update` or `shot.add` operations through `yamakan.project.applyBatch`.
`TAKE_LIMITS` gains `mappings: 64`, `orphans: 64` and `orphanCandidates: 4`.

tasks.title: Persist the brief, scene scripts and shot intent in the story document
tasks.objective: What a film is meant to be (its brief), what each scene says (its script) and what each shot is meant to show (its intent) are stored in the project's story document, inside its 256 KiB limit, so they survive a new browser, a backup and a restore, and an agent can read them. Text that today lives only in one browser is brought in once, by the person's own action.
currentBaseline: `src/create/CreateWorkspace.tsx` keeps Create's draft in browser `localStorage` under `yamakan.create.brief.<projectId>` and reads it back with `readBrief` (`src/create/create-model.ts`). `CreateBrief` is `{prompt, modelId, seed, direction}`: it is the request for one shot, not a brief for a film. It is lost with the browser profile and no command can read it.

`src/create/create-story.ts` `addMadeVideo` records a made video as one shot with one take in a story titled 'Made in Create' and writes the prompt into the shot's `notes`, cut to 2,000 characters; `madeRecords` reads the prompt back from `shot.notes`. `RunReceipt` holds `model, revision, prompt, seed, steps, sha256, licence, inputs` and no direction choices.

`core/story.ts`: `StoryDocumentSchema` is `{format, formatVersion: 1, title, scenes}`; a scene is `{id, name, shots}`; a shot is `{id, name, durationTicks, notes, referencePacks, takes, selectedTakeId}` with `notes` at most 2,000 characters. There is no field for a brief, a script, framing, movement, action or dialogue.

`STORY_LIMITS.documentBytes` is `256 * 1024`; `core/documents.ts` refuses a larger canonical story with LIMIT_EXCEEDED 'Canonical document exceeds 262144 bytes.'. There is no separate budget for text.

`yamakan.story.save` (`core/command/registry.ts`) is scope `project:write`, `mutation: true`, whole-document, compare-and-swap on `expectedRevision` and `expectedContentHash`. The browser calls it from two places in `src/main.tsx` (the Director's Cinema placement and Create's story save).

`core/prompts/directions.ts` `DIRECTIONS` has four kinds (`shot`, `movement`, `lens`, `light`) whose choices are short lower-case ids; `composePrompt` (`src/create/create-model.ts`) turns the choices into words appended to the prompt.
MPR-101 moves the story to format version 2 and, by its own text, defines the fields of this card in that version as schema and validation only. Nothing writes or shows them until this card.
interfaces: These four items are the story format version 2 fields that MPR-101 ships as schema and validation. Lengths are counted as `Name` and `Note` are today (string length). Every field is optional, every object is strict, and an empty value is left out, never stored as an empty string or empty object.

Story `brief` (`StoryBriefSchema`): `logline` 1 to 500 characters; `audience` 1 to 300; `format` 1 to 120; `tone` 1 to 300; `languages`: 1 to 8 distinct BCP 47 tags, each 2 to 35 characters matching `^[A-Za-z]{2,3}(-[A-Za-z0-9]{2,8})*$`, compared without regard to case.
Scene `sceneText` (the scene's script; `script` is a name `tests/command.test.ts` forbids in a command's input): 1 to 4,000 characters of plain text.

Shot `intent` (`ShotIntentSchema`): `framing` 1 to 200 characters; `movement` 1 to 200; `action` 1 to 2,000 (so a Create prompt of `PROMPT_LIMIT` fits whole); `dialogue` 1 to 500; and `direction`: at most the four keys of `DirectionKind`, each value 1 to 40 characters matching `^[a-z0-9-]+$`. `direction` is a fifth field beyond the four the plan names; it keeps Create's direction choices as they were chosen. A value that is not a present choice in `DIRECTIONS` is kept and shown as text.

`STORY_LIMITS` gains `textBytes: 96 * 1024` and `briefLanguages: 8`. `storyTextBytes(story)` (`core/story.ts`) is the sum of the UTF-8 byte lengths of every string value in `brief`, every scene `sceneText` and every string value in every shot `intent`; keys and JSON punctuation are not counted. A story over the budget is refused with LIMIT_EXCEEDED 'The story's brief, scripts and shot intents hold <n> bytes of text; the limit is 98304.'. The whole document still has to fit `documentBytes`.

No new command. tasks.title: Add a bounded shot history read command: the revision ledger of one shot
tasks.evidence: Merged as 447b6a7d8458e00ee01b54084835d5e0cc433097 (PR #301, pinned to 2e59ea2, which adds only the receipt and its write-up to dc47876); qualify:revisable-shot passed at dc47876 on GitHub's Linux machine with a stand-in engine (docs/evidence/ultimate/MPR-107-shot-history-receipt.json); main's CI passed; acceptance's 'no prompt text' is met for the prompt fields, while a shot's name, a take's label and an engine's message may hold such words; nothing of it ran on the founder host but its tests and one in-memory timing
tasks.objective: One read command answers, for one shot, what was tried and what it cost: the takes the shot holds and how each was made, every generation or render attempted for it (failed and cancelled ones too), every take replacement applied to it (revision and principal), and totals. The answer is bounded and paged. It is the data SS-016 measures and the 'show the ledger' step of the Stage 1 demonstration.
currentBaseline: No command returns a shot's history: the registry (`core/command/registry.ts`) has no `yamakan.shot.*` command. `yamakan.take.list` gives the present takes, `yamakan.generation.list` gives a project's generations, and `yamakan.project.history` gives revisions; none joins them by shot.

`yamakan.generation.list` hides rows marked `dismissed`, and `GenerationService.start` (`core/engines/generation.ts`) marks a request refused before sending as `state: failed, dismissed: true`. So failed attempts a person dismissed and attempts that never left are in the ledger but in no answer.

Generation rows are `jobs` rows of kind `remote-generation` (`REMOTE_GENERATION`, `core/jobs.ts`) whose `payload` is the JSON ledger row; `generationPayloads` reads them without an engine being configured. The `jobs` and `attempts` tables have no time column; a generation row carries `startedAt`, and `endedAt` only once MPR-101 has merged.
Before MPR-102 a generation row does not name a shot, and before MPR-101 a Blender render job does not either. Rows made earlier cannot be tied to a shot.

`yamakan.take.apply` commits through `ProjectStore.applyOperations`, whose revision row always reads `operation: project.applyBatch` (`core/store.ts`). No row names the shot or the take, so a replacement cannot be told from any other edit without comparing two whole project snapshots.

`revisions(project_id, revision, snapshot_hash, parent_revision, operation, receipt_id)` and `command_receipts(id, principal_id, project_id, request_id, request_digest, committed_revision)` hold the principal of a revision; neither holds a time. A project has at most 10,000 revisions (`MAX_REVISION`).
No adapter reports quota use today (`usage.quotaSeconds` is null in MPR-101's records), so a quota total can only say 'not reported'.
interfaces: New read command `yamakan.shot.history` (scope `project:read`, not a mutation, no receipt, not human-only). Strict input: `{projectId, documentId, shotId, limit?, before?}`; `limit` is 1 to 100 (default 50) attempts; `before` is the `next` number of the previous page. No path, no free text.

Output: `{documentId, shotId, sceneId, name, contentHash, revision, current, takes, attempts, next, replacements, replacementTotal, totals, gaps}`. `current` is `{selectedTakeId, shownTakeId, clips}` from the present story and timeline (the reading `listTakes` gives).

`takes` (at most `STORY_LIMITS.takesPerShot`, 8): the takes the shot holds now, each `{takeId, kind, label, selected, shown, recordHash, addedAtRevision, origin, route, source, summary, timings, usage, derivedFromTakeId, changedFields}`. The last nine come from the take's `TakeRecord` (MPR-101) and are null for a take without one. `summary` is `{recipeId, modelId, operation, seed, width, height, durationFrames, fps, steps, promptHash}`: no prompt text. `addedAtRevision` is the revision of the `story_document_versions` row that holds the record for this story.

`attempts` (newest first, at most `limit`): each `{seq, kind, id, route, outcome, sent, imported, recipeId, startedAt, endedAt, wallMs, quotaSeconds, takeId, takeInShot, derivedFromTakeId, diagnostic}`. `kind` is `generation` or `render`; `seq` is the creation order of the job row; `outcome` is `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelled` or `uncertain`, derived by one new pure function in `core/shot-history.ts` from the row's `state`, `phase`, `cancelled` and `imported` (main has no shared function: `yamakan.generation.list` returns `state`, `uncertain`, `stopped` and `imported` as separate fields built inline); `sent` is false only when the row never left: its `phase` is not `sent` and its `state` is `failed` (the rule `mayHaveLeft` in `core/engines/generation.ts` applies); a row whose `executionRef` is null for any other reason may have left and is `uncertain`; `takeId` comes from the row's `take` field (MPR-102) and `takeInShot` says whether the shot still holds it; `derivedFromTakeId` is given when the row has it (MPR-103); `diagnostic` is cut to 200 characters. Dismissed rows are included. `next` is the `seq` to pass as `before`, or null.

`wallMs` is `endedAt - startedAt` when the row has both, else null. `quotaSeconds` is the value in the take's record when the attempt made a take and the adapter reported it, else null. Null always means not reported; the command never estimates.
`replacements` (the newest, at most 32) with `replacementTotal`: each `{revision, principalId, fromTakeId, toTakeId, clips}`, read from replacement notes (next item).

Replacement note: `yamakan.take.apply` (scope, receipt, input and result unchanged) also stores, in the same transaction as its revision, one immutable content-addressed document of new kind `takeReplacement` (format `yamakan.take-replacement`, `formatVersion` 1, at most 512 bytes): `{documentId, shotId, fromTakeId, toTakeId, clips, revision, principalId}`. It is held for the story's document id through a `story_document_versions` row, the way MPR-101 holds take records, so there is no SQL schema step, and it is never a project document reference, so the limit of 32 documents per project is not touched. `ProjectStore.applyOperations` gains an optional last argument that builds at most one such attachment inside the commit.

`totals`: `{attempts, succeeded, failed, cancelled, running, uncertain, takes, replacements, wallMs, wallMsUnknown, quotaSeconds, quotaUnknown, complete}` over every attempt of the shot, not only the page. `wallMs` sums the attempts that have it and `wallMsUnknown` counts those that do not; the same for quota. `complete` is false when a scan limit was reached.

`gaps`: a closed list of codes, each returned only when the scan met the case: `untargeted-attempts` (the project has generation rows that name no shot), `unlinked-renders` (render jobs that name no shot), `earlier-replacements` (batch revisions older than the story's first replacement note), `scan-limit`.

`core/shot-history.ts` (new): `SHOT_HISTORY_LIMITS = { attempts: 100, defaultAttempts: 50, replacements: 32, answerBytes: 128 * 1024, jobRowsScanned: 5000, notesScanned: 2000, noteBytes: 512, diagnosticChars: 200 }`, `TakeReplacementSchema`, `shotHistory(...)`. `core/jobs.ts` gains `shotAttemptRows(db, projectId, target, before)`, which reads the project's generation and render job rows newest first (descending creation order) and yields those naming the shot.

Bound on the answer: the command serialises its answer and, if it is over 131,072 bytes, drops the oldest attempts of the page and sets `next` to match, so a page may be shorter than `limit` but an answer is never larger.

Notes count against the workspace's creative document space like any held document: at most 512 bytes each.

tasks.title: Add one model catalog and check every existing model list against it
tasks.evidence: Merged as 60ccce5ed0994b21aecbfb286400856f37288d97 (PR #295); qualify:model-catalog passed at 5f511b5 on the founder host (docs/evidence/model-system/model-catalog.json); main's CI passed
tasks.objective: One typed catalog names every model Yamakan offers, is considering or has refused, by exact identity (host, model slug, revision, variant), with its operations, limits, licence facts, lifecycle and evidence. One test proves that every other model list in the repository agrees with it, and nothing a person sees changes.
currentBaseline: `core/engines/kaggle.ts` `KAGGLE_RECIPES` holds three recipes (`kaggle-wan22-ti2v-5b`, `kaggle-wan22-ti2v-5b-first-frame`, `kaggle-cogvideox-2b`) with model, revision, licence, width, height, frames, fps, steps, timeouts, folder, slug and output. It is the only list the live route runs from (`offeredKaggleRecipes`, and `yamakan.generation.options` in `core/command/registry.ts`).

`src/create/create-model.ts` `CREATE_MODELS` repeats the facts of two of those models for the page (name, licence, width, height, frames, fps, steps, seconds to make). Only the test 'the page's facts and the recipe say the same' in `tests/kaggle-engine.test.ts` ties it to `KAGGLE_RECIPES`. It has no entry for the first-frame recipe.

`core/engines/comfyui.ts` `PINNED_COMFY_RECIPES` and `core/engines/manifests.ts` `PINNED_MODEL_MANIFESTS` are both empty frozen arrays; `tests/comfyui-engine.test.ts` and `tests/engine-absence.test.ts` assert that.

`core/engines/candidates.ts` is a schema and validator (`EngineCandidatesSchema`, `parseEngineCandidates`, `selectionBlockers`, `selectionCautions`), not a list. The list is the frozen YU-043 evidence `docs/evidence/ultimate/engine-candidate-manifests.json` with three candidates: `wan2.2-ti2v-5b-native` (status `blocked`, repository `Wan-AI/Wan2.2-TI2V-5B` at commit `921dbaf3f1674a56f47e83fb80a34bac8a8f203e`, a remote service reference named `dashscope`), `wan2.2-ti2v-5b-diffusers` and `cogvideox-2b-diffusers` (both `eligibleForQualification`).
`core/engines/v1-bridge.ts` `SERVER_RECIPES` are stand-in recipes for the fake engine and `docs/evidence/yamakan/provider-registry.json` is research evidence. Neither names a model a person can run.

No file records a model's lifecycle, a verification date, a source URL, or a model that was evaluated and refused, except the frozen evidence file. A licence is free text in `KaggleRecipe.licence` and `CreateModel.licence`; `ACCEPTED_MODEL_LICENSES` in `core/engines/manifests.ts` is used only by `manifests.ts` and `candidates.ts`, not by the live Kaggle route.

`docs/provenance/import-policy.json` lists `core/engines` in `donorRoots`. Every file there must appear in `localFilesInDonorRoots` (objects with `path` and `reason`) or `npm run provenance:check` fails. The `format:check` script in `package.json` does not cover `core/engines`.
interfaces: `MODEL_CATALOG_FORMAT = 'yamakan.model-catalog/v1'`: a code constant naming the shape. It is not a stored document; no project, database or evidence format changes.

`ModelIdentity = { host, model, revision, variant }` (strict zod object): `host` is the lower-case DNS name where the weights are published (today only `huggingface.co`), `model` is the publisher's slug (for example `Wan-AI/Wan2.2-TI2V-5B-Diffusers`), `revision` is a 40-character lower-case hex commit, `variant` is a short token (`diffusers`, `native`). A family name without a revision does not parse.

`CatalogOffer = { route: 'kaggle' | 'comfyui' | 'local', recipeId: string | null, operation: Operation, lifecycle: 'candidate' | 'qualified' | 'offered' | 'retired', limits: { width, height, frames, fps, steps, promptWordsRead: number | null, roles: string[], references: { count, mediaTypes, maxBytes } | null }, evidence: string[] }`; since MPR-202, `limits` also has `durationFrames: { min, max }` and `audioOut` (OA-15), and the offer `measured: { at, samples } | null` (OA-17). `evidence` holds repo-relative paths under `docs/evidence/`. `recipeId` is null for a candidate that has no recipe yet. `references` is null for every recipe at the baseline, because no recipe takes a reference image.

`CatalogLicence = { weightsLicence, sourceUrl, verifiedAt }`: the licence identifier as the publisher states it, the https URL where it was read (data only, never fetched by code), and the date it was read. This is a record of facts, not a gate; MPR-208 extends the block and owns the gate.

`CatalogEntry = { id, name, identity, licence, offers: CatalogOffer[], verifiedAt, sourceUrl }` and `CatalogRefusal = { id, identity, refusedAt, reason: 'REMOTE_SERVICE_REFERENCE' | 'LICENCE_UNACCEPTED' | 'ROUTE_RETIRED' | 'ROUTE_PROHIBITED' | 'INTERFACE_UNSUPPORTED', note, evidence: string[], sourceUrl }`.
`MODEL_CATALOG` (deep-frozen `{ format, entries, refused }`), `ModelCatalogSchema`, `parseModelCatalog(value)`, `catalogEntryFor(model, revision)`, `catalogOfferFor(recipeId)`.

`catalogDisagreements({ kaggleRecipes, comfyRecipes, modelPins, candidates, createModels })` returns a list of plain sentences, empty when every list agrees with the catalog. It is a pure function, used by the test and by the qualification script.

Bounds enforced by the schema: at most 64 entries, 8 offers per entry, 32 refusals, 8 evidence paths per offer or refusal, every string bounded; `JSON.stringify(MODEL_CATALOG)` is at most 65,536 bytes.
No command, scope, table, error code or SQLite schema step is added by this card.

tasks.title: Report capabilities as three-state cells and project generation options from them
tasks.objective: One command tells a person or an agent what each route can do with each model for each operation. Every cell says supported, unsupported or unverified, with where the answer comes from, its date, its limits and a reason code. The list of models a person can start is a projection of the same report, so the two cannot disagree.
currentBaseline: `yamakan.engines.capabilities` in `core/command/registry.ts` (scope `project:read`, `mutation: false`, input `z.object({}).strict()`) returns one row per `Operation` only: `{ operation, available, verified, reason, message, version, expiresAt }`, built from `discoverEngineCapabilities` in `core/engines/manifests.ts`. It knows nothing of routes or models. With `ENGINE_ENABLED = false` (`core/engines/contract.ts`) every row is `ENGINE_DISABLED` (`tests/engine-absence.test.ts`).

`yamakan.generation.options` returns `{ route: 'kaggle' | null, models: [...] }` built inline from `offeredKaggleRecipes()` and `notebookUrl` (`core/engines/kaggle.ts`). It is empty unless the service was started with the Kaggle CLI variables, and it does not consult `yamakan.engines.capabilities`.
The Kaggle adapter's `capabilities()` in `createKaggleEngine` returns an empty list. ComfyUI is reported by a separate command, `yamakan.engines.comfyui`, and `PINNED_COMFY_RECIPES` is empty.

`core/engines/reasons.ts` `ENGINE_REASON_MESSAGES` has text for 4 of the 11 `RefusalReason` codes (`ENGINE_DISABLED`, `WEIGHTS_ABSENT`, `HARDWARE_UNQUALIFIED`, `RIGHTS_UNQUALIFIED`); `engineReasonMessage` answers 'This operation is not available.' for the rest. `src/i18n.ts` has `engine.reason.*` keys for the same four in English and Arabic.

`core/router/explain.ts` `explainRoutes` uses its own free-string reason codes (`PROVIDERS_DISABLED`, `OPERATION_UNSUPPORTED`, `NOT_QUALIFIED`) that are not in `core/engines/reasons.ts`; `ROUTER_PROVIDERS_ENABLED` is false.

Page callers: `src/main.tsx` calls `yamakan.engines.capabilities` and `yamakan.generation.options`; `src/director/DirectorPanel.tsx` calls `yamakan.engines.capabilities`. Both read the `operations` rows.

No answer today separates 'Yamakan refuses this' from 'nobody has checked this'. For example the Wan first-frame recipe ignoring a last frame is recorded in the frozen `docs/evidence/ultimate/engine-candidate-manifests.json` and as an `INPUT_UNSUPPORTED` refusal in `submit` of `core/engines/kaggle.ts`, but no command reports it.
interfaces: `yamakan.engines.capabilities`: scope `project:read`, `mutation: false`, input unchanged (`z.object({}).strict()`). The output keeps `operations` exactly as it is and adds `report`.

`CapabilityReport = { format: 'yamakan.capability-report/v1', routes: [{ route: 'kaggle' | 'comfyui' | 'local', configured: boolean, reason: ReportReason | null }], cells: CapabilityCell[], refused: [{ catalogId, identity, reason, because, refusedAt, evidence }], reasonMessages: Record<ReportReason, string> }`. `reasonMessages` holds the English text only for codes that appear in this answer. A refusal's `reason` is `MODEL_REFUSED`, which has a message; `because` is the catalog's own word for why.

`CapabilityCell = { route, catalogId, identity: { host, model, revision, variant }, recipeId: string | null, operation: Operation, state: 'supported' | 'unsupported' | 'unverified', reasons: ReportReason[], source: { kind: 'evidence' | 'catalog' | 'build', ref: string, samples: number | null }, asOf: string, limits: { width, height, frames, fps, steps, durationFrames: { min, max }, audioOut: boolean, promptWordsRead, roles, references: { count, mediaTypes, maxBytes } | null } | null }`. `durationFrames` and `audioOut` are OA-15, accepted on 2026-11-23: how many frames a video of the recipe may have (one number twice where the recipe fixes it, as every recipe at the baseline does) and whether its video comes with sound (none does); the catalog's offers (MPR-201) gain both. `references` is null for every recipe at the baseline, because no recipe takes a reference image. By OA-17, accepted on 2026-11-23, each measured fact carries a date and a sample size. What is measured here is that a recipe ran with its limits: those are one fact, of one evidence file. `CatalogOffer` in `core/engines/catalog.ts` (MPR-201) gains `measured: { at: date, samples: integer from 1 to 1000 } | null`, written from the offer's own evidence and checked against it by a test; `source.samples` is `measured.samples` for a cell whose source is evidence, and null for any other. A limit that no run measured (a local candidate's) is in no measured cell. `reasons` is empty only when `state` is `supported`, and holds at most 4 codes, the deciding one first.

By OA-15, a request may name reference pictures: `reference` joins the input roles of `EngineRequestV2Schema` (`core/engines/contract-v2.ts`) for `textToVideo` and `imageToVideo`, after the frames, PNG or JPEG, at most `ENGINE_V2_LIMITS.references` (4); the catalog's roles and a take record's input roles (MPR-101) gain the word. No engine or recipe honours it, so a request with one is refused with `INPUT_UNSUPPORTED`, and no command takes one.

`core/engines/reasons.ts`: new type `ReportReason` = the 11 `RefusalReason` codes plus five report-only codes: `NOT_QUALIFIED`, `OPERATION_NOT_OFFERED`, `OFFER_RETIRED`, `ROUTE_NOT_CONFIGURED`, `MODEL_REFUSED`. `ENGINE_REASON_MESSAGES` gains text for the 7 `RefusalReason` codes it lacks and for the 5 new codes. The `RefusalReason` enum in `core/engines/contract-v2.ts` does not change, so no adapter changes.
`src/i18n.ts`: `engine.reason.<CODE>` in English and Arabic for each of the 12 added codes.

New `core/engines/capability-report.ts` (declared in `localFilesInDonorRoots`): `buildCapabilityReport({ catalog, discovery, kaggleConfigured, comfyConfigured, localConfigured })` and `projectGenerationOptions(report, kaggle)`; both pure.
`yamakan.generation.options`: scope, input and output shape unchanged; its `models` are now chosen by `projectGenerationOptions`.
No new command, scope, table or error code. `LIMIT_EXCEEDED` (existing, `core/command/errors.ts` `ErrorCodes`) is the refusal when a report would pass its bounds.
tasks.sourceDecision: BUILD: the report is a pure projection of the MPR-201 catalog and of facts the service already holds; nothing is copied, and both commands keep their present fields.
sourceReuse: `MODEL_CATALOG`, `catalogOfferFor` (MPR-201, `core/engines/catalog.ts`) supply the cells' models, offers, limits and evidence paths.
`discoverEngineCapabilities` (`core/engines/manifests.ts`) keeps supplying the `operations` rows and supplies the deciding reason for local-route cells.
`offeredKaggleRecipes` and `notebookUrl` (`core/engines/kaggle.ts`) keep supplying the execution facts in `yamakan.generation.options` (name, expected seconds, timeout, notebook address).

`engineReasonMessage` (`core/engines/reasons.ts`) and the `engine.reason.*` pattern in `src/i18n.ts`, with the existing test 'each reason has the same English text in the interface and an Arabic one; every operation has a label' in `tests/engine-absence.test.ts`.
