tasks.title: Add a generation preflight with estimate, egress disclosure and a hash that start checks
tasks.objective: Before anything is recorded or sent, a person sees what a generation would do: the request as it will run, every reason it would be refused, how long it is expected to take and on what basis, what is known about quota, exactly what leaves this computer and to which host and account, and which inputs the model will honour. Starting then carries a hash of that answer, so what runs is what was shown.
currentBaseline: There is no preflight command. `yamakan.generation.start` (`core/command/registry.ts`; scope `project:write`, mutation, `humanOnly`, `refusesRequestId: NO_REPLAY`) validates, records (`ledger.begin`) and sends (`adapter.submit`) in one call to `createGenerationService().start` in `core/engines/generation.ts`.

The only estimate a person sees is `expectedSeconds` from `KAGGLE_RECIPES`, returned by `yamakan.generation.options` and shown as minutes in the `create.agree` text of `src/i18n.ts` (`Math.ceil(model.expectedSeconds / 60)` in `src/create/GeneratePanel.tsx`). It has no range, no worst case, no basis and no date.

`GenerationRecord` has `startedAt` and no end time on this baseline, so the service cannot say how long its own finished runs took (MPR-207 adds `endedAt`). `GenerationLedger.list` returns one project's newest rows only (50 at most in `JobSupervisor.generationLedger()` in `core/jobs.ts`).

`core/engines/kaggle.ts` has no quota query. Quota is learned only when a push is refused (`REFUSED_PUSH` matches `quota`); the recorded example is `docs/evidence/ultimate/kaggle-quota-refusal-receipt.json` ('Maximum weekly GPU quota of 30.00 hours reached'). Whether the Kaggle CLI can report remaining GPU quota is not verified.

What leaves is described only in prose: `create.agree` and `create.agreePicture` say the prompt, the seed and (for a picture) the picture go to the person's private Kaggle notebook and stay in its history. No command gives a byte count, a host or an account. The script that leaves is built by `scriptWithBrief` (`SCRIPT_BYTES` is 1,000,000; a first frame travels inside the script as `firstFrame.data`, sized by `imageRoom`).

Start's input is strict: `{ projectId, recipeId, prompt?, seed?, width, height, durationFrames, firstFrameAssetId?, noUnconsentedPerson?: true }`. Its refusals today are `VALIDATION` (for example image-to-video without a first frame or without `noUnconsentedPerson`), the consent refusals of `permittedToSend`, and `CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE` (another run of the recipe still followed, or an adapter refusal through `engineReasonMessage`). Only the first failing check is reported.

Callers of `yamakan.generation.start`: `src/main.tsx` (which `scripts/qualify-kaggle-screens.mjs` and `scripts/qualify-kaggle-generation.mjs` drive through the page), `tests/generation-service.test.ts` and `tests/request-id-refusal.test.ts`. `scripts/qualify-comfyui-generation.mjs` calls the service's `start` directly, not the command. No agent, SDK or CLI path can call it, because it is human-only.
interfaces: New command `yamakan.generation.preflight`: scope `project:read`, `mutation: false`, not human-only (an agent may ask; it records nothing and sends nothing). Input: the same strict schema as `yamakan.generation.start`, exported once as `GenerationStartInput` and used by both commands. Path-free; the prompt is bounded by `ENGINE_V2_LIMITS.promptChars`.
Output `GenerationPreflight = { format: 'yamakan.generation-preflight/v1', request, refusals, estimate, quota, egress, delivery, gates, preflightHash }`.

`request = { projectId, recipeId, catalogId, route, operation, promptChars, promptSha256, seed: number | null, width, height, durationFrames, fps, firstFrameAssetId: string | null, firstFrameSha256: string | null }`. The prompt text is not echoed. `seed: null` means the seed is chosen at start.

`refusals: [{ errorCode, reason: ReportReason | null, gate: 'egress' | 'spend' | 'download' | null, message }]`, at most 16: every check `start` makes before it records the run that this input would fail, each as the `ErrorCodes` value and plain message `start` would throw. Two kinds are not listed: refusals the adapter gives inside `submit`, and a run of the same recipe that only a status call to the route would show as still followed (preflight judges that from the stored rows only). Empty means the local checks pass; it is not a promise that the provider will accept the run.

`estimate = { unit: 'seconds', measures: 'wallClockAsFollowed', low, high, worst, basis: 'static' | 'historical', samples, asOf }`. The type also names `liveQuote`, which no route produces today. There is no currency field, because no route charges money.

`quota = { remaining: 'unknown', reason, lastQuotaRefusalAt, secondsFollowedSince, windowDays }`, taken from `kaggleQuotaFacts` (MPR-205). For a route that uses no quota the block is `{ remaining: 'notApplicable' }`.
`egress = { leavesThisComputer: boolean, host, account, items: [{ kind: 'prompt' | 'seed' | 'script' | 'firstFrame', bytes }], bytesUpperBound, keptRemotely: boolean, remoteCancel: false }`.

`delivery = { runsAt: { width, height, frames, fps, steps, durationFrames: { min, max }, audioOut, promptWordsRead }, roles: [{ role, given, honoured, reason: ReportReason | null }] }`, from the catalog offer (MPR-201). `durationFrames`, `audioOut` and the `reference` role are OA-15's, accepted on 2026-11-23 (MPR-202).
`gates = [{ kind, state, approvalId, expiresAt }]`, from `gateState` (MPR-204).

`preflightHash`: 64 lower-case hex characters, SHA-256 over a stable serialisation of `{ format, request, recipeHash, estimate.basis, estimate.worst, egress.host, egress.account, egress.bytesUpperBound, each gate's kind, state and approval id in order, resourcePolicyHash }`. It contains no clock value, so it changes only when what would run, or whether it may run, changes.

`yamakan.generation.start` input gains `preflightHash`. Scope `project:write`, `humanOnly` and `refusesRequestId: NO_REPLAY` are unchanged. A hash that does not match is refused with `VALIDATION` before anything is recorded or sent.

`createGenerationService` gains `prepare(request)` (all checks and normalisation, no ledger write, no adapter call) used by both `preflight` and `start`; `GenerationLedger` gains `ended(recipeId, limit)` for the historical basis. New file `core/engines/preflight.ts` (declared in `localFilesInDonorRoots`) holds the estimate, the hash and the output schema.
No new scope, table, error code or SQLite schema step.

The preflight's `egress` block also carries the two booleans `proxyConfigured` and `certificateOverride` of MPR-205 (a required dependency), beside the fields listed for `egress` above; it never carries a proxy address or certificate path.

The value is wall-clock time as this service followed the run; it is not Kaggle's own GPU accounting, and the output says so in `measures`.

tasks.title: Add default-deny gates for egress, spend and download with recorded human approvals
tasks.objective: Nothing leaves this computer, uses a remote allowance or is downloaded unless a person has recorded an approval for exactly that route, host, account and purpose, with an expiry and a limit. Each kind has one place in the code where the check is made, and tests prove that without an approval no process is started and no connection is opened.
currentBaseline: The Kaggle route is switched on by environment alone: `server/main.ts` passes `kaggle = { cli, username }` to `CreativeAPI`, and `generationOf` in `core/command/registry.ts` builds `createKaggleEngine({ cli: kaggleCli(ctx.kaggle.cli), username, ... })`. No stored record says a person allowed this service to contact Kaggle.

The only per-run agreement is in the page: `agreedFor` state in `src/create/GeneratePanel.tsx` beside the `create.agree` and `create.agreePicture` texts. The service never sees it, except `noUnconsentedPerson: true` for a first-frame picture.

A recorded, revocable, expiring human approval already exists for one thing: likeness consent. `grantConsent`, `revokeConsentRecord` and `listConsents` in `core/director/runtime.ts` write immutable rows in `likeness_consents`, append-only rows in `consent_revocations`, stamp the workspace epoch (`director_epoch`, raised on restore by `core/recovery.ts`) and replay request ids through the private `once` function over `director_requests`. `permittedToSend` in `core/engines/generation.ts` uses it for a first-frame picture only.

`kaggleCli` in `core/engines/kaggle.ts` is the one function that starts the Kaggle CLI (`execFile`); every push, status and output call of `createKaggleEngine` goes through the `KaggleCli` function it returns. It has no permission check.
`createGenerationService().start` in `core/engines/generation.ts` writes `ledger.begin` and then calls `adapter.submit`. Nothing limits how many runs are started or how much remote time they may use.

The product has no download path. Outbound network call sites in `core`, `server`, `cli` and `mcp` are in one file, `core/engines/comfyui.ts` (two `fetch` calls and one `WebSocket`), and `comfyBaseUrl` there accepts only a numeric loopback address. `server/main.ts` imports `node:http` to listen. `sdk/client.ts` calls the local service through an injected fetch.

Process starts are already a closed list: `processSpawnAllowlist` in `docs/provenance/import-policy.json` names `core/process/owner.ts`, `core/process/access.ts`, `core/render.ts` and `core/engines/kaggle.ts`, checked by `npm run provenance:check`.

The workspace database is at `WORKSPACE_SCHEMA_VERSION = 18` in `core/store.ts`; steps are constants `SCHEMA` to `SCHEMA_V18` applied in order, and a database newer than the build is refused ('Workspace database version N is newer than this build supports.').
interfaces: Where approvals live: three new STRICT tables in the existing workspace SQLite database, added by the next free schema step (`WORKSPACE_SCHEMA_VERSION` is 18 on this baseline; take the next free number at merge). No new database, file or store.

`gate_approvals(n INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, id TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(kind IN ('egress','spend','download')), route TEXT NOT NULL, host TEXT NOT NULL, account TEXT NOT NULL, purpose TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(purpose IN ('generation','qualification')), limit_runs INTEGER NOT NULL, limit_units INTEGER NOT NULL, limit_unit TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(limit_unit IN ('seconds','bytes')), proxy_configured INTEGER NOT NULL, certificate_override INTEGER NOT NULL (each 0 or 1; OA-20, accepted on 2026-11-23), granted_at INTEGER NOT NULL, expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL, grantor_principal_id TEXT NOT NULL, epoch INTEGER NOT NULL) STRICT`, with length checks on `route` (1 to 40), `host` (1 to 253) and `account` (1 to 80). Rows are never updated.

`gate_approval_revocations(approval_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES gate_approvals(id), revoked_at INTEGER NOT NULL, principal_id TEXT NOT NULL) STRICT` and `gate_approval_uses(approval_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES gate_approvals(id), use_id TEXT NOT NULL, units INTEGER NOT NULL, used_at INTEGER NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY(approval_id, use_id)) STRICT`. Both append-only.
No currency column exists. An approval cannot authorise a money charge in this build; a paid route must add that with its own schema step under MPR-222 after FD-5.

What an approval binds to: kind, route (`kaggle` today), host (fixed per route by the server: `kaggle.com`), account (the configured Kaggle username), purpose, expiry, a run limit and a unit limit (`seconds` of worst-case run time for spend, `bytes` for egress and download), the granting principal and the workspace epoch. A restore brings no approval back: its tables are removed whatever a backup holds in them and made again empty (as built: raising the epoch alone did not void one planted in a backup that has no epoch table). One of another epoch is void.

New module `core/gates.ts` (top level of `core`, not a donor root): `approveGate(store, input, receipt?)`, `revokeGate(store, input, receipt?)`, `listGateApprovals(store, network, nowMs)`, `gateState(store, ask, nowMs)` returning `{ kind, state: 'approved' | 'missing' | 'expired' | 'revoked' | 'exhausted' | 'voided' | 'changed', approvalId, expiresAt, runsLeft, unitsLeft, uses }`, `requireGate(store, ask, nowMs)` which returns the approval or throws `CommandError('CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE', message)`, and `consumeGates(store, asks, useId, nowMs)`, which counts one use of each ask, all of them or none, in one transaction. `ask = { kind, route, host, account, purpose, network: { proxyConfigured, certificateOverride } }`; `network` is read from what the route's program would be given, never its values, and an approval given under other settings is `changed` and allows nothing (OA-20). An approval for contacting that is only used up still allows following what was counted on it; `requireGate` is never the check of a start. Every match is exact string equality; there are no wildcards.

Command `yamakan.gates.approve`: scope `consent:grant`, mutation, `humanOnly`, keeps a receipt (request-id replay through `once` over `director_requests`). Strict input `{ kind, route: 'kaggle', host (1 to 253 characters, host-name pattern), account (1 to 80), purpose, ttlMs (60,000 to 366 days), limit: { runs (1 to 1000), units (0 to 2^40) } }`. The server refuses with `VALIDATION` a host that is not the route's fixed host or an account that is not the configured one, and refuses `kind: 'download'` with `CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE` ('This build downloads nothing.').

Command `yamakan.gates.revoke`: scope `consent:revoke`, mutation, `humanOnly`, keeps a receipt, input `{ approvalId }` strict. Command `yamakan.gates.list`: scope `consent:grant`, `mutation: false`, `humanOnly`, input `{}` strict, at most 200 approvals, newest first, each with its state and what is left, and `route`: what the route set up here would ask for (host, account, whether a proxy and a certificate setting are there, the most that one run is counted as) and how its two gates stand, for the page.

No new scope: the three commands reuse the human-only scopes `consent:grant` and `consent:revoke`. Dedicated `gate:approve` and `gate:revoke` scopes would be cleaner to audit but change `Scopes` and `HumanOnlyScopes`; that needs a founder decision and is not part of this card.

No new error code: a missing, expired, revoked, exhausted or voided approval is `CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE` with a plain message naming what to approve; bad input is `VALIDATION`; an agent is refused with `SCOPE_DENIED` by `authorize`.

Egress choke point: `kaggleCli(file, { mayConnect })` in `core/engines/kaggle.ts`. `mayConnect` is required and is called before every start of the Kaggle CLI program (not before the `taskkill.exe` call in `endTree` that ends a timed-out CLI process tree); when it throws, no process is started. `generationOf` passes `() => requireGate(store, { kind: 'egress', route: 'kaggle', host: 'kaggle.com', account, purpose: 'generation' }, Date.now())`.

Spend choke point: `createGenerationService({ ..., permit })` in `core/engines/generation.ts`. `permit({ generationId, recipeId })` is required (as built: the permit itself knows the recipe's time limit, `kaggleTimeout`, and `SCRIPT_BYTES`) and is called in `start` after every other check and before `ledger.begin`. For Kaggle `bytesUpperBound` is `SCRIPT_BYTES` from `core/engines/kaggle.ts` until MPR-203 supplies a closer count. `permit` has exactly one call site, and MPR-504 and MPR-505 add their checks at that same place, never at a second one. For Kaggle it requires the egress and spend approvals and writes one use row for each (use id is the generation id). For ComfyUI on loopback the registry passes the exported constant `noRemoteUse`, so the choice is explicit in code.
Download choke point: `requireGate` with `kind: 'download'`. No approval of that kind can be recorded, so it always refuses; any future download code must call it first.

The names use `gates`, not `approvals`, so they do not collide with the agent approval requests of MPR-504. MPR-505 enforces per-agent budgets at these same functions; MPR-210 and MPR-222 reuse them for hosted providers.

tasks.title: Contain the Kaggle CLI route: environment, folder, caps, tested version and quota facts
tasks.objective: The Kaggle command-line tool, which needs the network and therefore cannot run inside the `native/procd` worker boundary, runs with as little of this computer as it needs: a named list of environment variables in which the proxy and certificate names are a written, tested and disclosed exception, a working folder the service owns, named output and time limits, and only a CLI version the adapter was tested with. The person sees what is known about quota, whether a proxy or certificate override is in use, and that a run cannot be stopped on Kaggle, and no committed file names a personal account.
currentBaseline: `kaggleCli` in `core/engines/kaggle.ts` starts the CLI with `execFile`: `windowsHide`, a 4 MiB `maxBuffer`, a per-call timeout that ends the whole process tree (`endTree`), and no `cwd`, so the CLI runs in whatever folder the service was started from.

The environment is already an allow-list, not the whole environment: `kaggleCliEnvironment` passes the names in `CLI_ENVIRONMENT` plus every variable whose name starts with `KAGGLE_`. The list deliberately includes `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `ALL_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY` (both cases), `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`, `CURL_CA_BUNDLE` and `SSL_CERT_FILE`, under the comment 'A network the CLI works on in the person's terminal must work here too.' The test 'the CLI gets its settings, not this service's environment' in `tests/kaggle-engine.test.ts` asserts that a proxy variable passes.

No CLI version is checked. The only version recorded in repository evidence is 2.2.4, inside the CLI's own upgrade notice in `docs/evidence/ultimate/kaggle-quota-refusal-receipt.json`; `cliWords` removes that notice from messages. Which version the successful recorded runs used is not verified.

Per-call time limits are literals at the call sites (for example 90,000 ms for `kernels status`). The size of a fetched video is already bounded: 'a download growing past what a run makes is stopped and removed' in `tests/kaggle-engine.test.ts`.

The CLI subcommands used are `kernels list`, `kernels pull`, `kernels push`, `kernels status` and `kernels output`. None reports remaining GPU quota; quota is learned only from a refused push (`REFUSED_PUSH`). Whether any Kaggle CLI command reports remaining GPU quota is not verified.

The page already says a run cannot be stopped on Kaggle (`create.runStopNote` and `create.runGoesOn` in `src/i18n.ts`; 'stopping says plainly that the run goes on' in `tests/kaggle-engine.test.ts`). `yamakan.generation.options` does not carry that fact, and nothing shows quota.

Two committed files, `scripts/kaggle/wan22-ti2v-5b/kernel-metadata.json` and `scripts/kaggle/cogvideox-2b/kernel-metadata.json`, carry a personal Kaggle account id in their `id` field. No product code, test or script reads them: the adapter writes its own `kernel-metadata.json` for each run from the configured username.

tasks.title: Define the five engine operations and add a conformance kit every adapter must pass
tasks.objective: Each of the five operations in the engine contract has one written definition that says what goes in, what comes out and what an adapter may never approximate; adding a sixth has a fixed path; every `EngineAdapterV2` passes one shared suite for the behaviours that protect the person (the row is recorded before anything is sent, a run is reconciled after a restart without being sent again, a stop never claims more than happened, a result is hash-checked); and a model enters the catalog only through a written checklist that a test reads.
currentBaseline: The five operations (`textToVideo`, `imageToVideo`, `videoEdit`, `transcribe`, `enhance`) exist only as the `Operation` enum and the strict branches of `EngineRequestV2Schema` in `core/engines/contract-v2.ts` ('One strict schema per operation: roles, counts and media are exact'). No document defines them in words, and no document says how a sixth is added.

`docs/MODEL_CAPABILITIES.md` is a proposal that names more operations than the contract has (thirteen when this card was written; recount at step 0). None of the extra ones has a schema branch, an adapter or evidence.

Four files implement `EngineAdapterV2`: `createFakeEngineV2` in `core/engines/fake.ts`, `bridgeV1` in `core/engines/v1-bridge.ts`, `createComfyEngine` in `core/engines/comfyui.ts` and `createKaggleEngine` in `core/engines/kaggle.ts`. Each is tested in its own file (`tests/engines.test.ts`, `tests/comfyui-engine.test.ts`, `tests/kaggle-engine.test.ts`, `tests/generation-durable.test.ts`) with a stand-in written inside that file. There is no shared suite.

`reconcile` is on the contract ('After a restart: what is known about an execution, never a resubmit'), but in all four adapters it is the same function as `status`, and `createGenerationService` in `core/engines/generation.ts` never calls it: a restarted run is followed through `status`.

`FakeEngineV2Options` has `unavailable`, `artifactBytes`, `failExecutions`, `beforeInput` and `stayRunning`. The fake cannot stand for an uncertain submit, a lost job, a restart, a corrupt artifact or a remote that goes on after a stop. Only `tests/engines.test.ts` uses it.

The protecting behaviours are tested per adapter only. 'stale attempts are fenced; the same generation replays its execution' and 'artifacts verify: bounded chunks, declared length and hash, for both adapters' in `tests/engines.test.ts` cover the fake and the bridge; the rule that an uncertain send is never repeated is tested for Kaggle in `tests/generation-durable.test.ts`.

`createGenerationService.start` records the row with `ledger.begin` in phase `sending` before `adapter.submit`, uses the generation id as `attemptKey` with a constant `leaseGeneration: 1`, and keeps the row in phase `sending` when the adapter answers `uncertain`.
No model-intake checklist exists as a document or as a test. `core/engines/candidates.ts` validates the shape of a candidate record; it is neither a list of models nor a checklist.
interfaces: New `docs/ENGINE_OPERATIONS.md`, section 'Operations': one second-level heading per operation, the heading text being the exact name in the `Operation` enum, in enum order. Each section states the purpose, the prompt rule, the inputs (role, count, media type), the output kind and a list headed 'never approximated'. The content is taken from `EngineRequestV2Schema`, not invented: `textToVideo` has a required prompt (1 to 4000 characters), no inputs but up to four `reference` pictures (PNG or JPEG; OA-15, MPR-202) and a video output; `imageToVideo` has an optional prompt, `firstFrame` alone or `firstFrame` then `lastFrame` (each PNG or JPEG), then up to four `reference` pictures, and a video output; no engine honours a reference yet, and the section says so; `videoEdit` has a required prompt, a `source` as MP4 alone or with a `mask` as PNG, and a video output; `transcribe` has no prompt field, one `audio` input as WAV or MP4, and a transcript output with an optional language; `enhance` has no prompt field, one `source` as MP4 and a video output.

Section 'Common to every operation': `recipeId`, `recipeHash`, `modelManifestHash`, an optional `seed`, at most 32 named bounded `controls`, `attemptKey`, `leaseGeneration`, `deadlineMs` and `resourcePolicyHash`; a video output declares width and height (16 to 8192, even), the frame rate as a fraction, the length in ticks and whether it has audio.

Section 'Nothing is approximated': an adapter that cannot honour a role, a control, a media type or the declared output answers `{ refused }` with `INPUT_UNSUPPORTED`, `CONTROL_UNSUPPORTED` or `OUTPUT_UNSUPPORTED` before anything is started or sent. It never drops an input, clamps or ignores a control, answers one operation with another, or returns a size, rate or length other than the declared one without failing the run.

Section 'Adding an operation': five steps, and the operation is offered nowhere until the last is done. (1) A written definition in this document. (2) A strict branch in `EngineRequestV2Schema` and the name in `Operation`; `ENGINE_CONTRACT_V2` stays as it is only if no existing branch changes. (3) Support in `createFakeEngineV2` and a passing run of the kit for it. (4) At least one real adapter that claims it in `capabilities()` and passes the kit. (5) Qualification evidence under `docs/evidence/` and a catalog offer (MPR-201) that passed the intake checklist. Section 'Proposed, not in the contract' lists the extra operations named in `docs/MODEL_CAPABILITIES.md` with the status PROPOSED.

`core/engines/fake.ts`: new export `createFakeWorld()` (executions, artifacts and the send count held outside the adapter, so two adapters over one world stand for before and after a restart) and new optional fields on `FakeEngineV2Options`: `world`, `uncertainSubmit: 'landed' | 'neverLanded'`, `lostExecutions: boolean`, `corruptArtifact: boolean`, `cancelOutcome: 'stopped' | 'continuing'`. With none set the fake behaves exactly as on main; `spawned()` stays the count of real starts.

New test helper `tests/fixtures/engine-conformance.ts` (not matched by the `npm test` glob, not in a donor root): exports `CONFORMANCE_CHECKS` (the closed list of check ids below), the type `ConformanceHarness`, `runConformance(harness)` (answers one `{ check, ok, detail }` per check) and `engineConformance(name, harness)`, which registers one `node:test` test per check named `<name>: <check id>`.

`ConformanceHarness`: `adapter()` (a new adapter over the same stand-in world on every call), `request(overrides)` (a valid request for an operation the adapter claims), `refusedRequests()` (requests the adapter must refuse, each with its expected `RefusalReason`; at least one, and for an adapter whose model ignores a role the schema allows, such as `lastFrame` on the Kaggle route, a request with that role), `context()` (the second argument of `submit`), `sends()` (real sends or starts so far), `remote: 'none' | 'stoppable' | 'unstoppable'`, `arrange` (functions `succeeded`, `uncertainLanded`, `uncertainNeverLanded`, `lost`, `corruptArtifact`, each putting the stand-in in that state), `unavailable` (scenario name to reason, for a state the stand-in cannot be put in) and an optional `service` (`store` and `ledger`) for the service-layer checks.

Adapter-layer checks: `refusal-sends-nothing` (every refused request answers its `RefusalReason` and `sends()` does not move); `status-parses` (every status parses with `ExecutionStatusSchema`); `ref-usable-at-once` (the `executionRef` from `submit` is accepted by `status`, `reconcile`, `requestCancel` and `enumerateArtifacts` before any polling); `same-attempt-never-sent-twice` (a second `submit` with the same `attemptKey` and `leaseGeneration` answers the same ref or refuses, and `sends()` stays 1); `uncertain-sends-nothing-more` (after an uncertain submit, `status` and `reconcile` send nothing, a run that landed can be followed to its end, and a run that never landed is never reported `succeeded`); `restart-reconciles-without-sending` (a new adapter over the same world answers `reconcile` for a known ref and sends nothing); `unknown-ref-answered-honestly` (a ref never issued is `unknown` or a thrown `NOT_FOUND`, never `succeeded`).

Adapter-layer checks, continued: `cancel-never-overclaims` (the answer parses with `CancellationSchema`; under `remote: 'unstoppable'` it never says `remoteOutcome: 'stopped'` or `remoteAcknowledged: true`; under `remote: 'none'` `billingOutcome` is `notApplicable` or absent); `artifact-verified` (every artifact of a succeeded run passes `readArtifactVerified`); `corrupt-artifact-rejected` (`readArtifactVerified` rejects when the bytes do not match the declared hash or length); `diagnostic-bounded` (every `diagnostic` and `notice` seen is at most `ENGINE_V2_LIMITS.diagnosticChars` long and holds no absolute path of this computer); `location-declared` (the adapter has `location` exactly when `remote` is not `none`).

Service-layer checks, run with `createGenerationService` over a recording wrapper of `memoryLedger()` when the harness gives `service`: `row-before-send` (`begin` is recorded before `sends()` first rises); `ref-before-poll` (the row holds `executionRef` before the first `adapter.status` call); `uncertain-row-not-resent` (the row stays in phase `sending`, and a new service with a new adapter on the same ledger lists and reads it without a send); `continuing-stop-blocks-import` (after a stop whose remote goes on, the row is `cancelled`, carries the not-stopped note, and the import behind `yamakan.generation.import` is refused); `corrupt-result-not-imported` (the import is refused with `VALIDATION` and no asset joins the store).

`tests/engine-conformance.test.ts` holds `ADAPTER_SUITES`, the closed map from each adapter file under `core/engines/` to the test file that calls `engineConformance` for it, and `PENDING`, the adapter files not yet registered (three after part a, none after part b).

New `docs/MODEL_INTAKE.md`: a checklist whose items each start with an id in backticks, mirrored by `INTAKE_ITEMS` in `tests/model-intake.test.ts`. Machine-checked against `MODEL_CATALOG` (MPR-201): `identity` (full identity tuple with an exact revision), `licence` (name, source URL, date read; the gate itself is MPR-208), `route`, `operation` (one of the five, with the roles honoured), `limits`, `evidence` (at least one existing path under `docs/evidence/` for an offer whose lifecycle is `qualified` or `offered`), `conformance` (the route's adapter file is in `ADAPTER_SUITES`, or in `PENDING` until part b lands). Written items, answered in the offer's evidence file: `egress` (what leaves this computer and to which host), `spend` (money or quota time a run can use, or none), `download` (what must be put on this computer and its size, or none), `withdrawal` (how the offer is retired and what happens to runs already made).
No new command, scope, error code, table, schema step or contract id. `EngineAdapterV2`, `EngineRequestV2Schema` and `core/engines/contract-v2.ts` are not changed.

tasks.title: Record a typed failure class and end time on every ended generation
tasks.objective: When a generation ends without a usable video, the stored row and the status and list answers say which of eight kinds of failure it was, whether it may still have used the person's quota or money, and what trying again takes. The class is a typed field beside the run state: no error code is added, the error envelope does not change, and trying again is always a new attempt started by the person, never an automatic resubmission.
currentBaseline: `GenerationRecord` in `core/engines/generation.ts` has `state`, a free-text `diagnostic`, `phase`, `cancelled` and `dismissed`. It has no failure class and no end time. `ExecutionStatusSchema` in `core/engines/contract-v2.ts` is a strict object of `executionRef`, `state`, `progress` and `diagnostic`.

Kinds of failure can be told apart only by the words of `diagnostic`. In `core/engines/kaggle.ts` they include "Kaggle's latest run is not this one.", 'The run ended without a video that passed its own checks.', 'The run made a different length from the one asked for.', 'The video is not a size this can take.', 'The run ended without a readable result.', the `WAS_KILLED` text and 'The run failed on Kaggle.'. In `core/engines/comfyui.ts` they include 'The job passed its deadline; ComfyUI was asked to stop it.', 'ComfyUI stopped reporting this job.', 'ComfyUI never reported this job.' and 'ComfyUI reported an error.'.

A refused start: in `createGenerationService.start`, a thrown error or a `{ refused }` answer from `adapter.submit` updates the row to `state: 'failed'` and `dismissed: true` and reaches the caller as a `CommandError`, so the row is not listed ('a push Kaggle refused is a failure with nothing to follow' in `tests/generation-durable.test.ts`). A quota refusal is recognised only inside the `REFUSED_PUSH` pattern in `core/engines/kaggle.ts`, mixed with every other refusal.

`yamakan.generation.status` answers `generationId`, `state`, `progress`, `diagnostic` and `imported`; rows of `yamakan.generation.list` add `uncertain`, `stopped` and `held`. The failure envelope is `error: { code, message, retryable }`, with `code` one of the 14 names in `ErrorCodes` in `core/command/errors.ts` and `retryable` fixed per code.

Nothing resubmits automatically. `core/jobs.ts` says 'A generation is never sent again automatically. Start a new one if it is wanted.'; the button `create-run-done` in `src/create/GeneratePanel.tsx` shows `create.runRetry` on a failed run, dismisses it and returns to the form; the scene `failed` in `scripts/qualify-kaggle-screens.mjs` asserts the attempt count stays 1.

Whether a run may still have used quota or money is said only on a stop: `CancellationSchema.billingOutcome` (`notApplicable`, `refunded`, `charged`, `unknown`), which the Kaggle adapter answers `notApplicable`. No surface says it for a failed or lost run.

Rows are stored as JSON in `jobs.payload` under the kind `remote-generation` by `JobSupervisor.generationLedger()` in `core/jobs.ts`. Its `parse` spreads the stored JSON without a strict schema, so an added optional field needs no SQLite schema step and is ignored by older code.

`core/jobs/rules/jobs.ts`, translated from TheHalfMoon/Gomrey `servers/fastapi/gomrey/jobs.py`, exports `TRANSIENT_ERRORS`, `classifyFailure(errorCode)` (answers `transient` or `permanent`) and `shouldRetry`. Among `core`, `server`, `mcp`, `cli`, `sdk`, `src` and `tests`, only that file and `tests/job-transitions.test.ts` name them.
interfaces: `FailureClass`, a closed enum beside `RefusalReason` in `core/engines/contract-v2.ts`: `refusedByPolicy`, `quotaExhausted`, `providerRejected`, `timeout`, `lostJob`, `invalidArtifact`, `cancelled`, `unknown`, and by OA-18, accepted on 2026-11-23, `credentialRejected` (the provider refused the credential) not billed, `afterChange`; `contentRefused` (the provider refused what the request asks for) may be billed, `afterChange`; `resourceExhausted` (the run said it had not enough memory or another resource) may be billed, `afterChange`. Where this card says eight classes, there are eleven. A Kaggle answer of 401 or 'Authentication required', at the question before a push or at the push, is `credentialRejected`; a run whose receipt, or a ComfyUI error whose type, is named as an out-of-memory error is `resourceExhausted`; no route here reports `contentRefused` yet. `ExecutionStatusSchema` gains `failureClass`, required where the state is `failed` or `cancelled` and refused in any other (OA-17, accepted on 2026-11-23): an adapter that does not know says `unknown`, and one that names none does not conform. `ENGINE_CONTRACT_V2` keeps its id: the field is output-only, every adapter is in this repository and is changed with it, no answer is stored, and the service still reads one without a class as `unknown`.

New `core/engines/failures.ts` (declared in `localFilesInDonorRoots`): the frozen table `FAILURE_CLASSES`, one entry per class with `meaning`, `mayStillBeBilled` and `retry`, where `RetryAdvice` is `afterChange`, `afterWaiting`, `afterChecking` or `whenWanted`.

Table: `refusedByPolicy` (Yamakan or the adapter refused before anything was sent) not billed, `afterChange`; `quotaExhausted` (the provider refused because a quota or rate limit is used up) not billed, `afterWaiting`; `providerRejected` (the provider refused the request for another reason, or took it and reported the run as failed) may be billed once the run was taken, `afterChange`; `timeout` (the run passed its deadline) may be billed, `afterChange`; `lostJob` (the provider no longer reports this run, or reports another in its place) may be billed, `afterChecking`; `invalidArtifact` (the run ended but its result is missing, unreadable, or not what was asked or declared) may be billed, `whenWanted`; `cancelled` (the person stopped it or stopped following it) may be billed, `whenWanted`; `unknown` (ended with no class recorded) may be billed, `afterChecking`.

`effectiveBilling({ failureClass, remote, left, refusedAtSubmit })` in the same file answers `{ mayStillBeBilled, billedIn }`. `mayStillBeBilled` is true only when the table says so, the route runs off this computer (`remote` is recorded on the row), the request may have left (`mayHaveLeft`) and it was not refused at submit. `billedIn` is `providerQuota` when true and `none` otherwise. No currency exists in this build; currency belongs to MPR-222.

A typed carrier for a refusal thrown from `submit`, with no change to `CommandError`: `refusedSubmit(failureClass, message)` builds `new CommandError('CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE', message, { cause: new SubmitRefusal(failureClass) })`, and `failureClassOf(error)` reads the cause. `CommandError` already keeps `options.cause` on the server side behind its public message, so nothing new reaches the wire.

`GenerationRecord` gains three optional fields: `failureClass`, `endedAt` (milliseconds from the service's `now`) and `mayStillBeBilled`. One helper inside `createGenerationService` is the only writer. It runs when a row first reaches `succeeded`, `failed` or `cancelled`, or when the person stops it; the first end wins and is never rewritten. `failureClass` is set only for a failed or stopped row, and is `unknown` when the adapter, against the contract, gave none.

`yamakan.generation.status` and each row of `yamakan.generation.list` gain optional output fields `failureClass`, `mayStillBeBilled`, `billedIn`, `retry` and `endedAt`. Inputs, scopes, the human-only rule and request-id refusal are unchanged; both are read commands.

Kaggle mapping, set where the message is produced (the adapter's `end` gains a class argument): a `{ refused }` answer or a `CommandError` thrown before the push is tried is `refusedByPolicy`; a refused push that matches a new named pattern `QUOTA_REFUSAL` (the quota words, the 'maximum batch, GPU, number or session' words and the 429 phrase, split out of `REFUSED_PUSH`) is `quotaExhausted`; any other refused push is `providerRejected`; no clear answer stays uncertain with no class; "Kaggle's latest run is not this one." is `lostJob`; the receipt's own error, `WAS_KILLED` and 'The run failed on Kaggle.' are `providerRejected`, or `timeout` when `pastLimit(run)` is true at that moment; the failed-checks, wrong-length, wrong-size, unreadable-result and garbled-after-`FETCH_TRIES` messages are `invalidArtifact`, and so is the receipt's own error when Kaggle reports the run complete (the `providerRejected` rule for a receipt's error applies only to a run Kaggle reports as failed); the cancel states are `cancelled`.

ComfyUI mapping: every `{ refused }` is `refusedByPolicy`; the two deadline messages are `timeout`; 'ComfyUI stopped reporting this job.' and 'ComfyUI never reported this job.' are `lostJob`; `execution_error` is `providerRejected`; `execution_interrupted` is `cancelled`. The fake gains an option `failureClass` used with `failExecutions`; the fake says `unknown` when it is given none, and the v1 bridge says `unknown` for a failure and `cancelled` for a stop, since an answer must name one (OA-17, accepted on 2026-11-23).

Service rules: a refused start keeps its code and message, stays failed, dismissed and unlisted, and its stored row now carries the class, `endedAt` and `mayStillBeBilled: false`. An error from `submit` that is not a `CommandError` is `unknown`. An import that fails its length or hash check leaves the row as it is, with no class, because the result can be fetched again.

Retry rule, written in the table's comment and tested: `retry` is advice to the person. A retry is a new `yamakan.generation.start` (a new generation id and `attemptKey`), which passes preflight once MPR-203 has merged. No code path sends again for a row that has a class.

Page: a line with `data-testid='create-run-class'` under the run note in `src/create/GeneratePanel.tsx`, worded by a function in `src/create/create-model.ts` from `failureClass`, `mayStillBeBilled` and `retry`. New keys in `src/i18n.ts`, English and Arabic: `create.failRefused`, `create.failQuota`, `create.failRejected`, `create.failTimeout`, `create.failLost`, `create.failInvalid`, `create.failCancelled`, `create.failUnknown`, `create.billMay`, `create.billNot`, `create.retryAfterChange`, `create.retryAfterWaiting`, `create.retryAfterChecking`, `create.retryWhenWanted`.
No new command, scope, `ErrorCodes` entry, envelope field, table, schema step or contract id. `CancellationSchema.billingOutcome` is unchanged.

`core/engines/manifests.ts`: `ModelManifestSchema.rights` holds only `license` and `commercialUse`; `ACCEPTED_MODEL_LICENSES` is `apache-2.0`, `mit`, `bsd-2-clause`, `bsd-3-clause`; `qualify()` answers `RIGHTS_UNQUALIFIED` for anything else. `PINNED_MODEL_MANIFESTS` is empty, so this check runs against no live route.

`core/engines/candidates.ts`: `selectionBlockers()` reports `MISSING_LICENSE`, `LICENSE_UNACCEPTED` and `GATED_MODEL`, and `packageLicenseAccepted()` checks package licences against `ACCEPTED_PACKAGE_LICENSES`. `core/engines/comfyui.ts`: `PINNED_COMFY_RECIPES` is empty and its recipe type has no licence field.

`src/create/create-model.ts`: `CREATE_MODELS` repeats `licence: 'Apache-2.0'` by hand for its two models, and `parseReceipt` copies `license` from a `yamakan.generation-receipt/v1` receipt into `RunReceipt.licence` without checking it.

interfaces: New browser-safe module `core/engines/licence.ts` (zod only, no `node:` import, in the manner of `core/engines/reasons.ts`). `core/engines` is a donor root, so the file must be declared in `localFilesInDonorRoots` of `docs/provenance/import-policy.json`. It exports `LICENCE_BLOCK_FORMAT = 'yamakan.model-licence/v1'`, `LicenceBlockSchema`, `licenceGate()` and `LicenceRefusal`. MPR-201 lands its own block type, `CatalogLicence` (`weightsLicence`, `sourceUrl`, `verifiedAt`), in `core/engines/catalog.ts`. This card replaces it with `LicenceBlockSchema` so that one type remains, and in the same PR updates `catalogDisagreements` and `tests/model-catalog.test.ts` (both from MPR-201) to compare `weights.name` where they compared `weightsLicence`.
`LicenceTerm` = strict object `{ name: string (1 to 120 characters), spdx: string | null, commercialUse: 'allowed' | 'notAllowed' | 'unknown' }`.

`LicenceBlockSchema` = strict object, every key required: `code: LicenceTerm`; `weights: LicenceTerm`; `baseModel: LicenceTerm | { kind: 'none' }`; `bundled: { name, role, term: LicenceTerm }[]` (0 to 16 entries) with `bundledReviewed: true`, so an empty list is a statement and not an omission; `revenueCap: { kind: 'none' } | { kind: 'cap', amount, currency } | { kind: 'unknown' }`; `territorialExclusions: { kind: 'none' } | { kind: 'excluded', regions: string[] } | { kind: 'unknown' }`; `hostedServiceRight: 'allowed' | 'notAllowed' | 'unknown'`; `outputUse: { kind: 'unrestricted' } | { kind: 'restricted', note } | { kind: 'unknown' }`; `watermark: { kind: 'none' } | { kind: 'visible' | 'invisible', note } | { kind: 'unknown' }`; `gated: 'no' | 'yes' | 'unknown'`; `attribution: { kind: 'none' } | { kind: 'required', text } | { kind: 'unknown' }`; `sourceUrl: string` (https, at most 300 characters); `verifiedAt: string` (ISO date); `evidence: 'DOC' | 'CLAIM' | 'IND' | 'ASSUMED' | 'UNKNOWN'`.
`licenceGate(block: unknown, use: { run: 'local' | 'hosted' }): { offered: true } | { offered: false; reasons: LicenceRefusal[] }`. Pure and synchronous: no clock, no file, no network.

`LicenceRefusal` = `BLOCK_MISSING | BLOCK_INVALID | FIELD_UNKNOWN | NOT_READ_AT_SOURCE | LICENCE_UNACCEPTED | NON_COMMERCIAL | REVENUE_CAP | TERRITORY_EXCLUDED | HOSTED_RUN_NOT_ALLOWED | OUTPUT_USE_RESTRICTED | GATED`. For display every refusal maps to the existing engine reason `RIGHTS_UNQUALIFIED` in `core/engines/reasons.ts`; no code is added to `ErrorCodes` in `core/command/errors.ts`.

`offeredKaggleRecipes()` and the catalog's selection of entries in the offered state additionally require `licenceGate(...).offered`. A Kaggle run is `run: 'hosted'`, because the weights run on a hosted service under the person's own account.

No command is added or removed and no command input changes. `yamakan.generation.options` keeps its `licence` string, now `weights.name` of the block; an entry the gate refuses is absent from `models`.

tasks.title: Show notices, the AGPL source offer and the route licence in the UI; widen the SBOM
tasks.objective: A person using Yamakan can read the third-party notices and the AGPL source offer inside the product, sees the licence terms of a generation route before starting a run, and the SBOM names vendored FFmpeg, the pinned Blender build and the native helper with versions and licences. Everything shown is read from files already in the tree; nothing is fetched at run time.
currentBaseline: `NOTICE` says of the OpenMontage-translated modules (AGPL-3.0, pin `9327439db69021ab4b0e2776729bf3b58fdb5a87`) that a loopback About view will carry the AGPL source-offer link 'when Director UI lands'. The Director UI exists (`src/director/DirectorPanel.tsx`). No About view exists: `src/` has no about folder and no notices or source-offer text, and `src/main.tsx` ends in a plain `<footer>`.

`server/main.ts` serves `/api/v1/hello`, `/api/v1/session`, `/api/v1/tools`, `/api/v1/call`, media routes and static files from `dist/` with content types for `.html .js .css .svg .png` only. No route and no command returns `NOTICE`, `LICENSE` or anything under `notices/` (23 files, about 195 KB in all).
`NOTICE` is not valid UTF-8: eight byte sequences in a single-byte encoding (a section sign and dashes) decode to replacement characters. `LICENSE` and the files under `notices/` decode cleanly.

`docs/provenance/imports.json` records four imports from `calesthio/OpenMontage` under AGPL-3.0 (for example `core/director/manifest.ts` and `core/director/stages.ts`). `package.json` has no `repository` or `homepage` field, so no public source location for Yamakan itself is recorded in the tree.

`scripts/sbom.mjs` (`npm run sbom`, and `npm run sbom:check` in CI) writes `docs/evidence/sbom/yamakan-runtime.cdx.json` (CycloneDX 1.5). It holds the npm runtime packages and one `file` component with a SHA-256 per line of `vendor/ffmpeg-win64-r8/SHA256SUMS`. It records no FFmpeg or libass version, no licence for those files, nothing for Blender and nothing for the `yamakan-procd` crate. No test under `tests/` covers it.
`scripts/bundle.ts`: `scaffoldDevBundle` copies `NOTICE` only (not `LICENSE`, not `notices/`) and writes a second SBOM from `sbomFromPackageLock`, which lists npm packages only.

Version and licence facts already in the tree: `vendor/ffmpeg-win64-r8/BUILD.json` (`ffmpegVersion` 7.1.5, `libassVersion` 0.17.3, `sources` hashes, `binaries` with hash and size per file, `packagesAtBuild`); `BLENDER_PIN` in `core/blender/runtime.ts` (version 5.3.0, commit, archive and tree hashes); `native/procd/Cargo.toml` (`yamakan-procd` 0.1.0, GPL-3.0-or-later, no dependencies).

At generation time the Create workspace shows only a licence name: `src/create/CreateWorkspace.tsx` passes `model.licence`, a hand-typed string from `src/create/create-model.ts`, into the `create.modelFacts` sentence of `src/i18n.ts`. No source URL, date verified, restriction or watermark statement is shown.
interfaces: New read command `yamakan.about.notices`: scope `project:read`, `mutation: false`, not human-only (an agent may read notices), no receipt because nothing changes. Strict input `{ document?: string }`, where `document` must equal one id from a closed index built at service start; no path is accepted and the id is never joined into a path. With no `document` it returns `{ product: { name, version, licence }, documents: { id, title, bytes, sha256 }[] (at most 64), sourceOffer }`. With a `document` it returns `{ id, title, text }`, `text` at most 262144 bytes. An unknown id is `NOT_FOUND`.

`sourceOffer` = `{ modules: { path, upstream, commit, licence }[], yamakanSource: { kind: 'url', url } | { kind: 'unset' }, combinedLicence: 'GPL-3.0-or-later with AGPL-3.0 modules (GPLv3 section 13)' }`. `modules` is derived from the AGPL entries of `docs/provenance/imports.json`. `yamakanSource` comes from a `repository` field in `package.json` once the founder supplies one; while it is absent the value is `unset` and the panel says so in plain words.

tasks.title: Define the hosted-provider profile of EngineAdapterV2 and prove it on a loopback fake
tasks.objective: Write down, as typed code and tests, what a hosted provider adapter must do (hold a credential reference and never the value, submit, poll, download, report usage, state its estimate tier) and prove those rules against a fake provider on 127.0.0.1 inside the test suite. No real provider code and no real host name enter the tree, and nothing in the running product can reach the profile.
currentBaseline: `EngineAdapterV2` in `core/engines/contract-v2.ts` has `capabilities`, optional `location`, `submit`, `status`, `requestCancel`, `enumerateArtifacts`, `readArtifact` and `reconcile`. `EngineContextV2` carries only `openAsset`. The contract has no credential, no usage record and no estimate; the only billing word in it is `billingOutcome` on `CancellationSchema` (`notApplicable`, `refunded`, `charged`, `unknown`).
Engines and providers are off: `ENGINE_ENABLED` is `false` (`core/engines/contract.ts`) and `ROUTER_PROVIDERS_ENABLED` is `false` (`core/router/explain.ts`), where the router rejects every candidate.

Adapters that exist: `createFakeEngineV2` in `core/engines/fake.ts` (in-process, no network), `core/engines/comfyui.ts` (speaks only to a loopback address given by number and sets `redirect: 'error'`), and `core/engines/kaggle.ts` (starts the Kaggle command-line tool through the spawn allowlist). None speaks to a hosted HTTP API. The only `fetch` under `core/` is in `core/engines/comfyui.ts`.

`GenerationRecord` in `core/engines/generation.ts` has optional `remote`, `notice` and `held` fields. It has no credential reference and no usage field, and `bringIn` accepts exactly one `video/mp4` artifact.

There is no credential store. The only secret the service writes is the session `token` file (`writeSecret` in `server/main.ts`). `docs/SECURITY.md` lists customer keys as a later gate ('keys later use a qualified secret service') and provider egress and spend as open 'before any provider activation'.
`docs/PROVIDER_MATRIX.md` and `docs/evidence/yamakan/provider-registry.json` are research data. No file under `core`, `server`, `src`, `cli`, `sdk`, `mcp`, `scripts` or `tests` reads them.

`npm run provenance:check` (`scripts/provenance.mjs`) limits process spawning to `processSpawnAllowlist` and requires every local file in a donor root (`core/engines` is one) to be declared in `localFilesInDonorRoots`. It does not limit network calls. `tests/engine-absence.test.ts` already holds a source-text walk over an import graph that refuses dynamic loads and words such as `fetch` and `WebSocket`; the same technique serves here.
interfaces: New module `core/engines/provider-profile.ts` (declared in `localFilesInDonorRoots` of `docs/provenance/import-policy.json`). It contains no network call, no network import, no host name and no address literal: all input and output goes through an injected `ProviderTransport`. Exports: `PROVIDER_PROFILE = 'yamakan.provider-profile/v1'`, `PROVIDER_PROFILE_ENABLED = false`, and the types and function below.

`CredentialRef` = strict `{ kind: 'vault', id }` with `id` matching `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$`. `CredentialResolver` takes a reference and returns a handle with one method `use(fn)`; the secret bytes exist only inside `fn`. The adapter keeps the reference, never the value, and passes the handle to the transport for each call.

`ProviderTransport` = `{ id, supports: { cancel, idempotencyKey, lookupByClientReference, usage, liveQuote }, quote?(request, credential), submit(request, credential, clientReference), poll(jobId, credential), cancel?(jobId, credential), lookup?(clientReference, credential), artifacts(jobId, credential) }`. Each answer is parsed by a strict bounded schema in the profile before use.

`UsageRecord` = `{ source: 'providerReported' | 'estimateOnly', unit, amount (decimal text), currency (or null for non-money units), asOf, providerJobId }`. `ProviderEstimate` = `{ tier: 'static' | 'liveQuote', unit, low, high, worst, currency, asOf, note }`. The estimate is returned by the profile and is not shown by the MPR-203 preflight, which has no currency; MPR-222 decides, with its money step, how a money figure is shown. The after-the-fact actual is the usage record.

`createProviderAdapter({ transport, credentialRef, resolveCredential, gates, clock })` returns `ProviderAdapter` = `EngineAdapterV2 & { profile, estimate(request), usage(executionRef) }`. The v2 contract and its schemas do not change: the credential reference is bound when the adapter is built, so no request, record or diagnostic ever has a field that could hold a secret.

Job rules the adapter enforces: ask the MPR-204 egress and spend gates before any transport call; send an idempotency key derived from `attemptKey` only where the transport declares support; return the provider job id as `executionRef` so the generation service stores it before the first poll; poll only (no inbound callback), with a bounded interval and the request `deadlineMs`; on first observed success stream each artifact at once through `readArtifactVerified` under `ENGINE_V2_LIMITS`; never place a provider URL in `executionRef`, a record or a diagnostic; never send a second submit for an attempt whose first submit is uncertain, even where an idempotency key exists; classify every failure with the MPR-207 classes, marking 'may still be billed' whenever a submit left this PC and no terminal answer was read.
`GenerationRecord` gains optional `credentialRef` and `usage`. Records written before this card have neither and read unchanged; no format version moves.
No command is added or changed. `generationOf` in `core/command/registry.ts` is untouched, so no command path can build a provider adapter.

Alternatives rejected: a new adapter contract version carrying credential and usage fields in the request schemas (puts a secret-shaped field into persisted requests and forces every existing adapter to move); a data-driven generic HTTP adapter configured by a provider description file (hides provider behaviour in data that no conformance test reads, and invites host names into the tree).

risks: Code that nothing calls can rot. The conformance kit run and the qualification script are what keep it honest; if MPR-222 never happens the profile should be removed rather than left to drift.

The profile is written before any real provider is chosen, so MPR-222 may need to change it (for example a provider that reports usage only on a separate account endpoint). The version string `yamakan.provider-profile/v1` exists so such a change is explicit.

tasks.title: Qualify a Windows DPAPI credential vault for customer provider keys
tasks.objective: A customer's provider key can be entered once by a person, kept on this PC protected by Windows DPAPI for the signed-in Windows account, used by a hosted adapter through a reference, and removed, without the key bytes ever reaching the project, the SQLite authority, a backup, a log, the SDK or an agent. The card also states plainly what this protection does not cover.
currentBaseline: There is no credential store. The only secret the service writes is the session `token` file: `writeSecret` in `server/main.ts` writes it into the workspace root after `restrictToOwner(root, 'dir')`. Agent tokens are stored as hashes (`hashAgentToken` in `core/agents.ts`).

`docs/SECURITY.md` promises that the project, archive, log and SDK never contain credential bytes, says customer keys 'later use a qualified secret service', and states that the product is not a defence against the same Windows account rewriting its own data.
No file under `core`, `server`, `src`, `native`, `scripts`, `cli`, `sdk` or `mcp` calls DPAPI (`CryptProtectData`, `CryptUnprotectData`) or any other secret service.

`native/procd` is a dependency-free Rust crate (`Cargo.toml` has an empty dependency table) with the binaries `yamakan-procd`, `worker-probe` and `yamakan-acl`, each using hand-declared Windows API bindings. `npm run build:native` builds them.

`core/process/access.ts` is the existing pattern for a native helper wrapper: it finds `yamakan-acl` from `YAMAKAN_ACL` or the release folder, answers `CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE` when the helper is not built, and runs it hidden with a timeout and a bounded output buffer. Spawning is limited to the files in `processSpawnAllowlist` of `docs/provenance/import-policy.json`.

`HumanOnlyScopes` in `core/command/registry.ts` are `agent:create`, `agent:revoke`, `director:approve`, `consent:grant` and `consent:revoke`. No scope is named for credentials. `yamakan.generation.start` shows the pattern for a human-only mutation that keeps no receipt: `humanOnly: true` with `refusesRequestId: NO_REPLAY`.

Human presence today rests on the single-use launch secret: `docs/evidence/qualification/q15-user-presence.json` (written by `scripts/qualify-q15-user-presence.ts`) records that no native Windows user-presence helper is wired in `native/procd`.

The workspace backup copies the SQLite database through the SQLite backup API (`backupDatabase` in `core/store.ts`) and the stored object files. Whether it copies any other file from the workspace root is to be confirmed in step 1.
interfaces: New native helper `native/procd/src/bin/yamakan-vault.rs` (found by Cargo as a binary of the existing crate; no new dependency). Sub-commands: `protect` reads at most 8192 secret bytes from standard input and writes the DPAPI blob as base64 to standard output; `unprotect` does the reverse; `selftest` protects and unprotects a random value and prints `OK`. No secret and no path is ever passed as an argument. Failure prints `ERROR <code> <message>` and exits 1, as `yamakan-acl` does. DPAPI is called at user scope with the no-prompt flag; buffers are zeroed before release.

New wrapper `core/process/vault.ts` (added to `processSpawnAllowlist`): `protectSecret(bytes)`, `unprotectSecret(blob)`, `vaultAvailable()`. It finds the helper from `YAMAKAN_VAULT` or the release folder, pipes the secret through standard input, runs hidden with a 10 second timeout and a 64 KiB output bound, and answers `CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE` when the helper is not built or the platform is not Windows.

New module `core/credentials.ts`: `createVault(root)` with `add`, `remove`, `list` and a `CredentialResolver` for MPR-210. Each credential is one owner-only file `<workspace root>/vault/<id>.json` holding `{ format: 'yamakan.credential/v1', id, providerId, label, createdAt, blob }`. At most 16 credentials. The plaintext is never cached: every use unprotects again and the bytes live only inside the resolver's `use` callback.

`yamakan.credentials.add`: scope `consent:grant`, mutation, human-only, `refusesRequestId: NO_REPLAY` (no receipt and no request digest, because the input holds a secret). Strict input `{ providerId, label (1 to 80 characters), secret (1 to 4096 characters) }`; path-free. Returns `{ ref: { kind: 'vault', id } }` and never the secret. It accepts only a `providerId` named by a provider profile (MPR-210) that the build registers; only the loopback fake's profile exists before MPR-222, so on the merged head it answers `CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE` outside tests.
`yamakan.credentials.remove`: scope `consent:revoke`, mutation, human-only, `refusesRequestId: NO_REPLAY`. Strict input `{ id }`. Deletes the file; a missing id is `NOT_FOUND`.

`yamakan.credentials.list`: scope `project:read`, `mutation: false`. Returns `{ id, providerId, label, createdAt }[]` only; never a blob and never a secret. An agent may read this list; it cannot add, remove or resolve.
No user interface is added here. The entry form belongs to MPR-222, which is the first card that has a provider to enter a key for.
tasks.sourceDecision: BUILD: a small dependency-free native helper beside `yamakan-acl`, with blobs kept as owner-only files outside the SQLite authority. Alternatives rejected: calling PowerShell `ProtectedData` (puts an interpreter, its profile, modules and script logging in the path of the secret, starts slowly, and needs a script-host entry in the spawn allowlist); a third-party Node native module (a new dependency with its own licence closure, a native build chain or a trusted pre-built binary, and code running inside the service process).
sourceReuse: The crate layout and hand-declared Windows bindings of `native/procd/src/bin/yamakan-acl.rs`.

`CredentialRef` and `CredentialResolver` from MPR-210.

acceptance: A secret added through `yamakan.credentials.add` is returned by the resolver byte for byte, and is gone after `yamakan.credentials.remove`.

A byte search for a random test secret finds it in none of: the SQLite database and its write-ahead log, the object store, every file under the workspace root (the vault blob included, which holds only ciphertext), a backup taken after the add, the service log output, and any command result.
Add and remove are refused for an agent token, refused without the human proof, and refused with a request id; `tests/parity.test.ts` holds for all three commands.
A contained worker (`worker-probe` under the engine worker profile) cannot read the vault folder, and a second Windows account is denied by the folder's access control.
With the helper not built, or on a platform other than Windows, every vault command answers `CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE` and nothing is written.

`docs/SECURITY.md` carries the threat statement: DPAPI at user scope protects the key against an offline copy of the disk, against other non-administrator accounts, and against accidental inclusion in backups and exports; it does not protect against any process running as the same Windows account, against an administrator or the system account, or while the key is in use in memory; and the key cannot be recovered if the Windows profile is lost or its password is force-reset, in which case the person enters it again.
testPlan: `tests/credential-vault.test.ts` (new): round trip through the commands with a fake provider id in a test catalog; file format and owner-only access; the 16-credential bound; removal; the resolver's `use` scope; the helper-missing path. A seventeenth credential is refused with the bound named in the message.

The same script runs the contained-worker read attempt and the second-account probe (`yamakan-acl probe-other`), and records as a stated limit, not a failure, that a plain process under the same account can unprotect the blob. performanceCriteria: One protect or unprotect through the helper takes under 300 ms at the 95th percentile over 50 runs on the founder host (process start included); the evidence file records the measured figures.
No plaintext cache exists: the unprotect cost is paid on each provider call, and the measured figure is small against a provider round trip.
`yamakan.credentials.list` answers in under 50 ms with 16 credentials.
compatibilityRequirements: Three commands are added; no existing command changes. No new scope is created: the two mutations reuse `consent:grant` and `consent:revoke`, which are already human-only.
No store, schema version or project format changes; the SQLite authority gains no table. The vault is machine and account state, not project state.
Windows only. On any other platform the capability is absent with a typed answer.

definitionOfDone: FD-5 is recorded and the gate check is quoted in the PR.
The helper, wrapper, vault module and commands are merged with the tests above.
The evidence file is committed with head SHA and host, with no step marked PASS that did not run.
`docs/SECURITY.md` states the mechanism and the limits exactly as written in this card.
risks: DPAPI does not defend against software running as the same Windows account, which is the main realistic threat on a personal PC. The statement of what DPAPI covers is [ASSUMED] from general knowledge of the Windows API; confirm it against the vendor documentation before the wording goes into `docs/SECURITY.md`, and let the qualification prove the same-account limit rather than hide it.

Reusing `consent:grant` and `consent:revoke` stretches scopes named for likeness consent. The alternative is a new human-only scope `credential:manage`, which needs founder agreement because the contract keeps the existing scope set. OS user presence (MPR-508, FD-9) would strengthen both choices.

Storage is files beside the `token`, not a table in the SQLite authority. The alternative (a table, workspace schema version 18 to 19 with a migration test) would put ciphertext into every backup and export and conflict with the promise in `docs/SECURITY.md`. The cost of the chosen route is a second small place where state lives; it holds no project truth.

The secret passes through the service process and the command input on its way to the helper. Whether any part of the command pipeline records mutation inputs is not verified; step 1 checks it and adds redaction if needed.
How an installed bundle carries native helpers is not verified (`scripts/bundle.ts` does not mention them); a release that ships providers must ship and hash-check `yamakan-vault` too.
blockingExternalRequirements: FD-5 recorded in `docs/FOUNDER_DECISION_RECORD.md` (customer-credential hosted providers authorised, after legal review of provider terms).

tasks.title: Qualify a local still-image runtime on the CPU-only founder host
tasks.objective: Find out by measurement whether one permissively licensed still-image model can run on the founder's PC (Intel i5-13420H, 16 GiB RAM, integrated graphics, little free disk) inside the existing worker boundary with no network, and move its catalog entry from candidate to qualified only if the measured run passes. Nothing is downloaded and nothing runs until FD-4 is recorded.
currentBaseline: No local model runs today. `PINNED_MODEL_MANIFESTS` in `core/engines/manifests.ts` is empty, `discoverEngineCapabilities` answers `ENGINE_DISABLED` while `ENGINE_ENABLED` is `false`, and `server/main.ts` never passes a `modelRoot` to the command context (it passes `comfyUrl` and `kaggle` only, each from a person-set environment value).

`Operation` in `core/engines/contract-v2.ts` has `textToVideo`, `imageToVideo`, `videoEdit`, `transcribe` and `enhance`; there is no still-image operation. `MediaType` already includes `image/png`. `bringIn` in `core/engines/generation.ts` accepts exactly one `video/mp4` artifact.

`ENGINE_WORKER_PROFILE` in `core/process/owner.ts` allows 4 processes, 30 minutes, 4 GiB of memory, 64 MiB of output, no GPU and no network; `checkProfile` bounds any profile to at most 8 processes, 6 hours and 64 GiB. `RunResult` reports `peakMemoryBytes` and `wallExceeded`.

`RESOURCE_POLICY` (version 3, `core/command/policy.ts`) keeps a 256 MiB disk reserve and a frozen qualification budget under which the worst case at once (the service, one job worker, one preview renderer, the import probes and one engine check, each at its limit; 7,468 MiB by the formula in `scripts/qualify-resources.ts`) must fit in half the RAM (8,192 MiB on a 16 GiB host); it gives no separate allowance to a model worker.

`docs/LOCAL_INFERENCE.md` classes the founder host as a 'Profile A' (offline CPU) candidate only, defines local AI ('Profile B') as an NVIDIA card with at least 8 GB of video memory for image work, 32 GB RAM and at least 60 GB free, and records about 2.9 GiB of free disk at the last preflight; the continuation ledger's entry for PR #278 later records about 1.9 GB free on C:. By that document the host does not qualify for local image work today.

Rights and format checks exist for candidates: `ACCEPTED_PACKAGE_LICENSES`, `selectionBlockers`, `fileFormatOf` and `modelFootprint` in `core/engines/candidates.ts`. `docs/LOCAL_INFERENCE.md` rules out pickle checkpoints and automatic custom-node installation.

The pattern for a large third-party runtime exists: `scripts/blender-install.ts` installs a person-downloaded archive into `workerToolsRoot()` only after its SHA-256 matches `BLENDER_PIN`, and `verifyBlenderForRun` checks it again before use. The product itself downloads nothing.
`docs/SECURITY.md` states that a real Python or model runtime needs its own qualification before use.
interfaces: Runner choice: stable-diffusion.cpp as a native executable (MIT [DOC]; pre-built Windows binaries with a CPU backend [DOC]), so no Python runtime is needed. The exact release, its archive hash and the executable hash are [UNKNOWN] until pinned at gate time.

Model candidates, in order: (1) Z-Image-Turbo, Apache-2.0 [DOC], 8 steps [DOC], about 4 GB when quantised for this runner [IND]; the licences of its text encoder and image decoder and the provenance of the quantised file are [UNKNOWN] and must be closed first. (2) FLUX.2 [klein] 4B, Apache-2.0 [DOC], 4 steps [DOC]; needs a quantised file whose provenance, licence and runner support are [UNKNOWN]. (3) OmniGen2, Apache-2.0 [DOC], low memory with sequential offload but very slow [DOC]; needs a Python runtime and therefore a separate runtime qualification, so it is a second choice. FLUX.1 [schnell] is not a candidate until its licence is read at source (Apache-2.0 is [ASSUMED]).

Refused, as negative catalog entries: FLUX.2 [dev], FLUX.2 [klein] 9B and FLUX.1 Kontext [dev] (non-commercial, gated [DOC]); FLUX 3 Image Klein (revenue cap, gated [DOC]); Qwen-Image-2.1 (research licence [DOC]); Stable Diffusion 3.5 (free only under a revenue cap, gated [DOC]); HiDream-I1 (MIT weights but a gated text encoder [DOC]); Krea-2 and Ideogram 4.0 open (licence [UNKNOWN]). The Apache-2.0 Qwen-Image line [DOC] is not refused on licence but is far too large for this host [ASSUMED].

New module `core/engines/local-image.ts` (declared in `localFilesInDonorRoots`): `LOCAL_IMAGE_PIN` (runner name, version, commit, archive and executable SHA-256; each model file with name, bytes, SHA-256 and format, which must be `gguf` or `safetensors`), `verifyLocalImageForRun`, `LOCAL_IMAGE_WORKER_PROFILE` (network `none`, gpu `none`, memory at most the 4 GiB limit of `ENGINE_WORKER_PROFILE`, wall time set from measurement within `checkProfile`), and `createLocalImageEngine({ toolsRoot, modelRoot, run })` returning an `EngineAdapterV2`. It starts the runner only through the run function of `core/process/owner.ts`; it spawns nothing itself.

New person-run script `scripts/local-image-install.ts` (npm script `local-image:install`), modelled on `scripts/blender-install.ts`: the person downloads the pinned files with their own browser, the script verifies each SHA-256 and installs into `workerToolsRoot()` and the model root. The product gains no downloader.

This card adds the still-image operation by the five steps MPR-206 lists: a written definition in `docs/ENGINE_OPERATIONS.md`, a strict branch in `EngineRequestV2Schema` and the name `textToImage` in `Operation` (`core/engines/contract-v2.ts`), support in `createFakeEngineV2` (`core/engines/fake.ts`) with a passing run of the kit, this card's adapter, and the qualification evidence with a catalog offer. English and Arabic labels for the operation go in `src/i18n.ts`. `bringIn` accepts one `image/png` for that operation.

No command is added. A catalog entry in the qualified state is not shown by `yamakan.generation.options`. For the qualification run only, `server/main.ts` reads a person-set environment value `YAMAKAN_QUALIFY_ROUTE` naming one catalog id (the same pattern as `COMFYUI_URL`); with it set, `yamakan.generation.start` (already human-only with `refusesRequestId: NO_REPLAY`) accepts that one route, and every answer marks it `qualificationOnly`. If MPR-201 or MPR-202 already defines how a qualified entry is run, use that instead.

tasks.title: Qualify local speech-to-text for Arabic and English captions, and one local voice
tasks.objective: Measure on the founder's PC whether a pinned local recogniser turns Arabic and English speech into caption proposals with a stated word error rate, and whether one permissively licensed voice model can speak fixed text, both inside the engine worker profile with no network. Entries move from candidate to qualified only on measured evidence; nothing is downloaded until FD-4 is recorded.
currentBaseline: The refusal lives in the command, not in the audio module: `yamakan.audio.transcribe` in `core/command/registry.ts` (scope `render:execute`, `mutation: false`, strict input `{ projectId, assetId, language }`) runs `assertLanguage`, `assertTranscribable` and `discoverEngineCapabilities`, then always throws `CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE`.

`core/audio/transcription.ts` already fixes the contract: `WHISPER_CPP` pins whisper.cpp version 1.9.5 (repository `ggml-org/whisper.cpp`, a commit, licence MIT, output flag `-ojf`); `WHISPER_LANGUAGES` includes `en` and `ar`; `TRANSCRIPTION_LIMITS` bounds a source to 3600 seconds, a run to 600 seconds of wall time and the queue to 2; `extractPcm`, `parseWhisperJson`, `TranscriptSchema`, `standInTranscript` and `captionProposal` exist. No runner executable and no model file is pinned by hash, and none is installed.
`server/main.ts` never passes a `modelRoot` to the command context, and `PINNED_MODEL_MANIFESTS` in `core/engines/manifests.ts` is empty.
There is no speech synthesis anywhere under `core/audio`, and `Operation` in `core/engines/contract-v2.ts` has no voice operation. `MediaType` already includes `audio/wav` and `text/vtt`.
`tests/transcription-contract.test.ts` is the only test that names `audio.transcribe`. Caption editing is already qualified separately (`scripts/qualify-captions-keyboard.mjs`).

`docs/SECURITY.md` requires a real model runtime to pass its own qualification inside the worker boundary before use, and the E-SEC row of `docs/plans/P10-qualification-activation/RELEASE_GATE_MATRIX.md` is open with the default 'Keep engines off'.

`docs/LOCAL_INFERENCE.md` lists faster-whisper as a CPU candidate with 'No output/Arabic benchmark', names 'optional CPU transcription later' for the offline CPU profile, and records about 2.9 GiB of free disk on the founder host; the continuation ledger's entry for PR #278 later records about 1.9 GB free on C:.

FD-4 as written covers speech-to-text and one voice model whose code and weights are under Apache-2.0, MIT or BSD terms, for qualification only. Lip sync, music, restoration and local video are outside it.
interfaces: Recogniser choice: whisper.cpp 1.9.5 as a native executable (MIT, as `WHISPER_CPP` already records; availability of a pre-built Windows binary for that version is [UNKNOWN]) with one multilingual Whisper model file. First candidate Whisper large-v3-turbo (MIT [DOC]); the provenance and licence of its converted model file and its size are [UNKNOWN] and must be closed in the MPR-208 block. Fallback: a smaller multilingual Whisper model if disk, memory or speed rule the first out. The research notes did not evaluate whisper.cpp itself, so its Arabic quality is [UNKNOWN] until measured.

Recogniser alternatives recorded: faster-whisper (MIT [DOC]) with WhisperX (BSD-2-Clause [DOC]) is rejected for the first qualification because it needs a Python runtime and its Arabic alignment model is [UNKNOWN]. Refused: pyannote diarisation (gated [DOC]); Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 (CC-BY-4.0 [DOC], no Arabic, and outside the FD-4 licence list).

New module `core/audio/whisper.ts`: `WHISPER_RUNTIME_PIN` (archive and executable SHA-256 for the `WHISPER_CPP` version; model file name, bytes and SHA-256), `verifyWhisperForRun`, and `runWhisper({ run, toolsRoot, modelRoot, pcm, language, signal })`, which starts the runner only through the run function of `core/process/owner.ts` under `ENGINE_WORKER_PROFILE` unchanged (4 GiB, no GPU, no network) and returns a transcript through `parseWhisperJson`. If the model does not fit that profile, choose a smaller model; do not widen the profile.

`yamakan.audio.transcribe` keeps its input, its scope `render:execute` and `mutation: false`; it stores nothing and returns a transcript and a caption proposal that a person accepts through the existing caption commands. It answers with a transcript only when the catalog entry for the route is in the required state, the service was given a model root, and the runner and model hashes verify; in every other case it throws the same `CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE` as today. A qualified but not offered entry runs only when the person-set `YAMAKAN_QUALIFY_ROUTE` names it (the switch MPR-220 describes; add it here if that card has not landed).

Voice choice (FD-4 allows one): Kokoro-82M, Apache-2.0 [DOC], English, fixed built-in voices, no Arabic [DOC]. A way to run it on Windows without Python is not verified; if it needs Python, that runtime gets its own containment qualification first or the voice part records BLOCKED. Arabic voice is a recorded gap. Alternative for the one slot: Chatterbox Multilingual (MIT [DOC], includes Arabic, retired upstream, embeds a watermark [DOC], CPU fitness [UNKNOWN]). Habibi-TTS (code MIT, some checkpoints Apache-2.0, others non-commercial [IND]) only after its licence texts are read at source.

Voices refused, as negative catalog entries: F5-TTS (non-commercial weights [DOC]); XTTS-v2 (Coqui Public Model License [DOC]); Higgs Audio v3 (research or non-commercial [DOC]); Fish Speech and OpenAudio (revenue cap, no hosted-service right [DOC]); IndexTTS (custom licence [DOC]); VibeVoice (research only [DOC]); Piper (GPL-3.0 with per-voice licences [ASSUMED]; read the licence at source before recording the refusal; outside the FD-4 list).

New module `core/audio/speech.ts`: the voice pin, its verify step and an `EngineAdapterV2` for the speech operation, producing one `audio/wav`. This card adds that operation by the five steps MPR-206 lists: a written definition in `docs/ENGINE_OPERATIONS.md`, a strict branch in `EngineRequestV2Schema` and the name `textToSpeech` in `Operation` (`core/engines/contract-v2.ts`), support in `createFakeEngineV2` (`core/engines/fake.ts`), this adapter, and the qualification evidence with a catalog offer. Input is text and a built-in voice id only: no reference audio and no voice cloning. No command is added; the run goes through `yamakan.generation.start` (human-only, `refusesRequestId: NO_REPLAY`), whose strict input gains a speech form holding the text and the voice id, and `bringIn` accepts one `audio/wav` for that operation.

New person-run script `scripts/local-speech-install.ts` (npm script `local-speech:install`), modelled on `scripts/blender-install.ts`: verifies person-downloaded files against the pins and installs them. The product gains no downloader.

Part a. Fix the measurement method in the evidence file before the run: the sample set (own recordings or permissively licensed speech, with duration per language), who wrote the reference text (a native Arabic reviewer under X-01), the Arabic and English normalisation rules, and the pass thresholds.
