tasks.title: Make the MCP tool list honest: filter by scope, fix mutation flags, handle cancellation
tasks.evidence: Merged as 5306ea9166ecb2e9a1fc1c7497271344de6995e1 (PR #297, pinned to 4105406, which adds only the receipt to 49d0e48); qualify:agent-mcp passed at 49d0e48 on the founder host (docs/evidence/qualification/mpr-501-agent-mcp.json), its cancelled call before it was sent; cancelling after the send is tested with a held test service; main's CI passed
tasks.objective: An agent connected over MCP is shown exactly the tools its token can call, each marked truthfully as reading or changing (and destructive or not), and a request the client cancels stops cleanly instead of being ignored.
currentBaseline: Facts read at main 4a8e1b5850f6c4302fe3e4563d6c378afeaf16b5. The baseline 7b1ca46ce20efaa603be12b51d57aee04a3f5f72 adds only PR #278 (six files: four code and test files of the Blender render path and two documents), which changes no fact stated here. `core/command/registry.ts` `catalog()` returns all 116 commands as `{name, scope, mutation, summary, legacyAlias, inputSchema}`; it takes no principal and carries neither `humanOnly` nor `refusesRequestId`.

`server/api.ts` `CreativeAPI.catalog()` and the `GET /api/v1/tools` route in `server/main.ts` return that full list to any authenticated principal. `mcp/main.ts` `tools()` turns every entry into a tool, so a token that holds only `project:read` is shown every tool plus the composite `yamakan_document_save`.

13 commands are `humanOnly: true` (the four `yamakan.consent.*`, `yamakan.generation.start|dismiss|cancel|import`, `yamakan.director.importLegacy`, `yamakan.director.approve`, `yamakan.agent.create|list|revoke`). `authorize` in `core/command/registry.ts` refuses them with `SCOPE_DENIED` ('This command requires the browser session.') unless the principal is `browser-ui`; an agent learns this only by calling.

`yamakan.proxy.build` and `yamakan.proxy.cancel` are declared `mutation: false` although their `run` calls `buildProxy` / `cancelProxy` in `core/media/proxies.ts`, which start and stop a build. `mcp/main.ts` `catalogTools` therefore advertises both with `readOnlyHint: true`.

`catalogTools` emits only `annotations: { readOnlyHint: !t.mutation }`. [DOC] The MCP specification (revision 2025-06-18, `ToolAnnotations`) has clients assume `destructiveHint: true` when it is absent, so every Yamakan mutation is presented as possibly destructive.

`mcp/main.ts` `handle` treats `notifications/cancelled` like `notifications/initialized` and returns; in-flight requests are counted (`MCP_LIMITS.inFlight` 16 in `mcp/framing.ts`) but not tracked by JSON-RPC id, and `sdk/client.ts` `YamakanClient.call(operation, parameters, requestId?)` accepts no abort signal.

Tests that pin the surface: `tests/parity.test.ts` ('REST and MCP replay the journey with identical results, errors and canonical bytes') requires MCP tool titles (minus the MCP-only composite `yamakan_document_save`, whose title is not a command name) to equal the REST catalog names for the same token and `tool.annotations.readOnlyHint === !command.mutation`; `tests/command.test.ts` requires `catalog().length === Object.keys(commands).length`; `tests/request-id-refusal.test.ts` requires every mutation to do exactly one of keep a receipt (its `run` source contains the word 'receipt') or set `refusesRequestId`, and the refusing set to equal its `validInput` keys.
interfaces: No new command. `core/command/registry.ts`: exported predicate `mayCall(principal, definition)` used by `authorize` and by the new `catalogFor(principal)`, which returns `{ tools, withheld }`; `catalog()` with no argument still returns every command.

Catalog entry gains three fields: `humanOnly: boolean`, `destructive: boolean`, `requestId: 'replayed' | 'refused' | 'none'` (replayed = mutation with a receipt, refused = `refusesRequestId` set, none = read).

`Definition` gains optional `destructive?: true`. Proposed initial members (each to be confirmed against its `run` in step 0; membership not verified here): `yamakan.workspace.restore`, `yamakan.workspace.collectGarbage`, `yamakan.job.cancel`, `yamakan.job.discard`, `yamakan.export.batchCancel`, `yamakan.proxy.cancel`, `yamakan.consent.revoke`, `yamakan.agent.revoke`, `yamakan.generation.cancel`, `yamakan.generation.dismiss`.
`yamakan.proxy.build` and `yamakan.proxy.cancel`: `mutation: true` and `refusesRequestId: NO_REPLAY` (scope `render:execute` unchanged, not human-only, input unchanged).

`CreativeAPI.catalog(principal?)`; the `GET /api/v1/tools` body keeps its fields, `tools` becomes the caller's callable commands and a new `withheld: [{ name, reason: 'scope' | 'browser-only' }]` names the rest.

MCP tool annotations: `readOnlyHint` (unchanged rule) and, on mutations only, `destructiveHint` from the registry. `idempotentHint` and `openWorldHint` are deliberately not emitted: the registry holds no fact they could be derived from.
`YamakanClient.call(operation, parameters, requestId?, options?: { signal?: AbortSignal })`.

`mcp/cancellation.ts` (new): `CANCEL_TWINS` (start command -> cancel command and how its arguments are built) and a pure `cancelPlan(operation, phase)` returning `abort` | `finish-then-cancel` | `finish-and-drop` | `ignore`.
tasks.sourceDecision: BUILD: filter in the service (one predicate shared with `authorize`) so REST and MCP stay identical per principal; the alternative of keeping human-only tools listed with a marker is rejected because a listed tool should be callable, and the alternative of filtering inside the MCP process is rejected because it would break the parity assertion.

tasks.title: Add a bounded job wait and a revision event cursor for agents
tasks.objective: An agent can wait for a job to change or finish in one bounded call and can follow committed project revisions from a cursor, through REST, the SDK, the CLI and MCP, without tight polling and without a new scheduler or socket server.
currentBaseline: `yamakan.job.status` in `core/command/registry.ts` (scope `job:read`, read, input `{ jobId }`) returns `JobSupervisor.status(jobId)` from `core/jobs.ts`, whose `#view` shape is `{id, projectId, revision, state, detail, progress, error, artifact, planHash, loudness}`. There is no way to wait: a client polls.

`core/store.ts` `events(afterEventId = 0, limit = 100)` reads the `outbox` table (`event_id` AUTOINCREMENT, `project_id`, `revision`, `operation`; a row is written beside both `INSERT INTO revisions` statements) and clamps the limit to 1..1000. No command exposes it; its only caller is `tests/workspace-db.test.ts`. No `DELETE FROM outbox` was found under `core`, so the table is not pruned.

`server/main.ts` has no websocket or server-sent-event route and sets `server.setTimeout(120_000)`. The preview, peaks and thumbnail routes stop work when the client leaves (`res.once('close', ...)` with an `AbortController`); `POST /api/v1/call` passes no signal and `CommandContext` has none.

Job progress is a number from 0 to 1 held in memory by `JobSupervisor` (`#progress`, read by `#view` as `this.#progress.get(row.job_id) ?? row.progress`); a Blender render reports `Math.min(0.9, 0.9 * made / frames)`. Whether any path changes a `remote-generation` job without a caller's request was not verified.

SS-007 work already on main covers a different need: `yamakan.progress.read` (`core/progress.ts` `readProgress`, hash cursor, `PROGRESS_LIMITS`) is a snapshot of Director runs, and `sdk/progress.ts` states 'There are no notifications: a client reads, and after a reconnect reads again.'
`sdk/client.ts` has no `waitForJob` or `followEvents`. `cli/main.ts` knows `<operation> <json> [requestId]`, `tools` and `stage-document` and exits 1 on a `YamakanError`.
`mcp/main.ts` writes only responses: it declares `capabilities: { tools: { listChanged: false } }` and never sends `notifications/progress`.

A restore gives the workspace a fresh execution epoch (`director_epoch`, raised in `core/recovery.ts`; read by `epochOf` in `core/director/runtime.ts`), and writes the backup into a new workspace folder while the original stays unchanged, so an `event_id` saved against the original may not mean the same row in the restored copy.
interfaces: `yamakan.job.wait`: scope `job:read`, read (`mutation: false`), not human-only, no request id. Input (strict): `{ jobId: Id, waitMs?: integer 0..25000 (default 25000), knownDetail?: one of the job states, knownProgress?: number 0..1 }`. Output: exactly the `yamakan.job.status` shape, read at the moment of return.

Return rule for `yamakan.job.wait`: at once when the job is terminal, is a `remote-generation` job, or already differs from what the caller knows; otherwise when `detail` changes, when `progress` exceeds `knownProgress` by at least 0.01, or when `waitMs` passes. Without `knownDetail` it returns only on a terminal state or the time limit.

`yamakan.events.read`: scope `project:read`, read. Input (strict): `{ after?: integer >= 0, epoch?: integer >= 1, limit?: integer 1..200 (default 100), projectId?: Id }`. Output: `{ format: 'yamakan.events', formatVersion: 1, epoch, reset, events: [{ eventId, kind: 'revision', projectId, revision, operation }], next, more }`.

`reset` is true when the caller's `epoch` is not the workspace's current epoch; the page then starts from the beginning. `next` is the last event id scanned (equal to `after` when nothing was scanned) and can always be passed back as `after`.

`JOB_WAIT = Object.freeze({ maxMs: 25_000, waiters: 32, waitersPerPrincipal: 4 })` and `EVENT_LIMITS = Object.freeze({ page: 200, scan: 5_000 })` as module constants (`core/jobs.ts`, `core/store.ts`); `RESOURCE_POLICY` is not touched.
`CommandContext.signal?: AbortSignal`, set by `server/main.ts` for `POST /api/v1/call` and passed through `CreativeAPI.execute`.

`sdk/wait.ts` (new): `waitForJob(client, jobId, { timeoutMs?, signal?, onUpdate? })` resolving `{ job, finished }`, and `followEvents(client, { after?, epoch?, projectId?, intervalMs?, signal? })`, an async iterator of `{ events, next, epoch, reset }` pages.
CLI: `npm run cli -- wait <jobId> [timeoutSeconds]` prints the last status; exit 0 when the job succeeded, 1 when it failed, was cancelled or the call failed, 2 when the time ran out first.

MCP: for `yamakan_job_wait` called with `params._meta.progressToken`, `notifications/progress` with `{ progressToken, progress, total: 1, message: <detail> }` each time progress rises; no other tool emits progress.
tasks.sourceDecision: BUILD: a long poll inside the existing HTTP service with an in-process notifier in `JobSupervisor`; the alternatives (a websocket or server-sent-event stream, or job rows added to `outbox`) are rejected because the server has neither today and the brief allows no new scheduler or socket server.
sourceReuse: `JobSupervisor.status` and `#view` in `core/jobs.ts` (the wait returns this exact value).
`ProjectStore.events` and the `outbox` table in `core/store.ts`.
The client-left pattern already used by the preview route in `server/main.ts` (`res.once('close', ...)` and an `AbortController`).
The `AbortSignal` option on `YamakanClient.call` and the in-flight table in `mcp/main.ts`, both added by MPR-501; `scripts/qualify-agent-mcp.mjs`, added by MPR-501.
No third-party code and no new dependency.
implementationSequence: Verify live main and reproduce the gap: confirm there is no `yamakan.job.wait` or `yamakan.events.read`, that `ProjectStore.events` has no command caller, and that an agent following an export must poll `yamakan.job.status`. If both commands exist with these contracts, record ALREADY_SATISFIED with evidence. In the same step list every place in `core/jobs.ts` that writes a job's state or progress.

`core/jobs.ts`: add a private notifier (`Map` of job id to a set of callbacks) and call it from every writer found in step 0 (claim, running, validating, finish, succeed, cancel, retry, discard, release, and one private setter that replaces the direct `#progress.set` calls). Add `wait(jobId, options, principalId, signal?)` that reads `status`, applies the return rule, and otherwise parks one waiter with a single timer for `waitMs`. A waiter is removed on return, on `signal` abort and in `close()`, which resolves every waiter with the current status.
Bound the waiters with `JOB_WAIT`: more than 32 in the service or 4 for one principal refuses the newest with `BUSY` (retryable). A `remote-generation` job is never parked.

`core/store.ts`: extend `events` (or add `eventsPage`) to take `projectId` and return `{ events, next, more }`, scanning at most `EVENT_LIMITS.scan` rows by primary key per call so a sparse project filter cannot walk the whole table. Add a public read of the workspace epoch (the value `epochOf` reads).

`core/command/registry.ts`: append `yamakan.job.wait` and `yamakan.events.read` with bounded strict schemas; add `signal` to `CommandContext`. `server/main.ts` and `server/api.ts`: create the signal for `POST /api/v1/call` and pass it into the context.

`sdk/wait.ts`: `waitForJob` loops `yamakan.job.wait`, passing back the last `detail` and `progress`, until a terminal state or `timeoutMs` (default 10 minutes); a network failure is retried with a growing pause up to 5 seconds, a `BUSY` answer after 1 second; when the service answers `VALIDATION` 'Unknown operation.' it falls back to reading `yamakan.job.status` once a second. `followEvents` reads pages and sleeps `intervalMs` (default 2000, minimum 500) only when a page is empty.
`cli/main.ts`: add the `wait` verb on top of `waitForJob`, with the exit codes above; `wait` cannot collide with an operation because every operation name starts with `yamakan.` or the legacy prefix.

`mcp/main.ts`: when `yamakan_job_wait` arrives with a progress token, serve it as a loop of service calls of at most 5 seconds each inside the caller's `waitMs`, sending a progress notification only when progress is higher than the last one sent and at most twice a second; stop on `notifications/cancelled` (MPR-501 table). Without a token it is one service call.
Tests (see testPlan). Update `tests/parity.test.ts` so the journey calls both new commands on both transports.
Document the two commands, the bounds and the cursor rule in `docs/AGENT_MCP_ARCHITECTURE.md` and `docs/OPERATIONAL_CONTRACTS.md`; add the `wait` verb to `README.md`.
Extend `scripts/qualify-agent-mcp.mjs` with the wait-and-restart journey, run it on the Windows host and commit the receipt.
acceptance: `yamakan.job.wait` for a finished job returns at once with a value deep-equal to `yamakan.job.status`.

For a queued job that then runs to success, a caller that passes back `knownDetail` and `knownProgress` sees each state change in order and a final `succeeded` status, with fewer service calls than one per second of job time.
With `waitMs: 0` the command behaves as `yamakan.job.status`; with no change it returns after `waitMs` (within 500 ms) with the unchanged status.

`yamakan.events.read` returns committed revisions in `eventId` order, never skips one, and a second call with `after: next` continues where the first stopped; `more` is false only when the scan reached the end of the table.
After a workspace restore, a call with the old `epoch` returns `reset: true` and the new epoch.
Both commands appear in the REST catalog and the MCP list for a token with the scope, with `readOnlyHint: true`, and `tests/parity.test.ts` passes.
`waitForJob` and `npm run cli -- wait` finish correctly when the service is restarted while they wait, using an agent token.
An MCP client that sent a progress token receives increasing progress values for a running job and then the final status as the tool result.
testPlan: New `tests/job-wait.test.ts`: return rule (terminal, changed, unchanged until the limit, `waitMs: 0`), the waiter bounds, release on abort and on `close()`, `remote-generation` returning at once, the SDK fallback against a registry without the command, and the CLI `wait` exit codes by spawning `cli/main.ts`.

New `tests/events-read.test.ts`: paging, `more`, the `projectId` filter with the scan bound (seed more than `EVENT_LIMITS.scan` rows of another project), `reset` after an epoch bump, and scope refusal.
Extend `tests/jobs.test.ts` ('a graceful shutdown re-queues running work for the next start'): a parked waiter resolves when the supervisor closes and no timer keeps the process alive.
Extend `tests/parity.test.ts` with both commands and `tests/mcp-surface.test.ts` (added by MPR-501) with the progress notifications and their absence without a token.
`npm test`; `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` and `npm run format:check` cover `sdk`, `cli`, `mcp` and `core`.
negativeTests: A token without `job:read` is refused `yamakan.job.wait` with `SCOPE_DENIED`; a token without `project:read` is refused `yamakan.events.read`.
`waitMs` of 25001, a negative `after`, `limit` of 201, or an unknown property is refused with `VALIDATION` before any waiter is parked.
An unknown job id answers as `yamakan.job.status` does today and parks nothing.
The fifth concurrent wait of one principal and the thirty-third in the service are refused with `BUSY`; the earlier ones still complete.
A client that disconnects mid-wait leaves no waiter and no timer behind (waiter count returns to zero).
No progress notification is sent for a call without a progress token, after the response, or with a value lower than the previous one.
e2eQualification: Extend `scripts/qualify-agent-mcp.mjs` (`npm run qualify:agent-mcp`, added by MPR-501): a JSON-RPC client over stdio with an agent token holding `project:write`, `render:execute`, `job:read` and `job:control` creates a project, uploads a fixture clip through `POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/assets` with the same token, places it with `yamakan_timeline_insert`, starts `yamakan_export_video`, waits with `yamakan_job_wait` and a progress token, the script restarts the service during the export, the client waits again until `succeeded`, then reads `yamakan_events_read` from the cursor it saved before the restart.

If the media runtime (`scripts/media-runtime-preflight.mjs`) is absent the run is BLOCKED, not PASS.

At most 32 parked waiters and one timer per waiter; an idle wait performs two status reads (entry and exit).

Boundary with SS-008: cancellation and recovery semantics are not changed; a wait only observes them. Boundary with SS-010: no browser polling loop is changed here.

A writer of job state that does not call the notifier would make a waiter late until its time limit, never wrong (the value is re-read on exit). The test in step 1 drives every transition in `core/jobs/rules/yamakan-transitions.ts` and fails if a waiter is not woken.

Held requests use sockets and MCP in-flight slots (16). The bounds and the 25-second ceiling, well under the server's 120-second timeout, limit this; [ASSUMED] common MCP clients time a request out at about 60 seconds.

tasks.title: Let the CLI and SDK act as an agent, generate CLI help, and add media import helpers
tasks.objective: The CLI and the SDK can run under an agent token taken from a file or the environment by the same rule as MCP, the CLI explains every operation from the live catalog, and an agent can bring media into a project through an SDK helper or an MCP tool that reads only from one configured import folder.
currentBaseline: `cli/main.ts` always reads `<workspace>/token` and so always acts as `local-client`; it never reads `YAMAKAN_AGENT_TOKEN` or `YAMAKAN_AGENT_TOKEN_FILE`. An agent contained in another Windows account (the arrangement `docs/SECURITY.md` asks for) cannot read that file, so it cannot use the CLI at all.

`mcp/main.ts` has the only agent-token rule: `bearerToken()` takes `YAMAKAN_AGENT_TOKEN`, else the file named by `YAMAKAN_AGENT_TOKEN_FILE` (re-read for every call), else the workspace token; at start-up it exits with code 2 unless one of the two is non-blank or `YAMAKAN_MCP_LOCAL_CLIENT=1` is set ('never a fallback'). Both names also accept the `DARZAIN_` prefix through `env()`.

`sdk/client.ts` `ClientOptions.token` is a fixed string (comment: 'Local-client bearer credential read from the workspace token file'); the SDK is also the browser's client (`src/main.tsx`), so it must stay free of Node-only imports.

The CLI has no help: with no arguments it throws a usage `Error`; `--help` is sent to the service as an operation and comes back as `VALIDATION` 'Unknown operation.'. Its verbs are `<operation> <json> [requestId]`, `tools` and `stage-document`.

Media import is a REST route, not a command: `POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/assets` in `server/main.ts` (authorised as `yamakan.project.save`, name in `X-Asset-Name`, `Content-Length` required, answer 200 `{ project, asset, probe }` or, for variable-frame-rate video, 202 `{ project, asset: null, job }` after a second check as `yamakan.export.video`). The catalog advertises it as `assetImport` in `server/api.ts`.

Only the browser uses that route (`importMedia` in `src/main.tsx`). `YamakanClient` has `uploadStudioBitmap` and `uploadCinemaModel` but no asset import; the header of `tests/parity.test.ts` says 'Media import has no MCP tool', and MCP's only composite is `yamakan_document_save`.
`tests/command.test.ts` forbids input properties named `path`, `file`, `filename`, `url`, `uri` and similar, for every registry command; there is no `tests/cli*.test.ts`.
interfaces: No new registry command and no new scope. The media tools are MCP-only composites over the existing upload route, like `yamakan_document_save`.

`sdk/credentials.ts` (new, Node-only, never imported by `sdk/client.ts` or `src`): `resolveCredential(env, { allowLocalClient })` returning `{ principalKind: 'agent' | 'local-client', read(): Promise<string> }`, and `clientFromEnvironment(options)` returning a `YamakanClient` bound to the loopback URL rule of `cli/main.ts`.

Credential rule (one implementation for MCP, CLI and SDK): a non-blank `YAMAKAN_AGENT_TOKEN` wins; else `YAMAKAN_AGENT_TOKEN_FILE`, read and trimmed for every request; if either variable is set but blank, or the file is missing, unreadable or empty, the call fails and nothing is sent; the workspace token is used only when neither variable is set and `allowLocalClient` is true (CLI: true, as today; MCP: only with `YAMAKAN_MCP_LOCAL_CLIENT=1`, as today).

tasks.title: Add hash-bound approval requests so an agent can ask a person to run a human-only command
tasks.objective: An agent that needs a human-only operation files a request bound to the command name and the hash of its exact input; a person sees it in a browser inbox, and approving it runs that one command once as the browser principal. Declining, expiry, a restore or revoking the agent leaves nothing run, and the agent can poll the outcome.
currentBaseline: `authorize` in `core/command/registry.ts` refuses every `humanOnly` command unless `principal.id === 'browser-ui'` (`SCOPE_DENIED`, 'This command requires the browser session.'). Thirteen commands are `humanOnly`: `yamakan.consent.grant|list|revalidate|revoke`, `yamakan.generation.start|dismiss|cancel|import`, `yamakan.director.importLegacy`, `yamakan.director.approve`, `yamakan.agent.create|list|revoke`.

An agent has no way to ask. There is no command group `approval`, no table for requests and no inbox in `src`; the registry comment above the generation commands says 'An agent cannot start one.' The four generation commands are scope `project:write`, `humanOnly`, `refusesRequestId: NO_REPLAY`.

The only hash-bound human approval today is `yamakan.director.approve` (scope `director:approve`, human-only, keeps a receipt): it binds a Director stage output by `outputHash` and `ttlMs` through `approveStage` in `core/director/runtime.ts`. It approves a result that already exists, not a pending command, and cannot carry an agent's request.

`execute` builds a request digest only for a mutation that came with a request id: `sha256Hex(canonicalJson({ apiVersion, format, operation, input }))`. The expression is inline in `execute`; there is no exported helper.

`GenerationRecord` in `core/engines/generation.ts` names no principal, so nothing records who asked for a generation. `createGenerationService().start` refuses an image-to-video unless `noUnconsentedPerson === true` (`VALIDATION`, 'Say that the still shows no real person whose consent to send it is not recorded.'); the type comment calls it 'a person's word' that 'is asked for each run'.

The workspace database is at `WORKSPACE_SCHEMA_VERSION = 18` (`core/store.ts`, latest block `SCHEMA_V18`) and is migrated one version at a time by `PRAGMA user_version`. Modules outside the store write through `store.transaction((db) => ...)`, as `core/director/runtime.ts` does. A workspace epoch exists (`director_epoch`; `bumpDirectorEpoch` exported, `epochOf` module-private) and `core/recovery.ts` raises it on restore.

MCP adds a `requestId` property to every tool schema (`REQUEST_ID` in `mcp/main.ts`), and `tests/command.test.ts` forbids input properties named `command`, `args`, `code`, `script`, `path` and similar. A request therefore cannot name its target `command` or its own id `requestId`.

`core/command/errors.ts` has no conflict code: the closed list is `VALIDATION`, `UNAUTHENTICATED`, `FORBIDDEN_ORIGIN`, `SCOPE_DENIED`, `NOT_FOUND`, `REVISION_CONFLICT`, `IDEMPOTENCY_MISMATCH`, `BUSY`, `LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, `MEDIA_INVALID`, `RECOVERY_REQUIRED`, `CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE`, `UNAVAILABLE`, `INTERNAL`.
interfaces: Storage: one new table `approval_requests` in the existing workspace database, added as the next free `WORKSPACE_SCHEMA_VERSION` at rebase (18 today, so 19 unless another card took it). Columns: `approval_id` (32 hex, primary key), `requester` (principal id), `operation`, `input_json` (canonical JSON of the parsed input, at most 32768 bytes), `input_hash` (64 hex), `reason`, `state` (`pending`, `approved`, `declined`, `withdrawn`), `epoch`, `created_at`, `expires_at`, `decided_at`, `decided_by`, `attested` (0 or 1), `executed_hash`, `outcome` (null, `started`, `succeeded`, `refused`), `generation_id`, `refusal_code`, `refusal_message` (at most 300 characters), `decline_note`. A unique partial index on (`requester`, `input_hash`) where `state = 'pending'`. Old databases gain the empty table; no existing row is rewritten.

`core/approvals.ts` (new): `APPROVAL_ELIGIBLE` (the four names below), `APPROVAL_NEVER` (the nine names below), `APPROVAL_LIMITS = { pendingPerRequester: 5, pendingWorkspace: 50, filedPerRequesterPerDay: 30, reasonChars: 500, inputBytes: 32_768, minMinutes: 5, maxMinutes: 1440, defaultMinutes: 60 }`, and the functions `fileApproval`, `readApprovals`, `withdrawApproval`, `listApprovals`, `claimApproval`, `settleApproval`, `declineApproval`. Limits are module constants; `RESOURCE_POLICY` is not touched.

Eligible (4): `yamakan.generation.start`; and `yamakan.generation.import`, `yamakan.generation.cancel`, `yamakan.generation.dismiss` only for a `generationId` recorded in `generation_id` of the same requester's own approved start. Never eligible (9): `yamakan.consent.grant`, `yamakan.consent.revoke`, `yamakan.consent.revalidate`, `yamakan.consent.list`, `yamakan.agent.create`, `yamakan.agent.list`, `yamakan.agent.revoke`, `yamakan.director.importLegacy`, `yamakan.director.approve`. The three human-only commands this card adds (`yamakan.approval.list`, `yamakan.approval.approve`, `yamakan.approval.decline`) are also in `APPROVAL_NEVER`, beyond the nine listed here, so the partition test passes. A human-only command in neither list is refused (default never).

`core/command/registry.ts`: exported `inputDigest(operation, input)` holding the digest expression that `execute` uses today (same bytes as before for receipts); new optional `CommandContext.onBehalfOf?: string` (the requester's principal id while an approved command runs; read by MPR-505, ignored by every existing command).

`yamakan.approval.request`: scope `project:write`, mutation, not human-only, `refusesRequestId: NO_REPLAY`. Input strict: a `z.discriminatedUnion('operation', ...)` with one member per eligible command, each `{ operation: z.literal(name), input: <that command's own schema> }`, plus `reason` (1..500 characters) and `expiresInMinutes` (5..1440, default 60). The start member uses the command's schema without `noUnconsentedPerson`. Returns `{ approvalId, operation, inputHash, state, expiresAt }`. A second identical filing by the same requester while the first is pending and unexpired in the current epoch returns the first. When the stored row is expired or void, the filing sets that row's stored `state` to `withdrawn` in the same transaction and then files a new one, so the unique index never blocks a re-filing; the caps count only unexpired pending rows of the current epoch.

`yamakan.approval.status`: scope `project:read`, read. Input strict `{ approvalId? }`. Returns `{ requests: [...], limits, eligible }` for the caller's own requests only (newest 50 when no id is given); each request is `{ approvalId, operation, inputHash, state, outcome, createdAt, expiresAt, decidedAt, generationId, refusal: { code, message } | null, declineNote }` where `state` is one of `pending`, `expired`, `void`, `approved`, `declined`, `withdrawn` and `outcome` is one of null, `running`, `succeeded`, `refused`, `unknown`.
`yamakan.approval.withdraw`: scope `project:write`, mutation, `NO_REPLAY`, input `{ approvalId }`; the requester's own pending request only.

Human-only, browser principal: `yamakan.approval.list` (scope `agent:revoke`, read; input `{ state?: 'pending' | 'decided', limit? 1..100 }`; returns full rows with the parsed input, the requester id and its token label), `yamakan.approval.approve` (scope `agent:create`, mutation, `NO_REPLAY`; input strict `{ approvalId, inputHash, noUnconsentedPerson?: z.literal(true) }`; returns the request view after the command ran), `yamakan.approval.decline` (scope `agent:revoke`, mutation, `NO_REPLAY`; input `{ approvalId, note? }` with `note` at most 200 characters).

Browser: `src/approvals.ts` (new, pure): `describeRequest(row, catalog)` giving the lines to show, `canApprove(row, now)`, `approveInput(row, attested)`. `src/approvals.tsx` (new): `ApprovalInbox`, shown beside `AgentAccess`, with a pending count on the Agent access entry.

Once MPR-203 has merged, a filed `yamakan.generation.start` input carries that card's `preflightHash`; when the request is approved the command checks it and passes the MPR-204 gates like any other start. Because that hash covers the gate approval ids, a request filed before the person records, renews or revokes a gate approval ends `approved` with `outcome: refused`, and the agent runs the preflight again and files a new request. `APPROVAL_NEVER` also takes `yamakan.gates.approve`, `yamakan.gates.revoke`, `yamakan.gates.list`, `yamakan.agent.setBudget` and the credential commands of MPR-211 when those cards add them.
The inbox shows, above every request, the fixed sentence 'An agent's reason may repeat text from files in this project.'
tasks.sourceDecision: BUILD: no existing module files a pending command for a person; the table lives in the one SQLite authority and execution goes through the unchanged `execute` path. Reusing `yamakan.director.approve` was rejected (it binds a finished stage output, not a command), and a general 'approve any command' was rejected because MPR-303 owns ordinary mutations and consent must stay a person's own act.
sourceReuse: `execute` and `authorize` in `core/command/registry.ts`: the approved command runs through them as `browser-ui`, so its own checks (engine present, recipe known, consent, project state) all still apply.
The digest expression in `execute` (moved into `inputDigest`), `canonicalJson` and `sha256Hex`.

`approveStage` in `core/director/runtime.ts` as the pattern for a hash-and-expiry bound approval written inside `store.transaction`; the epoch value behind `bumpDirectorEpoch` for voiding requests after a restore.
`store.listAgentTokens` for the requester's label and active state; `tests/agent-token-lifecycle.test.ts` as the pattern for a schema-step test.

Parse the input with the target command's schema, store its canonical JSON and `inputDigest`. Enforce the three caps with `LIMIT_EXCEEDED` naming the cap. For a start, run the cheap refusals first (engine present, recipe known) and return the command's own error so nothing is filed that cannot run. In the same transaction delete declined, withdrawn and expired rows older than 30 days, at most 100 per filing; approved rows are kept.

`core/approvals.ts` deciding: `claimApproval` is one conditional `UPDATE ... SET state = 'approved', outcome = 'started' WHERE approval_id = ? AND state = 'pending' AND expires_at > ? AND epoch = ? AND input_hash = ?`; zero rows changed means refuse with the precise reason (`NOT_FOUND`, or `VALIDATION` for already decided, expired, void after a restore, or hash mismatch). Before the claim, re-parse the stored input with the command's current schema and check the requester is still active (an agent token that is revoked or ended makes the request void); either failure refuses and leaves the row pending for the person to decline.

Add the six commands. `yamakan.approval.approve` claims, then calls `execute({ ...ctx, requestId: undefined, onBehalfOf: row.requester }, row.operation, input)` and then `settleApproval` with `succeeded` and the generation id (for a start) or `refused` with the error code and a clipped message. Give its `run` an explicit return type so `typeof commands` does not refer to itself. Its `run` and the others must not contain the word `receipt` (see `tests/request-id-refusal.test.ts`). Attestation: when the stored input has `firstFrameAssetId`, `noUnconsentedPerson: true` is required from the person and is added to the executed input; when it has none, sending it is `VALIDATION`. Store `attested` and `executed_hash` (the digest of what actually ran).

Start-up and crash rule: a row left at `outcome = 'started'` is never run again; `yamakan.approval.status` and `.list` report it as `unknown` with the text that the person should look at the generation list. No timer is added: `expired` and `void` are computed when a row is read.

tasks.title: Add per-agent budget envelopes, enforced at approvals and at the egress and spend gates
tasks.objective: A person gives each agent token an envelope (generations, provider quota seconds, currency, bytes sent off the machine, local job seconds, an end date); the service refuses anything beyond it with `LIMIT_EXCEEDED` and a precise reason, and the agent can read what remains. Anything that spends or leaves the machine is zero until a person sets it.
currentBaseline: An agent token has no budget. `agent_tokens` in `core/store.ts` holds `agent_id`, `token_hash`, `scopes`, `label`, `revoked`, `created_at`, `expires_at`; `yamakan.agent.create` takes `{ label?, scopes, expiresInDays? }` and there is no `yamakan.agent.setBudget` or `yamakan.budget.*` command.

The only per-principal allowance is the private `budgetFor` in `core/store.ts` ('Agents may fill at most half of a workspace budget'): it halves stored-bytes budgets for documents, Studio bitmaps and 3D models. It says nothing about generations, quota, money, egress or time.

Generation is human-only (`yamakan.generation.start` and three more), so today an agent can cause none. After MPR-504 an agent can file requests, limited only by the request caps in `APPROVAL_LIMITS` (how many are pending), not by what they would cost.

`GenerationRecipe` in `core/engines/generation.ts` is `{ id, hash, operation, modelManifestHash }`: no cost, quota or size estimate exists before MPR-203. `GenerationRecord` has `startedAt` but no end time and no measured quota use.
`yamakan.router.explain` accepts `remainingBudgetMinor` (`explainRoutes` in `core/router/explain.ts`): a number the caller states, read from no store.

The `jobs` table records no submitting principal (columns `job_id`, `kind`, `project_id`, `frozen_revision`, `idempotency_key`, `payload`, `state`, `cancel_requested`, `progress`, `error`, `artifact`, `plan_hash`), so local job time cannot be attributed to an agent until MPR-507 adds `submitted_by`.

`CommandError` in `core/command/errors.ts` carries a code and a message only; `LIMIT_EXCEEDED` is not retryable. A refusal's detail therefore lives in its message, and machine-readable amounts need a read command.
interfaces: Storage, in the existing workspace database at the next free `WORKSPACE_SCHEMA_VERSION` at rebase: `agent_budgets` (`agent_id` primary key referencing `agent_tokens`, `generations`, `quota_seconds`, `currency_minor`, `currency_code` nullable, `egress_bytes`, `wall_seconds` nullable, `expires_at` nullable, `set_at`, `set_by`) and `agent_budget_usage` (`agent_id`, `dimension`, `ref_kind` of `approval` or `job`, `ref_id`, `amount`, `state` of `reserved` or `spent`, `at`; primary key on the first four). Old databases gain two empty tables; an agent with no row has no envelope.

Envelope input (strict): `generations` 0..100000, `quotaSeconds` 0..31536000, `currencyMinor` 0..1000000000, `currencyCode` three capital letters and required when `currencyMinor` is above zero, `egressBytes` 0..1099511627776, `wallSeconds` optional 0..31536000, `expiresInDays` optional 1..366. The four dimensions that spend or leave the machine are required integers and there is no value meaning unlimited. `wallSeconds` absent means local jobs are not limited by this envelope, which is today's behaviour.

`yamakan.agent.setBudget`: scope `agent:create`, mutation, human-only, `refusesRequestId: NO_REPLAY`; input `{ agentId, budget }`. It replaces the limits and keeps the usage; a limit below what is used is allowed and refuses further use. `yamakan.agent.create` gains optional `budget` of the same shape, written in the same transaction as the token. `yamakan.agent.list` rows gain `budget` and `used`. Neither command is approval-eligible (both go in `APPROVAL_NEVER` of MPR-504).

`yamakan.budget.read`: scope `project:read`, read; input strict `{ agentId? }`. An agent reads only its own envelope; another agent's id answers `NOT_FOUND`; only `browser-ui` may name any agent. Output `{ format: 'yamakan.agent-budget', formatVersion: 1, agentId, set, expiresAt, expired, currencyCode, dimensions }` where each of `generations`, `quotaSeconds`, `currencyMinor`, `egressBytes`, `wallSeconds` is `{ limit, spent, reserved, remaining }` (`limit` and `remaining` null for an unlimited `wallSeconds`). For `local-client` and `browser-ui` without an id the answer is `{ set: false, applies: false }`.

`core/agents/budget.ts` (new): `setBudget`, `readBudget`, `reserveForApproval(db, { agentId, approvalId, amounts }, now)`, `recheckAtClaim`, `commitAtGate(db, { agentId, approvalId, dimension })`, `releaseForApproval`, `assertJobAllowed(db, agentId, now)`, `debitJob(db, { agentId, jobId, seconds })`. Every refusal is `LIMIT_EXCEEDED` with the fixed form 'Agent budget: <dimension> limit <n>, spent <n>, reserved <n>, needed <n>.' or 'Agent budget: none set.' or 'Agent budget: ended.'; no path, prompt or account name.
`CommandContext.approvalId?: string`, set by `yamakan.approval.approve` beside `onBehalfOf` from MPR-504, so a gate can find the reservation it commits.

What counts as used: `spent` rows, plus `reserved` rows whose approval request is pending and unexpired in the current epoch, or approved with outcome `started`. Nothing is released by a timer; a declined, withdrawn, expired or void request simply stops counting.
tasks.sourceDecision: BUILD: no per-agent budget exists; two small tables in the one SQLite authority and checks at four existing choke points. Reusing `budgetFor` was rejected (it is a fixed half-share of storage, not a person's envelope), and storing the envelope inside the token's `scopes` JSON was rejected because usage must be a ledger and scopes are checked by a ceiling.
sourceReuse: `claimApproval`, `fileApproval` and `settleApproval` in `core/approvals.ts` (added by MPR-504): the reserve, re-check and release calls run inside their transactions.

The estimate and egress disclosure behind `preflightHash` from MPR-203, and the gate functions of MPR-204. Their exact signatures are not verified here (those cards are written by another track); step 0 reads them on live main.
`store.createAgentToken`, `store.listAgentTokens` and the `expires_at` handling in `core/store.ts`; `tests/agent-token-lifecycle.test.ts` as the pattern for the schema-step test.
`jobs.submitted_by` from MPR-507 and the terminal-state path `#finish` in `core/jobs.ts` for local job seconds.
`src/agent-access.ts` and `src/agent-access.tsx` for the person's controls; no third-party code.
implementationSequence: Verify live main and reproduce the gap: create an agent token, file approval requests up to the pending cap and confirm nothing limits their cost; call `yamakan.budget.read` (unknown operation). Read what MPR-203 and MPR-204 actually merged: how an estimate is fetched for a `preflightHash`, and what the gate functions take. If either is missing, do part a only and record part b as BLOCKED on that interface. If budgets exist, record ALREADY_SATISFIED with evidence.

Registry: add `yamakan.agent.setBudget` and `yamakan.budget.read`, the optional `budget` on `yamakan.agent.create`, and the `budget` and `used` fields on `yamakan.agent.list`. Add `yamakan.agent.setBudget` to `APPROVAL_NEVER` and to `validInput` in `tests/request-id-refusal.test.ts`.

Enforcement point 1, filing: `fileApproval` calls `reserveForApproval` for a `yamakan.generation.start` request by an `agent:` principal: one generation, and (part b) the estimate's quota seconds, currency and egress bytes. No envelope, an ended envelope or too little left refuses the filing; nothing is stored.

Enforcement point 2, approval: `recheckAtClaim` runs in the same transaction as `claimApproval`; a limit lowered since filing refuses the approval and leaves the request pending. On `settleApproval`: `succeeded` turns the generation reservation into `spent`; `refused` releases what no gate committed.

Part b (needs MPR-203, MPR-204 and MPR-507). Enforcement point 3, the gates: pass `onBehalfOf` and `approvalId` from the `run` of `yamakan.generation.start` into `createGenerationService().start` as fields outside the command input, and from there to the MPR-204 egress and spend gates, which call `commitAtGate` before any connection is opened. A missing estimate for a dimension counts as exceeding it. A currency other than the envelope's is refused; there is no conversion.

Enforcement point 4, local job seconds: where a job is submitted with `submitted_by` an `agent:` id, `assertJobAllowed` refuses when `wallSeconds` is set and already used up, or when `wallSeconds` is set and the same agent already has a job that is not terminal, so the overshoot stays at one submission (one batch for `yamakan.export.batch`), because admission in `core/jobs.ts` has no per-agent limit of its own; at the terminal state `debitJob` writes the wall time this card measures in `core/jobs.ts` around each attempt, summed and rounded up (the `attempts` table stores no times today). Proxy builds are not jobs and are not counted.

Browser: in `src/agent-access.tsx` add the envelope fields to token creation (all zero by default, with the sentence that this agent cannot ask for generations until a limit is set), an edit control, and spent, reserved and remaining per agent; in the inbox added by MPR-504 show what the request would use and what would remain. Strings in `src/i18n.ts`.

Tests (see testPlan). Docs: `docs/SECURITY.md` (what is and is not budgeted, `local-client` is not), `docs/COST_ROUTER.md` (the stored envelope against the caller-stated `remainingBudgetMinor`), `docs/AGENT_PLATFORM.md`, `docs/PROJECT_DATA_MODEL.md`.
Extend `scripts/qualify-approvals.mjs` (added by MPR-504) with the budget journey; run on the Windows host and commit the receipt.
acceptance: An agent with no envelope cannot file a generation request: `LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, 'Agent budget: none set.'
With `generations: 2`, two filings succeed and the third is refused naming limit 2, reserved 2, needed 1; declining one makes one filing possible again without any other step.
`yamakan.budget.read` shows the same numbers the refusals name, before and after a service restart.
Lowering a limit below what is reserved refuses the next approval at the claim and runs nothing.

With part b: a start whose estimate exceeds remaining quota seconds, currency or egress bytes is refused at filing; if the envelope shrinks afterwards, the gate refuses before any connection, and the stand-in engine records no push.
With `wallSeconds` set and used up, the agent's next export or render is refused at submission; with it absent, the agent's local jobs behave exactly as before this card.

An agent cannot read another agent's envelope and cannot call `yamakan.agent.setBudget`; a database from before this card opens with no envelopes and every existing token still works for everything it could do before.
testPlan: New `tests/agent-budget.test.ts`: set, read, reserve, re-check, commit, release and debit against a temporary workspace with an injected clock; envelope expiry and the token's own end; every refusal text; usage after restart.

Extend `tests/command.test.ts`, `tests/parity.test.ts`, `tests/request-id-refusal.test.ts` and `tests/agent-access.test.ts` (the pure half of the panel: defaults all zero, remaining shown, no unlimited choice).
`npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check`.
negativeTests: `yamakan.agent.setBudget` called by an agent or by `local-client` is `SCOPE_DENIED`; filing it as an approval request is refused as never eligible.
An agent passing another agent's id to `yamakan.budget.read` gets `NOT_FOUND`, the same answer as for an id that does not exist.
Envelope input with a negative number, a fraction, `currencyMinor` above zero without `currencyCode`, an unknown property or a value above the bound is `VALIDATION`.
Two filings sent together when one generation remains: exactly one is accepted.
A request reserved before a restore does not count after it (the request is void), and a spent row is never removed by decline, expiry or restore.
A refusal message contains only the dimension name and integers: a test asserts no prompt text, path, label or account name appears.

With `wallSeconds` used up, an agent's `yamakan.job.rerun` of a failed job is refused with `LIMIT_EXCEEDED` and inserts no row; the check sits in the supervisor's insert path in `core/jobs.ts`, so every submission route passes it.

An agent with 60 seconds of `wallSeconds` left submits three renders together: the first is admitted and the second and third are refused with `LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, because the agent already has a job that is not terminal.

With part b, one request is refused at the gate with the stand-in Kaggle CLI recording no push.

performanceCriteria: A budget check is one indexed read of one agent's rows inside the transaction that already runs; with 10000 seeded usage rows for one agent the check adds under 5 ms median in `tests/agent-budget.test.ts` on the reference host (measured and recorded in the receipt).
No timer, sweep or background task is added; a job writes at most one usage row and an approval at most four.
compatibilityRequirements: Schema: the workspace database moves one version; old databases gain two empty tables; tokens, scopes and receipts are unchanged. The agent scope ceiling (`assertAgentScopeCeiling`, defined in `core/command/registry.ts` and used by `core/agents.ts`) and the human-only rule are untouched.

Behaviour change, intended: once this card lands, an agent without an envelope can no longer file generation requests that MPR-504 alone accepted. Local renders and exports by agents are unchanged unless a person sets `wallSeconds`.
A person's own generation from the browser carries no `onBehalfOf` and is never checked against any agent envelope. `local-client` has no envelope.

Boundary with MPR-301: that card's envelope belongs to a pipeline at shot-list approval; this one belongs to a token. When both apply both must pass. Boundary with MPR-204: the gates and their approvals are that card's; this card only adds a refusal inside them. Boundary with MPR-207: a retry is a new request and reserves again. `RESOURCE_POLICY` is not edited.

Nothing can debit the currency dimension in this build: no priced route exists and the gates of MPR-204 have no currency column. The envelope stores the limit so that no further schema step is needed later; it becomes live only with MPR-222, after FD-5.
definitionOfDone: The four command changes exist with the scopes and inputs above and are covered by the registry tests.

The agent panel shows and edits envelopes, with zero defaults and no unlimited choice.

The interfaces of MPR-203 and MPR-204 are not verified, so part b starts by reading them.
`core/command/registry.ts` changes often: rebase on live main and keep the additions append-only; the schema version is taken at rebase.

Debits use the estimate, not a measurement: `GenerationRecord` has no end time or measured quota use, so real Kaggle quota use may differ from what is booked. Nothing is refunded automatically. The alternative, reconciling from a measured value, waits for MPR-101 to record one.

Local job seconds are checked before a job and debited after it, so the envelope can be overshot by one job, and an attempt cut off by a crash may be under-counted. A reset of usage is not offered: to start again a person makes a new token. Both are stated in the docs.

tasks.title: Add an append-only audit feed of mutation calls and a provenance trace read command
tasks.objective: A person can see which principal called which mutation command, when, with what outcome and whether it carried a request id; and for an asset, a take or an export job one read command returns the chain export, revision, clip, take, generation record, inputs. Both outputs hold ids and hashes only: no prompt text, no path, no token label, no account name.
currentBaseline: No audit or trace command exists: the registry has no `yamakan.audit.*` or `yamakan.provenance.*` operation. `yamakan.lineage.evaluate` is unrelated and its name must not be reused: it is a stateless check of reviewer independence over descriptors the caller supplies (`evaluateReviewIndependenceV1`) and reads no project data.

`execute` in `core/command/registry.ts` is the one path every command takes (`resolveOperation`, `authorize`, input parse, `run`). It records nothing about a call unless the caller sent a request id; then `command_receipts` keeps `principal_id`, `project_id`, `request_id`, `request_digest` and `committed_revision`.

`revisions` in `core/store.ts` holds `operation` and an optional `receipt_id` but no principal; `outbox` holds `event_id`, `project_id`, `revision`, `operation` and is read by `store.events(afterEventId, limit)`. The `Commit` type carries a principal only inside `receipt` or as `editStepAuthor`, so a commit made without a request id cannot be attributed afterwards.

`edit_history.author` names a principal only for steps of an undo history, and `core/store.ts` deletes those rows (two `DELETE FROM edit_history` statements). `outbox` and `revisions` are never updated or deleted by code under `core/`.

Calls that write no project revision leave no ordered record: token creation and revocation, consent grant and revocation (their tables keep `grantor_principal_id` and `principal_id`, but no feed reads them), generation start, job submission and cancel. The `jobs` table names no principal.

Lineage exists in pieces and no command walks it: a take's `lineage` (`TakeLineageSchema` in `core/story.ts`: `outputHash`, `inputs`, optional `continuity` references by document id and hash); `GenerationLineage` in `core/engines/generation.ts` (`outputHash`, `inputs`, `recipeId`, `recipeHash`, `modelManifestHash`, `seed`, `promptHash`); a derivative asset's link to its original (`core/jobs.ts`); an export job's `frozen_revision` and `plan_hash`.

Generation records are kept as `remote-generation` rows of the `jobs` table (`generationLedger` in `core/jobs.ts`). A `GenerationRecord` holds the prompt text and names no principal. `promptHash` is unsalted, as the comment beside `GenerationLineage` says.
`yamakan.events.read` (MPR-502) reports revision events with no principal, by design, and points to this card for attribution.
interfaces: Storage, in the existing workspace database at the next free `WORKSPACE_SCHEMA_VERSION` at rebase (18 at the planning head): table `audit_log` (`audit_id` integer primary key autoincrement, `at` integer milliseconds, `epoch`, `phase` of `began`, `ended` or `denied`, `began_id` nullable, `principal_id`, `on_behalf_of` nullable, `approval_id` nullable, `operation`, `project_id` nullable, `input_hash` nullable (null on a `denied` row, because `authorize` runs before the input is parsed), `request_id_hash` nullable, `outcome` nullable (`ok` or one of `ErrorCodes`), `revision` nullable, `capped` 0 or 1), STRICT, with an index on (`principal_id`, `audit_id`) and two triggers that abort any UPDATE or DELETE. Old databases gain an empty table; nothing before the upgrade is reconstructed.

`core/audit.ts` (new): `AUDIT_LIMITS = { page: 200, defaultPage: 100, deniedPerPrincipalPerHour: 100 }`, `appendAudit(db, row)`, `readAudit(db, { viewer, after, limit, projectId, principalId })`. `input_hash` is the digest `execute` already computes for receipts (`sha256Hex(canonicalJson({ apiVersion, format, operation, input }))`; MPR-504 exports it as `inputDigest`, reuse that if merged). `request_id_hash` is the SHA-256 of the caller's request id; the request id itself is not stored, because it is caller-chosen text.

Writer: `execute` only. For a command with `mutation: true`: a `denied` row when `authorize` refuses an authenticated principal (at most `deniedPerPrincipalPerHour`; the last one stored in an hour has `capped: 1`); a `began` row after the input parses and before `run`; an `ended` row with `began_id` and `outcome`. `revision` is the integer `revision` of the command's own result when it has one (not verified for every mutation; the test lists the commands that return none). `on_behalf_of` and `approval_id` are copied from the command context when MPR-504 and MPR-505 are merged, otherwise null. Read commands are not recorded.

`yamakan.audit.read`: scope `project:read`, read, not human-only. Input strict `{ after?: integer 0.., epoch?: integer 0.., limit?: 1..200, projectId?: Id, principalId?: string of at most 64 characters }`. `browser-ui` sees every row and may filter by `principalId`; every other principal sees only rows where it is `principal_id` or `on_behalf_of`, and naming another principal answers `NOT_FOUND`. Output `{ format: 'yamakan.audit', formatVersion: 1, epoch, reset, entries: [{ auditId, at, phase, beganId, principalId, onBehalfOf, approvalId, operation, projectId, inputHash, requestIdHash, outcome, revision, capped }], next, more }`. Cursor and epoch follow the rule of `yamakan.events.read` (MPR-502): a cursor from another epoch answers `reset: true` from the start.

`yamakan.provenance.trace`: scope `project:read`, read. Input strict `{ projectId: Id, subject }` where `subject` is a discriminated union on `kind`: `{ kind: 'asset', assetId }`, `{ kind: 'take', shotId, takeId }`, `{ kind: 'job', jobId }`. Output `{ format: 'yamakan.provenance-trace', formatVersion: 1, projectId, subject, nodes, edges, gaps, truncated }`. Node kinds and their only fields: `job` (`jobId`, `jobKind`, `state`, `frozenRevision`, `planHash`), `revision` (`revision`, `snapshotHash`, `operation`, `principalId` or null, `receipt` true or false), `asset` (`assetId`, `hash`), `take` (`shotId`, `takeId`, `outputHash`), `generation` (`generationId`, `recipeId`, `recipeHash`, `modelManifestHash`, `seed`, `promptHash`, `operation`, `attestedNoUnconsentedPerson`), `continuity` (`packDocumentId`, `packContentHash`, `entryId`), `consent` (`consentId`, `state`). Edges are `{ from, to, kind }` with `kind` of `rendered-from`, `uses`, `derived-from`, `generated-by` or `input-of`.

`core/provenance-trace.ts` (new): `traceProvenance(store, { projectId, subject })` with `TRACE_LIMITS = { nodes: 500, depth: 8 }`; a visited set stops cycles; hitting a limit sets `truncated: true`. Every link that cannot be resolved from stored data is one entry in `gaps` as `{ at, reason }` with `reason` from a closed list (`no-lineage-recorded`, `generation-record-missing`, `revision-author-not-recorded`, `consent-link-not-recorded`, `artifact-hash-not-recorded`, `asset-missing`). Nothing is inferred. There is one lineage resolver: MPR-701 calls this function for its manifest when this card has merged; if MPR-701 merged first, this card moves that card's resolver here and both use it.

tasks.title: Put the Blender worker in the memory budget, queue its jobs fairly, add rerun from failed
tasks.objective: A second Blender job waits in a bounded, fair queue (at most 4 waiting) and reports its position instead of being refused; a failed local job can be run again on request as a new linked job; and the Blender worker's memory limit is measured and brought inside the frozen worst-case budget, or the card stops and reports.
currentBaseline: `submitBlenderRender` and `submitBlenderTrack` in `core/jobs.ts` refuse when any `blender-render` or `blender-track` row is not terminal (`BLENDER_RENDERS_AT_ONCE = 1`): `LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, 'A Blender render is already running; wait for it or cancel it.' and 'Blender is already working; wait for it or cancel it.' Nothing waits. `docs/SECURITY.md` records the result as a known limit: an agent with `render:execute` can keep the one slot busy until someone with `job:control` cancels.

The refusal is asserted in `tests/blender-render.test.ts` ('a second render while one runs is refused, and a cancelled one leaves nothing') and in `scripts/qualify-cinema-blender.mjs` (the page element `cinema-blender-problem` in `src/cinema/BlenderRender.tsx` must match 'already running').

One serial pump runs every job kind. `#claim` in `core/jobs.ts` takes `SELECT * FROM jobs WHERE state = 'queued' ORDER BY rowid LIMIT 1`: first in, first out across all kinds and principals. `RESOURCE_POLICY.enforced.activeJobs` (128) caps active rows.

The `jobs` table has no submitting principal and no link between jobs; the `submit*` methods take no principal. Its `UNIQUE(project_id, kind, frozen_revision, idempotency_key)` constraint means a second row for the same work needs a different key.

`failed` is terminal (`YAMAKAN_LEGAL_TRANSITIONS` in `core/jobs/rules/yamakan-transitions.ts`). `yamakan.job.retry` (scope `job:control`, `refusesRequestId: NO_REPLAY`) only re-queues a job in `reconciliationRequired`; no command runs a failed job again.

Proxies are not jobs. `core/media/proxies.ts` remembers a failed build in memory for `PASSING_FAILURE_MS` (60 s) or `SETTLED_FAILURE_MS` (10 min); `yamakan.proxy.build` (scope `render:execute`, input `{ projectId, assetId }`) has no way to ask again sooner. Its waiting list is bounded by `QUEUE_DEPTH = 4` and answers `BUSY`.

Memory, read from code and not measured: both Blender spawn sites in `core/jobs.ts` pass `profile: ENGINE_WORKER_PROFILE, memoryBytes: ENGINE_WORKER_PROFILE.memoryBytes`, and `ENGINE_WORKER_PROFILE` in `core/process/owner.ts` sets 4 GiB. The test 'the frozen qualification rule sits inside the enforced limits' in `tests/resource-policy.test.ts` counts the service (300 MiB), two workers at `renderMemoryBytes` (2 GiB) and three at `workerMemoryBytes` (1 GiB): 7,468 MiB against 8,192 MiB. With the Blender limit in the job worker's place the sum is 9,516 MiB.

The policy text in `core/command/policy.ts` says a worker's limit must be `workerMemoryBytes` or `renderMemoryBytes` and its measured peak at most `workerPeakShareOfLimit` (0.875) of that limit. The 4 GiB Blender limit is neither. procd reports a worker's peak (`peakMemoryBytes`, tested in `tests/resource-policy.test.ts`).
interfaces: Memory: `JOB_WORKER_MEMORY_BYTES` exported from `core/jobs.ts`, a frozen map from job kind to the limit its worker runs under, used at every spawn site. The Blender entries hold the limit chosen in step 2. `ENGINE_WORKER_PROFILE`, `RESOURCE_POLICY` and `core/qualification-policy.ts` are not edited; the owner already takes the smaller of the profile's limit and the `memoryBytes` option.

Storage, at the next free `WORKSPACE_SCHEMA_VERSION` at rebase (18 at the planning head): `jobs.submitted_by` (text, nullable, 1 to 64 characters) and `jobs.retry_of` (text, nullable, a `job_id`), with a partial index on `retry_of`. Old rows keep null: no known submitter, not a rerun. Both columns and the index land in one schema step in part b; part c adds none. In the order rule and the per-principal limit, null counts as one shared principal.

`BLENDER_QUEUE = { waiting: 4, waitingPerPrincipal: 2, rerunsPerChain: 3 }` in `core/jobs.ts`. Waiting means state `queued`; a job counts as waiting until the pump claims it. Admission for a Blender kind, checked before the insert: 4 Blender rows already waiting answers `BUSY` 'The Blender queue is full (4 waiting); wait or cancel one.'; 2 already waiting from the same `submitted_by` answers `BUSY` 'You already have 2 Blender jobs waiting.' One Blender job at a time stays true because the pump is serial.

Order: `#claim` still takes the oldest queued row. When that row is a Blender kind, it takes instead the queued Blender row whose submitter least recently had a Blender job leave `queued` (never comes first; ties by `rowid`). Other kinds keep their place. The order is computed from stored rows, so it is the same after a restart.

`submit`, `submitBatch`, `submitBlenderRender`, `submitBlenderTrack` and `submitDerivative` gain an optional last argument `submittedBy`; registry callers pass the principal id of the command context, and the upload route in `server/main.ts` (the only caller of `submitDerivative`) passes the id of the principal it authorised. The job view from `#view` gains `queuePosition` (1-based place in claim order while `queued`, else null) and `retryOf` (job id or null). The submitter's id is not put in the view; attribution is MPR-506.

`yamakan.job.rerun`: scope `render:execute`, mutation, not human-only, `refusesRequestId: NO_REPLAY` (as `yamakan.job.retry`); input strict `{ jobId: Id }`. Only for a job in `failed` of kind export, Blender render or Blender track. A failed frame-rate conversion is `VALIDATION`, because its staged original is released when it fails (the file is imported again). It inserts a new `queued` row with the same kind, project, frozen revision, payload and plan hash, `retry_of` set to the failed job, `submitted_by` the caller, and an idempotency key derived from the failed job's id and the rerun's number in its chain, so a second rerun of the same failed job does not collide with the first (the constraint above forbids reusing a key). It passes the same admission checks as a new submission. If a rerun of that job is already not terminal, that job is returned. A fourth rerun in one chain is `LIMIT_EXCEEDED`. A `remote-generation` job is `VALIDATION` (a generation is retried through MPR-207).

`yamakan.proxy.build` gains optional `retry: true` (a literal). It forgets a remembered failure whose state is `failed` and queues the build again under the existing `QUEUE_DEPTH`; a remembered `unsupported` answer is kept.
tasks.sourceDecision: ADAPT: the queue is the existing `jobs` table and the existing serial pump with a relaxed admission check and one ordering rule; no new scheduler, store or state. A rerun is a new row because `failed` is terminal in the closed state machine; adding a `failed` to `queued` transition was rejected (it would rewrite a finished job's attempts and break the terminal rule the recovery tests rely on).

tasks.title: Decide and deliver operating-system user presence for human-only commands (Q15)
tasks.objective: Either a human-only command runs only after the person at the PC confirms with Windows Hello or their PIN (option A, a small native helper), or the recorded fallback is kept and every agent-containment claim is limited to what the fallback supports (option B). The founder chooses under FD-9; until then nothing is built and no Q15 pass is claimed.
currentBaseline: `authorize` in `core/command/registry.ts` refuses a `humanOnly` command unless `principal.id` is `browser-ui` (`SCOPE_DENIED`, 'This command requires the browser session.'). 13 commands are human-only at the planning head. Nothing asks the operating system whether a person is present.

The browser session comes from a single-use launch secret that the page exchanges for a session cookie (`server/main.ts`; tested in `tests/agent-principals.test.ts` and `tests/http.test.ts`). The receipt gives the secret a 60 s life.
`docs/evidence/qualification/q15-user-presence.json` records `outcome` `fallback` with `bindingFailApplied: true` and an empty `probes` list, at commit `09539bf5243b8fcdbf800a1275af5c3af1940462`.
`scripts/qualify-q15-user-presence.ts` (`npm run qualify:q15`) runs no probe: it writes `fallback` on every host, refuses a dirty tree, and writes the receipt file directly.

`docs/SECURITY.md` ('Until Q15 OS user presence is wired into each human-only command, these hold') says an agent run as the user, with the workspace token or file access, is trusted as the user, and that containment needs a separate Windows account or an AppContainer.

`docs/evidence/qualification/q15-user-presence-assessment.md` prefers `Windows.Security.Credentials.UI.UserConsentVerifier`, keeps `native/procd` free of dependencies, suggests a separate helper such as `native/presence/`, and notes that an interactive prompt cannot run in headless CI. Nobody has run such a helper.
`docs/FOUNDER_DECISION_RECORD.md` holds no FD-9 decision at the planning head; it only names Q15 as still on the fallback. No `native/presence` directory, `core/presence.ts` or presence test exists.
interfaces: Option B (keep the fallback): no code interface. `docs/SECURITY.md` and the Agent access panel state in one plain sentence that human-only commands are bound to the browser session and not to a person, and that an agent running as the same Windows account is trusted as the user. `npm run qualify:q15` is re-run on the head and still writes `fallback`.

Option A, helper: a new crate `native/presence/` building `yamakan-presence.exe`, separate from `native/procd`. Arguments are one of two fixed words, `check` or `request`, plus a reason id from a closed list (`human-only-command`); no caller text ever reaches it. It calls `UserConsentVerifier` and exits 0 verified, 1 cancelled or not verified, 2 not available on this device, 3 error. The prompt wording is fixed in the helper. That a desktop process must use the window-handle form of the call is [ASSUMED] from the assessment and not verified.

Option A, `core/presence.ts` (new): `PresenceProvider { availability(), request(reasonId) }`, `createPresenceGate({ provider, clock })`, `PRESENCE = { windowSeconds: 120, promptSeconds: 60, cancelledPerMinute: 3 }`. Mode is decided once at service start: `enforced` when the helper is present and `check` exits 0, else `fallback`. `YAMAKAN_PRESENCE=fallback` at service start forces `fallback` by name (needed by automated qualification scripts); the mode is always shown.

Option A, gate: in `execute`, for a `humanOnly` command and only after `authorize` has accepted the `browser-ui` principal. With mode `enforced` and no confirmation for this browser session inside `windowSeconds`, the helper is started and awaited; exit 0 records the confirmation in memory for that session; anything else refuses with `SCOPE_DENIED` 'Confirm with Windows Hello or your PIN to run this command.' A helper that is missing, fails or exceeds `promptSeconds` refuses with `UNAVAILABLE`; it never counts as verified. One prompt at a time; after three cancelled prompts in a minute the answer is `BUSY` with no new prompt. The command context gains `sessionId?: string`, set by `server/api.ts` for the browser session (not verified that one is carried today).

Option A, `yamakan.presence.status`: scope `project:read`, read, input strict `{}`. Output `{ format: 'yamakan.presence', formatVersion: 1, mode: 'enforced' | 'fallback', reason }` with `reason` from a closed list (`helper-missing`, `not-available-on-device`, `forced-fallback`, `not-windows`, `ok`). No device or account detail.

The Q15 receipt keeps its id `yamakan.qualification/q15-user-presence/1` if only `probes` is filled and `outcome` changes; if a field is added the id moves to `/2` and the docs say so. `outcome` may be `pass` only from an interactive run on Windows with a person confirming once and cancelling once.
tasks.sourceDecision: DEFER: blocked on FD-9. If the founder chooses option A the work is BUILD (a small helper and one gate; no existing code does this) with WRAP of the Windows API through the `windows` crate; if option B it is a documentation and receipt change only.

tasks.title: Wire ripple delete, ripple trim, insert and group move into the timeline UI
tasks.objective: A person can ripple delete, ripple trim, insert at the playhead and move a group of clips in the Edit timeline by keyboard and by pointer; each action is stored as one typed `timeline.*` operation in one `yamakan.project.applyBatch` revision, so one Undo reverses it, and every refusal is shown with the reducer's reason. This extends the existing `Timeline` component and the existing commit path in `src/main.tsx`; no editing engine, command or store is added.
currentBaseline: `core/command/registry.ts` defines `yamakan.timeline.rippleDelete`, `yamakan.timeline.rippleTrim`, `yamakan.timeline.insert` and `yamakan.timeline.groupMove` (scope `project:write`, mutation, receipt kept). The same four operation types are in `OperationSchema` in `core/timeline/operations.ts`, so `yamakan.project.applyBatch` (`BatchSchema`, 1 to 64 operations) accepts them. Reducer tests: `tests/ripple.test.ts`, `tests/group-move.test.ts`.

No file under `src/` calls any of the four commands or sends a `timeline.*` operation. `src/edit-ops.ts` exports `rippleDeleteClip` and `groupMoveClips`, which apply the reducer operation to the local view, but the UI never calls them; there is no helper for `timeline.rippleTrim` or `timeline.insert`. `groupMoveClips` catches and discards the reducer's refusal.

`src/main.tsx` `editPanel` renders `<Timeline>` (`src/editor/components/Timeline.tsx`) with `trimMode='normal'` fixed and without `onRippleDeleteClip`, `onTrimModeChange`, `rangeIn` or `rangeOut`. The component's context menu offers 'Ripple delete' only when `onRippleDeleteClip` is passed, so the item never appears. Whether the 'Trim mode' control renders without `onTrimModeChange` is not verified.
Selection is one clip (`selectedClipId: string | null` in `TimelineProps`, `selected` in `src/main.tsx`). `timeline.groupMove` takes 1 to 64 clip ids.

The timeline key handler matches Ctrl/Cmd+C/X/V/D by the typed character (`event.key`, lower-cased, so these four depend on the keyboard layout) and ArrowUp/ArrowDown by `event.key`; the rest use physical `event.code`: `KeyN` (snapping), Shift+ArrowLeft/Right (trim end one frame), Alt+ArrowLeft/Right (move one frame), `Comma`/`Period` (trim start one frame), `BracketLeft`/`BracketRight` (trim to playhead), ArrowUp/ArrowDown (previous/next edit point). Tooltips advertise `C`, `V/R/O/Y/U`, `Del` and `Shift+Del`, which have no handler; no Delete or Backspace handler exists in `src/` outside the Studio canvas engine. The clip context menu opens by right-click only.

`operationsBetween` in `src/edit-diff.ts` turns a local edit into typed operations but never emits a `timeline.*` operation and returns null above `MAX_GESTURE_OPERATIONS` (64); `commitOnce` in `src/main.tsx` then shows `status.draftNeedsSave` and only a snapshot save can store the edit. A ripple made as a plain local edit would be stored as one `clip.remove` plus one `clip.move` per shifted clip, and one that shifts more than 63 clips could not be stored as typed operations at all.

Ripple in the reducer is per track: `computeRippleAdjustments` (`core/timeline/ripple/diff.ts`) builds adjustments per track id from intervals vacated on that track, and `rippleCloseGaps` (`core/timeline/operations.ts`) drops adjustments on locked tracks. `collectTrackIntervals` records a vacated interval only when a clip disappears or its end moves earlier, and `tests/ripple.test.ts` covers ripple trim with `endTicks` only; what `timeline.rippleTrim` does for a start-only trim or an end extension is not verified. `timeline.insert` shifts clips whose start is at or after `startTicks` on the target track only, then adds the clip; an insert whose `startTicks` falls inside a clip is expected to be refused as an overlap (not verified).

`scripts/qualify-edit-equivalence.mjs` (`npm run qualify:edit-equivalence`, SS-014) drives normal trim, move and snap by pointer and by keyboard at two frame rates with undo, redo, reopen, focus-away commit and a locked-track refusal. It drives no `timeline.*` operation, and its JSON receipt is not committed; the written result is `docs/evidence/ultimate/SS-014-edit-equivalence.md`. Undo and Redo are toolbar buttons in `topBar` (`action.undo`, `action.redo`); a Ctrl+Z binding was not found in `src/main.tsx` (elsewhere not verified).
interfaces: No new command, scope, schema or project format. Used unchanged: `yamakan.project.applyBatch` (`project:write`, mutation, receipt kept under the request id `commitOnce` already sends, strict bounded path-free input) carrying `timeline.rippleDelete`, `timeline.rippleTrim`, `timeline.insert`, `timeline.groupMove` and, for an insert inside a clip, `clip.split`; `yamakan.project.undo` and `yamakan.project.redo`.

`src/edit-diff.ts` additions: `type EditIntent = { from: Project; to: Project; operations: Operation[] }`; `intentOperations(intent: EditIntent | null, base: Project, draft: Project): Operation[] | null` returns `intent.operations` only when `intent.from` equals `base` and `intent.to` equals `draft` under the module's existing `exact()` comparison, the list has at most 64 operations, and `applyBatch(fromEditView(base), operations)` reproduces `fromEditView(draft)` exactly; `changedIds(from: Project, to: Project): Set<string>` returns the id of every clip, track and scene that is added, removed or different between the two.

`src/edit-ops.ts` additions (pure, no swallowed errors): `rippleDeleteOps(p, clipId)`, `rippleTrimOps(p, clipId, edge: 'start' | 'end', ticks)`, `insertOps(p, { assetId, trackId, startTicks, durationTicks, sourceStartTicks, clipId, splitClipId })` (returns `clip.split` then `timeline.insert` when `startTicks` is strictly inside a clip on the track, else `timeline.insert` alone), `groupMoveOps(p, { anchorClipId, clipIds, anchorStartTicks, targetTrackId, snapTicks?, playheadTicks? })`, each returning `Operation[]`; `refusalText(e: unknown): string` strips the `Operation N (type): ` prefix that `applyBatch` adds. `rippleDeleteClip` and `groupMoveClips` keep their names if a test imports them and are rebuilt on these builders.
`src/main.tsx`: `editIntent(build: (p: Project) => Operation[]): Promise<void>` beside `edit`; state `trimMode: 'normal' | 'ripple'` and `selectedIds: string[]` beside `selected`.

`TimelineProps` additions, all optional: `selectedClipIds?: string[]`, `onSelectClips?(ids: string[], primaryId: string | null)`, `onRippleTrimClip?(clipId: string, edge: 'start' | 'end', time: number)`, `onGroupMove?(move: { anchorClipId: string; clipIds: string[]; anchorStart: number; targetTrackId: string })`, a fourth argument on `onDropMedia?(mediaId, trackId, time, mode?: 'place' | 'insert')`, `labels?: Partial<Record<string, string>>` for translated text. `onRippleDeleteClip`, `onTrimModeChange` and a non-fixed `trimMode` are passed for the first time.

Key map added (physical `event.code`, ignored when the event target is an input, select, textarea or contenteditable, and, apart from the two asset-button keys, acting only when focus is inside the timeline root as the existing editing keys do, because the timeline stays mounted while other workspaces and the Studio panel are shown): `Delete`/`Backspace` remove leaving a gap; `Shift+Delete`/`Shift+Backspace` ripple delete; `KeyV` normal trim mode; `KeyR` ripple trim mode; `Shift+BracketLeft`/`Shift+BracketRight` ripple trim start/end to the playhead; `Shift+KeyI` and `Insert` on a focused asset button insert at the playhead; `Ctrl/Cmd+KeyA` select all (at most 64); `Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+ArrowLeft/Right` extend the selection; `Alt+ArrowUp/Down` move the selection to the previous/next track of the same kind; `Shift+F10` and `ContextMenu` open the clip menu. No existing binding changes meaning.

New message keys in `src/i18n.ts`, English and Arabic: labels for ripple delete, the two trim modes, insert at playhead, select all, the selection count, `timeline.refused` with a `{reason}` placeholder, `timeline.selection.tooMany` with `{max}`, `timeline.insert.noTrack`, and a note that a ripple moves later clips on the clip's own track only. Key names may follow the file's existing prefixes.
tasks.sourceDecision: ADAPT — the reducer operations, their commands and the donor-derived `Timeline` component exist and are tested; this card connects them through one typed intent path in the existing commit code, and nothing new is imported; because `src/editor/components/Timeline.tsx` and `src/editor/editor.css` are ledgered imports, each edit to them updates `importedSha256` and `modifications` in `docs/provenance/imports.json`. Rejected: calling the timeline commands directly from the UI (a second write path beside `commitOnce` and the local history) and letting `operationsBetween` describe a ripple (stores N moves instead of the typed operation and fails above 64).
