tasks.title: Add speed, LUT and sound unlink/relink to the clip inspector; state loudness honestly
tasks.objective: The existing clip inspector in the Edit workspace lets a person set a clip's speed, import and apply or remove a `.cube` LUT, and unlink or relink a video clip's sound, each through the existing reducer operations and each undoable; it says where loudness normalisation really happens (for the whole export, not per clip); and when a clip cannot take an operation it shows the reason the reducer or the service gives.
currentBaseline: The inspector is the inline `<section className='inspector'>` in `editPanel` (`src/main.tsx`) with the headings `clip.sound.heading` (enable checkbox and gain), `clip.dissolve.heading`, `clip.transform.heading`, `clip.animation.heading` and `title.heading`. It has no speed, LUT or unlink control. For a clip that cannot carry sound it shows a hint (`clip.sound.notVideo`, `clip.sound.noAudio`).

Speed: `yamakan.clip.setSpeed` and the `clip.setSpeed` operation exist (`project:write`, mutation). The reducer case in `core/timeline/operations.ts` refuses titles ('Titles do not support retime.'), clamps silently to 1/100..5/1 (`clampRetimeRate`, `MIN_RETIME_RATE`, `MAX_RETIME_RATE` in `core/retime/rate.ts`), leaves `durationTicks` unchanged and does not check the source length; `core/canonical.ts` checks 'Clip extends beyond its source.' without the speed factor. A speed that reads past the end of the source is therefore accepted today; what preview and export show for it is not verified. `setClipSpeed` in `src/edit-ops.ts` is imported by `tests/set-speed.test.ts` and `tests/browser-command-history.test.ts` and returns the project unchanged when the reducer refuses.

LUT: `yamakan.lut.import` (`project:write`, mutation; `.cube` text up to `LUT_LIMITS.sourceBytes`, LUT_3D_SIZE 2 to 33, 0 to 1 domain, no other keywords; name 1 to 120 characters; compare-and-swap on `expectedRevision` and `expectedContentHash`) stores an immutable `lut` document. A clip uses it through `clip.setEffects` with a `lut` effect (`documentId`, `contentHash`; 'A clip has at most one LUT.'). No file under `src/` calls `yamakan.lut.import`. `setClipTransform` in `src/edit-ops.ts` keeps an existing LUT when the transform changes.

`yamakan.document.list` returns each document's id, kind, schema version and content hash but no name; a LUT's name is inside its content, read with `yamakan.document.get`. `DOCUMENT_LIMITS.documentsPerProject` is 32 (defined in `core/document-ref.ts`, re-exported by `core/documents.ts`).

Unlink and relink: `clip.unlinkSound { clipId, audioTrackId, audioClipId }` and `clip.relinkSound { clipId, audioClipId }` exist as operations and as commands. `unlinkVideoSound` (`core/audio/unlink.ts`) needs a video-track media clip whose asset has an audio stream and whose `sound.enabled` is true, and a free place on an unlocked audio track; it adds an audio clip with the same asset, range, gain, fades and speed and disables the embedded sound. `relinkVideoSound` needs only matching asset ids: it removes the audio clip and re-enables sound with the audio clip's gain and fades, so the audio clip's moved or trimmed position is discarded. Nothing records which audio clip came from which video clip. `clip.setSound` refuses 'Relink the unlinked audio clip before enabling embedded sound.'

`operationsBetween` in `src/edit-diff.ts` emits `clip.setSpeed` and `clip.setEffects`, so speed and LUT changes made on the local view commit through today's path. It never emits `clip.unlinkSound` or `clip.relinkSound`; those need the `editIntent` path that MPR-601 part a adds.

Loudness normalisation is not a clip operation. It is the `normalizeLoudness` flag of `yamakan.export.video` and `yamakan.export.batch` (`core/audio/loudnorm.ts`, `DEFAULT_LOUDNORM_TARGET`: -16 LUFS integrated, -1.5 dBTP, LRA 11), and the UI never passes it. The brief's wording 'loudness normalisation' in the clip inspector conflicts with this.
The line `data-testid='preview-parity'` in `src/main.tsx` already names `lut` and `extremeRetime` among the things the browser preview does not show the way the export does (`core/render/parity.ts`).
interfaces: No new command, scope, schema or project format. Used unchanged: `yamakan.project.applyBatch` carrying `clip.setSpeed` and `clip.setEffects` (through `edit` and `operationsBetween`) and `clip.unlinkSound`, `clip.relinkSound`, `track.add` (through `editIntent`); `yamakan.lut.import` (`project:write`, not human-only, receipt kept under the request id, strict bounded path-free input); `yamakan.document.list`, `yamakan.document.get`, `yamakan.document.capability` (read only).

`src/inspector/clip-controls.ts` (new, pure, no React): `speedFromPercent(percent: number): { num: number; den: number }` (integer 1 to 500, reduced by the greatest common divisor); `SPEED_PRESETS` (25, 50, 100, 150, 200, 400 percent); `maxSpeedForSource(clip, asset): { num: number; den: number } | null` (null when the asset has no duration); `refusalOf(p: Project, operations: Operation[]): string | null` (applies with `applyLocal` in a try/catch and returns `refusalText` of the thrown error); `relinkCandidates(p, clipId)` (audio-track clips with the same `assetId`, only when the video clip's `sound.enabled` is false); `unlinkTarget(p, clipId): { trackId: string } | { newTrack: true } | { refused: string }`; `lutName(fileName: string): string` (extension, control and direction characters removed, at most 120 characters).

`src/edit-ops.ts` additions: `setClipLut(p, clipId, lut: { documentId: string; contentHash: string } | null)` (keeps the transform, mirrors `setClipTransform`); `unlinkSoundOps(p, clipId, ids: { audioClipId: string; newTrackId: string })` (returns `clip.unlinkSound` alone, or `track.add` for an audio track followed by `clip.unlinkSound`); `relinkSoundOps(p, clipId, audioClipId)`. `setClipSpeed` stops catching the reducer's refusal.

tasks.objective: The existing Finish panel gains an export section that offers exactly what the export commands accept and nothing more: the loudness option for a single export, up to four output sizes exported as one batch with per-output status, cancel and download, and an OTIO export that shows the loss report from `yamakan.project.otioLosses` before the file can be downloaded. The Finish workspace is `<section className='finish' data-testid='finish-panel'>` in `src/main.tsx`: the `workspace.finish` heading, `workspace.finishIntro`, the output line `data-testid='finish-output'` (frame size and length) and the captions panel. It has no export settings.

`yamakan.export.batch` (`render:execute`, mutation, refuses a request id and asks for the idempotency key; `idempotencyKey` 1 to 60 characters; 1 to 4 `variants` of `{ name, width, height }` with name matching `/^[a-z0-9-]{1,16}$/`, even width 16 to 1920 and even height 16 to 1080; optional `normalizeLoudness`), `yamakan.export.batchStatus` (`job:read`; `{ projectId, batchId }`; returns state COMPLETED, RUNNING, FAILED or CANCELLED and one job view per output with its variant) and `yamakan.export.batchCancel` (`render:execute`, mutation) are in `core/command/registry.ts` and are exercised by `tests/relink-variants.test.ts`. No file under `src/` calls any of them.

The export encoding is fixed in `core/render.ts`: an MP4 file with H.264 video (`libx264`, preset veryfast, CRF 20, Rec.709 limited range) and AAC sound at 192 kbit/s. No command input selects a codec, bitrate, container or frame rate. `core/render/plan.ts` states that pictures are fit inside the frame (letterboxed), and the summary of `yamakan.export.batch` says each output size is rendered 'with the same contain fit'. The donor file `src/editor/utils/exportSettings.ts` defines wider export options that no command accepts.

Loudness: with `normalizeLoudness` the job view carries `loudness` (off, pending, measured with `inputI` and `targetI`, unmeasured, unknown); the target is `DEFAULT_LOUDNORM_TARGET` in `core/audio/loudnorm.ts` (-16 LUFS, -1.5 dBTP, LRA 11); a sound that cannot be measured is refused with 'This sound is too quiet or too short to measure, so it cannot be normalized. Export without normalizing loudness.' (`tests/loudness-export.test.ts`).

OTIO: `yamakan.project.otioLosses` and `yamakan.project.exportOtio` (`project:read`, input `{ projectId }`) return an `OtioLossReport` (`core/interchange/otio.ts`: `carried` track and clip counts, `losses` rows of subject, id, field and effect 'dropped' or 'yamakanOnly', and the referenced `media` with name, hash and bytes); `exportOtio` returns `{ timeline, report }` (`tests/otio-commands.test.ts`). No file under `src/` calls either.

`RESOURCE_POLICY` v3 (`core/command/policy.ts`) allows one active render worker (`activeRenderWorkers`), so the outputs of a batch are rendered one after another; a batch can be refused with 'Not enough free disk space for this batch's exports.' or 'Too many active jobs.'
interfaces: No new command, scope, schema or project format. Used unchanged, with their existing scopes and human-only rule: `yamakan.export.video` (now with `normalizeLoudness` when chosen), `yamakan.export.batch`, `yamakan.export.batchStatus`, `yamakan.export.batchCancel`, `yamakan.job.cancel`, `yamakan.project.otioLosses`, `yamakan.project.exportOtio`. tasks.title: Add first run: locally built sample project and an honest capability banner
tasks.objective: A person who opens Yamakan with no project sees, in the existing empty state, (1) a banner built only from the service's capability commands that says what works on this PC, what needs their own remote account, and what is unavailable and why, and (2) one button that builds a small sample project on this PC from FFmpeg test patterns, with no download, no model, at most 64 MiB of disk, and only when pressed. The sample is an ordinary project that can be edited and exported.
currentBaseline: With no project open every workspace renders `emptyPanel()` in `src/main.tsx`: `<section className='empty'>` with `empty.title`, `empty.body` and `empty.persist`. It offers no sample and says nothing about what this PC can do.

Capability facts are spread over several places: the 'Local engine' panel (`data-testid='engine-panel'`, which calls `yamakan.engines.comfyui` only when its check button is pressed), the generate controls (`yamakan.engines.capabilities` in `src/main.tsx` and `src/director/DirectorPanel.tsx`, `yamakan.generation.options`) and the Blender panel (`yamakan.blender.capability`). `yamakan.studio.capability`, `yamakan.scene.capability` and `yamakan.director.capability` are not called from `src/`.

`yamakan.engines.capabilities` returns, per operation, `available`, `verified`, a `reason` (ENGINE_DISABLED, WEIGHTS_ABSENT, HARDWARE_UNQUALIFIED, RIGHTS_UNQUALIFIED; `core/engines/reasons.ts`) and a message; the keys `engine.reason.*` exist in `src/i18n.ts`. `yamakan.generation.options` returns `route` ('kaggle' or null). `yamakan.blender.capability` returns `available`, a version and a reason.

`yamakan.project.create` (`project:write`, mutation, name 1 to 120 characters) creates an empty project. No command builds sample media, and the list of `yamakan.project.*` commands in `core/command/registry.ts` has no delete, so a project stays until its workspace data is removed.

The service starts FFmpeg only through `workers()` in `core/process/workers.ts` (one `ProcessOwner`; on Windows the binary is pinned by `PINNED_SHA256` under `vendor/ffmpeg-win64-r8`). The queue in `core/jobs.ts` runs one job at a time (kinds `export`, `blender-render`, `blender-track`, `cfr-derivative`). `submitDerivative` is the precedent for a job whose output becomes an asset through `stageAsset` and `attachAsset` (`core/store.ts`); the upload handler in `server/main.ts` requires the caller to be authorised for `yamakan.export.video` before it queues that job.
`importMedia` in `src/main.tsx` already waits for such a job and then calls `yamakan.project.open` and `accept(opened)`; that is the pattern for adopting a project a job has changed.
Qualification scripts synthesise their media with FFmpeg lavfi sources (for example `scripts/qualify-playback.mjs`); the repository holds no sample media and nothing downloads any.
The founder host has integrated graphics, 16 GiB of memory and very little free disk; `RESOURCE_POLICY` v3 keeps `diskReserveBytes` of 256 MiB free and is frozen.
interfaces: New command `yamakan.project.createSample`: scope `project:write`; mutation; not human-only (the same rule as `yamakan.project.create`); refuses a request id and asks for the idempotency key, as `yamakan.export.video` does, and the same key returns the same project and job. Its handler also requires the caller to be authorised for `yamakan.export.video`, as the upload path does before `submitDerivative`. Input, strict and path-free: `{ name: string 1..120, idempotencyKey: string 1..80 }`. No input value reaches an FFmpeg argument. Output: `{ project, job }` with the job view `yamakan.job.status` returns. Refusals before anything is created: 'Not enough free disk space for the sample project.' and the queue's existing 'Too many active jobs.'. Available over REST and MCP alike.

New job kind `sample-media` in `core/jobs.ts`, queued by a new `submitSample(projectId, idempotencyKey)` modelled on `submitDerivative`, with payload `{ specVersion: 1 }`. It is cancelled with `yamakan.job.cancel` and follows the queue's existing interruption rules. It adds no table and no scheduler.

`core/sample/spec.ts` (new, pure): `SAMPLE_SPEC_VERSION = 1`; `SAMPLE_LIMITS = { totalBytes: 64 MiB, itemBytes: 24 MiB, itemWallSeconds: 60, items: 4 }`; `SAMPLE_ITEMS`, four fixed entries of `{ assetName, output, args }`: a six-second 1280 by 720 `testsrc2` picture at 30 frames a second with a 440 Hz `sine` tone (H.264 and AAC in MP4), a four-second `smptebars` picture without sound (MP4), one `testsrc2` frame (PNG), and an eight-second 220 Hz `sine` tone (16-bit WAV, 48 kHz); `sampleOperations(project, assets, ids): Operation[]`, at most one batch that adds a video and an audio track when the project has none and four `clip.add` operations.

`src/firstrun/capability-tiers.ts` (new, pure, no React): `type Tier = 'here' | 'remote' | 'unavailable' | 'notChecked'`; `capabilityTiers(results): { id: string; tier: Tier; reasonKey: MessageKey | null; message: string | null }[]`, where each entry of `results` is a capability command's result or `{ failed: true }`. Rows: `editing` (always 'here'), `blender`, one row per operation of `yamakan.engines.capabilities` ('here' only when `available` and `verified` are both true), `remoteGeneration` ('remote' only when `route` is 'kaggle'), `studio`, `scene`, `director`. A failed call or a shape the mapper does not recognise is 'notChecked', never 'here'.

`src/firstrun/FirstRun.tsx` (new), rendered inside `emptyPanel()` below the three existing lines. Props: `call`, `t`, `lang`, `busy`, `onOpen(project)` (the existing `accept`). Test ids: `first-run`, `first-run-capability`, `first-run-capability-row-<id>`, `first-run-recheck`, `first-run-sample`, `first-run-sample-note`, `first-run-sample-status`, `first-run-sample-cancel`, `first-run-error`.

New message keys in `src/i18n.ts`, English and Arabic: banner heading, the three group headings, row labels, 'Not checked', the sample button, the note ('Builds four short test-pattern files on this PC with the bundled FFmpeg. Nothing is downloaded. Uses at most 64 MiB of disk.'), the job states and the sample project's default name.
tasks.sourceDecision: BUILD — a small job that drives the already pinned FFmpeg through the existing process owner and queue, plus one panel in the existing empty state; nothing is imported and no media is committed. Rejected: committing sample media and fetching it from the page (it adds binary files to the repository and a provenance record for them, and the instruction for this card is that the sample is built locally from FFmpeg test patterns); and running the encoder inside a synchronous command (it would start an encoder outside the one-job-at-a-time queue).
sourceReuse: `core/process/workers.ts` `workers()` and `mediaTools()` for every FFmpeg run, with the memory and thread limits the other job handlers pass.
`core/jobs.ts` `submitDerivative` and its handler as the model for the new kind; the free-space check `submitBatch` applies before admitting a batch.

`core/store.ts` `create`, `stageAsset`, `attachAsset` and `applyOperations`, so sample media goes through the same probe, hash and content-addressed store as an upload and the timeline is one ordinary revision.
`src/main.tsx` `accept` and the wait-then-open pattern of `importMedia`; the existing `engine.reason.*` strings.
implementationSequence: Verify live main and confirm the empty state offers no sample and no capability summary, or record ALREADY_SATISFIED with evidence. The handler runs each `SAMPLE_ITEMS` entry through `workers()` in the job's work folder with `-nostdin`, the policy's render threads, the worker memory limit and a wall limit of `itemWallSeconds`; refuses an output larger than `itemBytes` or a running total above `totalBytes`; skips an item when the project already holds an asset with that name (so a re-run after an interruption adds nothing twice); stages and attaches each output; then applies `sampleOperations` as one revision through `applyOperations`.

Part a. Add `yamakan.project.createSample` to `core/command/registry.ts`: first look for an existing `sample-media` job with this idempotency key in any project and, when one exists, return its project and job; otherwise check free disk (`diskReserveBytes` plus twice `SAMPLE_LIMITS.totalBytes`) and the active-job limit, then create the project at 30 frames a second, then queue the job. Extend `tests/request-id-refusal.test.ts` and whatever lists `tests/parity.test.ts` reads so REST and MCP both expose it. First pull request.

Part b. Banner `first-run-capability`: three labelled lists ('Works on this PC', 'Needs your own remote account', 'Unavailable'), each row with its reason from `engine.reason.*` or the command's message (`dir='auto'`). It reads no hardware in the browser and names no model, GPU or speed. The remote row says the work runs on the person's own Kaggle account and quota, not on this PC, and appears only when `route` is 'kaggle'.

Part b. Sample: `first-run-sample` with the note beside it. A press calls `yamakan.project.createSample` with the translated default name and one idempotency key, then polls `yamakan.job.status` once a second, showing state and progress in `first-run-sample-status` (`role='status'`) with `first-run-sample-cancel` (`yamakan.job.cancel`). On COMPLETED it calls `yamakan.project.open` and `onOpen`. On FAILED or CANCELLED it shows the service's text, says the project exists with the files built so far, and offers to open it.

Part b. Add `scripts/qualify-first-run.mjs` and the npm script `qualify:first-run`; run it on the Windows host with Edge; commit `docs/evidence/qualification/first-run.json` with head SHA and host; re-run `npm run qualify:engine-panel` unedited. Second pull request.
acceptance: On a fresh workspace the empty state shows the banner and the sample button; both are reachable and operable by keyboard alone with visible focus, in English and in Arabic with a right-to-left page.

Every banner row equals what the capability commands returned at that moment: no row is 'Works on this PC' unless its command said available (and, for engine operations, verified); a failed call shows 'Not checked'. On the founder host local generation is listed as unavailable with the service's reason.

Nothing is built, created or written until the sample button is pressed. One press creates exactly one project; a repeated press or a retried request with the same key returns the same project and job.

The finished sample project has four assets and four clips, opens in the Edit workspace, plays in the preview, and exports through the existing export; its assets total at most 64 MiB, and the measured total is in the receipt.
During first run and the sample build the browser makes no request to another origin and the service starts no process other than the pinned FFmpeg and ffprobe.

Before the press, the button's text says that the sample project stays in the workspace (step 0 confirms that no command removes a project; the review found none).

When `yamakan.generation.options` answers `route: null`, the first-run panel says 'Video generation is not set up on this PC. It needs a route you set up and approve.' With a route it states the recipe's expected minutes, the clip length and that a run cannot be stopped once started.
testPlan: `tests/sample-project.test.ts` (new): `SAMPLE_ITEMS` has four entries whose arguments contain only fixed strings, no path separator outside the output name and no network protocol; durations and sizes match the card; `sampleOperations` applied with the reducer to an empty project and to a project that already has tracks yields a project that passes canonical validation with four clips; the command's input schema rejects an extra key, an empty name and a 121-character name.

`tests/jobs.test.ts` (extend): `submitSample` with the same key returns the same job; it is refused when the active-job limit is reached and when free disk is below the reserve plus 64 MiB, and in both cases no project is created.

`tests/capability-tiers.test.ts` (new): a table of command results to rows, including available but not verified, each reason code, `route` null, a failed call and an unrecognised shape; no input yields 'here' without `available: true`.
`tests/request-id-refusal.test.ts` and `tests/parity.test.ts` (extend as their lists require) for the new command; `tests/engine-absence.test.ts` passes unedited.
`npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run test:e2e`, `npm run provenance:check`, `npm run brand:check`.
negativeTests: A caller with `project:write` but without the scope of `yamakan.export.video` is refused and no project is created.
Too little free disk: the command refuses with its message, no project and no job exist, and the button shows the message.
The job is cancelled midway: the project exists with the assets attached so far and no half-written asset; a second build is a new project, and nothing is silently retried.
A capability call fails or times out: the row reads 'Not checked'; the sample button still works.
An input with a `path`, `url` or `args` key is rejected by the strict schema.

tasks.title: Add a continuity journey test: one project through Create, Story, Edit, Finish and back
tasks.objective: One automated journey proves that a single project can be started in the simple workflow (Create: prompt or brought-in media to a placed clip), taken into the advanced workflows (Story with shots, takes and the Cinema panel; Edit with the timeline, sound and captions), and brought back, with every hop keeping the same canonical project and every clip, take, shot, caption and scene still editable afterwards. The journey reports a loss as a failure; it does not hide one.
currentBaseline: The four workspaces are views of one project: `WORKSPACES = ['create', 'story', 'edit', 'finish']` in `src/workspaces/ProjectShell.tsx`, a tab list with ids `workspace-tab-<name>` and arrow, Home and End key handling. There is no separate 'simple' or 'advanced' mode and no second project format; this card uses 'simple' for Create and Finish and 'advanced' for Story and Edit. Cinema is a panel inside Story (`cinema-viewport`, `cinema-project-save`), not a workspace.

Each surface has its own qualification script and receipt: `scripts/qualify-create-workspace.mjs`, `scripts/qualify-take-review.mjs`, `scripts/qualify-director-cinema.mjs`, `scripts/qualify-cinema-activation.mjs`, `scripts/qualify-captions-keyboard.mjs`, `scripts/qualify-kaggle-screens.mjs`, `scripts/qualify-edit-equivalence.mjs`. Each starts its own project. None carries one project through all of them and compares what each hop left unchanged.

`scripts/browser-e2e.mjs` (`npm run test:e2e`) is one long linear journey for the editing path with an Arabic and keyboard step; `tests/journey.test.ts` covers import and scenes at store level. Neither goes Create to Story to Edit and back.

The service can show the whole state the comparison needs without new commands: `yamakan.project.export`, `yamakan.document.list` and `yamakan.document.get` (which also carry the project's Cinema scene, a creative document), `yamakan.take.list`, `yamakan.project.history`.

Generation in a browser journey on this host is only possible through the stand-in Kaggle command line `scripts/fixtures/fake-kaggle.mjs`, wired by environment variables as `scripts/qualify-kaggle-screens.mjs` does (Windows only). The stand-in engine `core/engines/fake.ts` is created inside tests and is not reachable from a running service. No real generation runs on this host.

A generated or imported clip is flattened pixels. Editability in this product means the clip on the timeline, the take and shot it belongs to, the reference pack, the caption document and the scene document; nothing in the code offers layers inside a generated clip.
Blender is optional on the host; `yamakan.blender.capability` reports whether it is available and the panel shows `cinema-blender-unavailable` when it is not.
interfaces: No new command, scope, schema, store or product behaviour. The journey uses only existing commands with the launch session's scopes.

`scripts/lib/continuity-sections.ts` (new, pure, beside `scripts/lib/frame-checks.ts`): `sectionHashes(state): Record<SectionName, string>` returns the sha256 of the canonical JSON (sorted keys, the rule of `core/hash/canonical.ts`) of each section of `state = { project, documents, takes }`. Sections: `assets`, `tracks`, `clips`, `sound` (the sound fields of clips), `story`, `takes`, `referencePacks`, `captions`, `cinemaScene`, plus `revision`. `changedSections(before, after): SectionName[]`. `HOPS`, the fixed table of hops with, for each, the sections it is allowed to change (an empty list for a hop that only switches workspace).

`scripts/qualify-continuity-journey.mjs` (new; npm script `qualify:continuity`). Receipt `docs/evidence/qualification/continuity-journey.json`: head SHA, host, browser version, and per hop `{ id, from, to, action, allowed, changed, verdict }` with verdict PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED and a reason; reopen timings as measured; counts of page errors and of requests to other origins.

Product files change only if a step cannot be driven because a control has no stable `data-testid`; then only the attribute is added (`src/main.tsx`, `src/workspaces/ProjectShell.tsx`), and the pull request lists each one.
tasks.sourceDecision: BUILD — a new qualification script and a small pure comparison helper on the pattern of the existing `scripts/qualify-*.mjs`; nothing is imported. Rejected: lengthening `scripts/browser-e2e.mjs`, which is already one long linear script whose early failure hides every later step.
sourceReuse: The service and browser start-up, launch link and receipt writing of `scripts/qualify-create-workspace.mjs` and `scripts/qualify-take-review.mjs`.

The stand-in Kaggle wiring of `scripts/qualify-kaggle-screens.mjs` (`YAMAKAN_KAGGLE_CLI`, `YAMAKAN_KAGGLE_USERNAME`, `KAGGLE_FAKE_NODE`, `KAGGLE_FAKE_SCRIPT`, `KAGGLE_FAKE_SCENE`) and `scripts/fixtures/fake-kaggle.mjs`, unedited.

Existing test ids: `create-generate`, `create-generate-start`, `create-bring-in`, `create-place`, `story-packs`, `story-refresh`, `take-review`, `take-review-open`, `take-proposal`, `take-proposal-apply`, `cinema-viewport`, `cinema-project-save`, `cinema-project-reopen`, `cinema-project-state`, `cinema-blender`, `cinema-blender-unavailable`, `captions-panel`, `captions-text`, `captions-save`, `shell-unsaved`, `finish-panel`.
FFmpeg lavfi sources for the brought-in media, as the existing scripts use.
implementationSequence: Verify live main and confirm no script or test carries one project through all four workspaces and back, or record ALREADY_SATISFIED with evidence. Then walk the journey by hand once against the real service and write down, in the pull request, the result shapes of `yamakan.project.export`, `yamakan.document.list`, `yamakan.document.get` and `yamakan.take.list` (the section names in this card are provisional until then), every control that lacks a test id, which arrow key moves forward in the tab list when the page is right to left, and any hop that already loses or changes data. A loss found here is reported to the coordinator before the script is written.
Add `scripts/lib/continuity-sections.ts` with `sectionHashes`, `changedSections` and `HOPS`, and `tests/continuity-journey.test.ts`.

Add `scripts/qualify-continuity-journey.mjs`, part 1 (simple workflow): fresh temporary workspace, real service, Edge. Create a project; in Create, generate one clip through the stand-in Kaggle route when the host is Windows, and bring in one FFmpeg-made clip in every case; place both (`create-place`). On a host where the stand-in route cannot run, the generation hop is BLOCKED with the reason and the journey continues with the brought-in clip.

Part 2 (advanced, Story): switch to Story with the keyboard; save a story with two shots that use the two clips; open take review and apply one take proposal; save a reference pack if step 0 shows the control; in the Cinema panel save the scene (`cinema-project-save`) and reopen it (`cinema-project-reopen`). A Blender render is attempted only when `yamakan.blender.capability` says available; otherwise the hop is BLOCKED and the script asserts `cinema-blender-unavailable` is shown.
Part 3 (advanced, Edit): switch to Edit; trim one clip, move one clip, change one clip's sound gain, add one caption line and save it.

Part 4 (back): switch to Create and place the brought-in clip a second time; switch to Story and confirm the shots, takes and scene are as saved; switch to Edit and trim the clip that was generated in part 1 and the clip placed in part 4; undo and redo that trim; switch to Finish and run one export to completion.

After every hop fetch the state through the commands, compute `sectionHashes`, and compare with `HOPS`: a section outside the hop's allowed list that changed is FAIL. After parts 2, 3 and 4 reload the page and reopen the project and require identical hashes. Hops that only switch workspace must change nothing, including `revision`, and must not raise `shell-unsaved`.

Run the whole journey a second time with the interface in Arabic (right-to-left page), switching workspaces by keyboard only and asserting that the focused tab is the one `document.activeElement` reports and that it has a visible focus indicator.

Add the npm script `qualify:continuity` to `package.json`, add the journey to the 'Complete human and agent journey' section of `docs/E2E_ACCEPTANCE.md` as a required receipt, run on the Windows host and commit `docs/evidence/qualification/continuity-journey.json`.

If a hop is FAIL, do not weaken the allowed list or the comparison. Record the defect with the hop's before and after sections, name the card that owns the surface, and keep this card open until the fix has merged and the receipt is PASS.
acceptance: One project id is used from the first hop to the last; no step creates, duplicates or converts a project, and no step uses a file path.
Every hop's changed sections are inside its allowed list, and every reload and reopen gives identical section hashes.

After the round trip: the generated clip and both placed clips can be trimmed in Edit and the trim can be undone and redone; the applied take can be replaced again through take review; the caption line can be edited and saved; the Cinema scene reopens with the saved state; the export at Finish completes and its artefact downloads.

The receipt names, hop by hop, PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED with a reason. A hop that needs Blender or the stand-in Kaggle route and cannot run is BLOCKED, never PASS, and the receipt's overall verdict is PASS only when no hop is FAIL and the only BLOCKED hops are those two kinds.
The journey runs in English and in Arabic with a right-to-left page, with workspace switching by keyboard alone and visible focus on the active tab.

During the journey the browser makes no request to another origin, the page raises no error, and no model, provider account or download is used; the receipt says that real generation was not exercised.

The journey runs one export and at most one Blender render, one job at a time, inside `RESOURCE_POLICY` v3; its temporary workspace is removed at the end so the host's disk is not consumed.
compatibilityRequirements: No product behaviour, command, schema or format changes. Added `data-testid` attributes are the only possible product edits.

definitionOfDone: Merged by a normal merge with a fresh independent review and exact-head CI; main verified after the merge.
`docs/evidence/qualification/continuity-journey.json` is committed with head SHA and host and an overall verdict of PASS under the rule in the acceptance list; every BLOCKED hop has its reason.
`docs/E2E_ACCEPTANCE.md` names the journey and its receipt.
Every defect the journey found is either fixed and merged or is the recorded reason the card is still open.
risks: The journey may find a real loss on current main (this is not verified either way). Then the card cannot close until the owning surface is fixed; the rule in the last sequence step keeps the test honest and the card open.

A long browser journey is prone to timing flakiness on a constrained host. Each hop waits for the service's own state (revision, job state), not for fixed delays, and a hop that times out is FAIL with the last observed state, not retried silently.

The section names depend on result shapes that are not verified here; step 0 fixes them. If a section cannot be separated (for example sound fields from other clip fields), it is merged with its neighbour and the allowed lists are widened only by that merge, with the reason in the pull request.
Generation is exercised only through the stand-in route on Windows; on other hosts and in CI the generation hop is BLOCKED and coverage comes from the brought-in clip.

Nothing checks that an Arabic string is correct, and nothing stops a string changing after someone has reviewed it.

tasks.title: Write a provenance manifest beside every export and a readable report from it
tasks.objective: Every finished video export has a bounded, hash-bound manifest stored beside it that states which project revision, clips, media, generation records, models, licences, consent ids and tool versions produced the file, and a person or an agent can read that as a plain provenance report. The stored manifest never holds a prompt, a seed, a name or a host path.
currentBaseline: Facts read at `4a8e1b5`. The baseline `7b1ca46` adds only PR #278 (six files: four code and test files of the Blender render path and two documents), which changes no fact stated here. `core/jobs.ts` `JobSupervisor` `#runExport` renders the job's frozen revision through `renderRevision`, renames the result to `exports/<jobId>/render-<attempt>.mp4` and commits through `#succeedIn`, which stores the artifact path and plan hash on the job and a JSON receipt in the `attempts.receipt` text column. Nothing about origin, licence, consent or tool versions is written.

`server/main.ts` serves an export only through `GET /api/v1/jobs/<jobId>/artifact` (authorised as `yamakan.job.status`, scope `job:read`) and only when the artifact matches `exports/<uuid>/render-<n>.mp4`. Its comment states that backups do not carry exports and a restored workspace exports again. `core/command/registry.ts` has `yamakan.export.video`, `yamakan.export.batch`, `yamakan.export.batchStatus`, `yamakan.export.batchCancel` and `yamakan.job.status`; no command returns provenance for an export.

`core/project.ts` `AssetSchema` holds id, name, kind, hash, extension, bytes, duration and dimensions. An asset has no origin, licence or generation field, so origin can only be derived: `core/engines/generation.ts` `GenerationRecord.imported` holds `{assetId, lineage}` and `GenerationLineage` holds output hash, input hashes, recipe id and hash, model manifest hash, seed and prompt hash. Those records live in the jobs table (`JobSupervisor.generationLedger`), not in the project document; MPR-101 moves a content-addressed record onto the take.

Tool identities exist but no export states them: `vendor/ffmpeg-win64-r8/BUILD.json` (`receipt`, `ffmpegVersion`, `ffmpegSha256`, `ffprobeSha256`, `libassVersion`), `core/process/workers.ts` `mediaTools()` (verifies the vendored binaries by SHA-256), `core/render.ts` `RENDERER_VERSION`, and `core/blender/runtime.ts` `BLENDER_PIN` (version and commit).
The service has no build identity: `package.json` says version `0.1.0` and a search of `core`, `server`, `cli`, `sdk` and `mcp` finds no code that reads a commit or build id.

Consent records are in `core/identity.ts` (`ConsentRecordSchema`) and the `likeness_consents` and `consent_revocations` tables of `core/store.ts`. `yamakan.consent.list` needs scope `consent:grant` from the browser session because it returns names; reference pack entries carry a `consentId` readable under `project:read`.

Start-up recovery in `core/jobs.ts` removes an interrupted attempt's output by exact name (`render-<n>.mp4` or `track-<n>.json`) and `#removeEmptyJobFolder` uses `rmdir`, which leaves a folder that still holds a file. Any new file in `exports/<jobId>/` must be named in both places or it is orphaned.
No C2PA or other content-signing code or dependency exists in the repository; the term appears only in research notes under `docs/research`.
interfaces: New schema `ExportManifestSchema` in `core/export-manifest.ts`, strict at every level: `format: 'yamakan.export-manifest'`, `formatVersion: 1`, `subject`, `project`, `tools`, `media`, `clips`, `consents`, `notRecorded`, `manifestHash`. This is a receipt format, not a project format; `core/project.ts` `formatVersion` does not move.

`subject`: `{ kind: 'video' | 'otio', jobId, attempt, sha256, bytes, container: 'mp4', width, height, frameRate: {num, den}, durationFrames, hasAudio, normalizeLoudness }`. This card writes only `kind: 'video'`; `'otio'` is reserved for MPR-702, so the version 1 schema already accepts the `'otio'` form, in which `jobId`, `attempt`, `container`, `width`, `height`, `frameRate`, `durationFrames`, `hasAudio`, `normalizeLoudness`, `project.planHash` and the `ffmpeg`, `ffprobe` and `libass` entries of `tools` are null (no job ran and no FFmpeg was used), and a test parses one such value.

`project`: `{ id, revision, snapshotHash, planHash }`, where `revision` is the job's frozen revision, `snapshotHash` is the canonical hash of that revision and `planHash` is the value `#succeedIn` already stores.

`tools`: `{ yamakan: {version, commit | null}, rendererVersion, ffmpeg: {receipt, version, sha256}, ffprobe: {sha256}, libass: {version}, blender: {version, commit} | null }`. `blender` is non-null only when at least one clip has origin `rendered`. `ffmpeg.receipt`, `ffmpeg.version` and `libass.version` are stated only when the binaries run are the pinned build that `mediaTools()` verified (it checks SHA-256 on Windows only; the Ubuntu CI job runs the tests with the system FFmpeg); otherwise they are null and listed in `notRecorded`, and `sha256` is that of the binary actually run.

`media[]` (at most 200, one entry per asset used on the timeline, sorted by `sha256`): `{ assetId, sha256, kind, bytes, origin: 'imported' | 'generated' | 'rendered', recordHash | null, promptHash | null, model: {id, manifestHash, licence | null} | null, licence | null, consentIds[] (at most 16) }`. The asset `name` is never copied, because it is usually the original file name. `promptHash` is written only when the person opted in for that export under FD-2, the same choice that allows prompt text; otherwise it is null and `recordHash` alone links the media to its record, which stays in the workspace.

`clips[]` (at most 200, sorted by track order then start): `{ clipId, trackKind, startTicks, durationTicks, sourceStartTicks, assetId | null, origin: 'imported' | 'generated' | 'rendered' | 'title', take: {documentId, storyContentHash, shotId, takeId} | null }`.

`consents[]` (at most 64): `{ id, purpose, state: 'active' | 'revoked' }` at the moment of export, never a name, label or encoding. `notRecorded[]` (at most 600): `{ subject: 'asset' | 'clip' | 'build', id, field }` for every value the project does not hold, for example the licence of imported media or the build commit.

`manifestHash`: SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the manifest without `manifestHash`, using `canonicalJson` and `sha256Hex` from `core/hash/canonical.ts`. `EXPORT_MANIFEST_LIMITS = { clips: 200, media: 200, consents: 64, notRecorded: 600, bytes: 1048576 }`.

New pure functions in `core/export-manifest.ts`: `buildExportManifest(input)`, `verifyExportManifest(text)` (bounds before parse, schema, `manifestHash` recomputed), `provenanceReport(manifest, extras?)` returning `{ sections, text }`, and `buildIdentity()` (version from `package.json`; commit from environment variable `YAMAKAN_BUILD_COMMIT` when it is 40 lower-case hex characters, otherwise null and listed in `notRecorded`).

Stored file: `exports/<jobId>/manifest-<attempt>.json`, two-space JSON with LF line ends and a final newline. The attempt receipt gains `manifestSha256` (SHA-256 of the stored bytes). The job view returned by `yamakan.job.status` and each output of `yamakan.export.batchStatus` gain `manifestSha256: string | null`. No SQL schema change.

New read command `yamakan.export.manifest`: scope `project:read`, `mutation: false`, input `z.object({ jobId: Id }).strict()`, returns `{ manifest, sha256 }` after checking the file against the receipt's `manifestSha256`. Not human-only; no receipt and no request-id rule because it changes nothing.

New read command `yamakan.export.provenanceReport`: scope `project:read`, `mutation: false`, input `z.object({ jobId: Id, prompts: z.enum(['hash', 'text']).optional() }).strict()`, returns `{ report, text }` with `text` at most 65536 characters of English plain text. `prompts: 'text'` is refused with `VALIDATION` until FD-2 is recorded; after that the prompt is read from the MPR-101 record at read time and shown only when the manifest carries a `promptHash` (an opted-in export) and the prompt's hash equals it.
tasks.sourceDecision: BUILD: a small Yamakan receipt format built from the same frozen revision the renderer used, stored beside the artifact and delivered by two read commands; C2PA signing is DEFER. No existing module states export provenance, and a signed standard manifest needs a signing identity and a certificate that are release decisions under X-02 and would cost money the founder has not approved.
sourceReuse: `core/hash/canonical.ts` `canonicalJson` and `sha256Hex`, as `core/takes.ts` `proposeReplace` uses them for a proposal hash.

`core/jobs.ts` `#runExport`, `#succeedIn` and the fault points `before-publish`, `after-publish` and `before-succeed`; the Blender track job in the same file is the precedent for a JSON file in `exports/<jobId>/`.
`core/process/workers.ts` `mediaTools()` and `vendor/ffmpeg-win64-r8/BUILD.json` for the FFmpeg identity; `core/blender/runtime.ts` `BLENDER_PIN`; `core/render.ts` `RENDERER_VERSION`.

The generation record and take reference that MPR-101 lands, and the catalog entry of MPR-201 for a model's licence. Until those exist the manifest reads `core/engines/generation.ts` `GenerationRecord.imported` through `JobSupervisor.generationLedger().list(projectId)`.
`tests/jobs.test.ts` fault-injection helpers and the real-service harness of `tests/parity.test.ts`.
No third-party code. The C2PA specification and its open-source implementations are not imported by this card [ASSUMED: at least one implementation is permissively licensed; not checked].
implementationSequence: Verify live main and reproduce the gap: on a temporary workspace run one `yamakan.export.video` to completion, list `exports/<jobId>/` and confirm it holds only `render-1.mp4`; confirm the catalog has no command containing `manifest` or `provenance`; record the names MPR-101 gave the generation record schema, its hash field on the take and its Blender record. tasks.title: Carry clip lineage in OTIO metadata and make the OTIO import proposal appliable
tasks.objective: An OTIO export states, per clip, where the clip came from in one namespaced metadata dictionary and comes with the same manifest a video export has, and an OTIO file read back becomes a hash-bound proposal batch a person can apply as one undo step. Lineage read from a file is checked against the project's own records and is never written from the file.
currentBaseline: Facts read at `4a8e1b5`. The baseline `7b1ca46` adds only PR #278 (six files: four code and test files of the Blender render path and two documents), which changes no fact stated here. `core/interchange/otio.ts` `toOtio(project)` writes flat string metadata only: `yamakan_clip_id`, `yamakan_timeline_start`, `yamakan_effects` and `yamakan_transition` on a clip, `yamakan_asset_id` and `yamakan_content_hash` on its media reference, `yamakan_project_id` and `yamakan_format_version` on the timeline. The types declare `metadata?: Record<string, string>`. No origin, take, generation record, model, licence or consent id is written.

`fromOtio(raw, assets)` returns `OtioProposal { name, clips, unresolved, ignored }`. It reads only the named metadata keys, bounds the whole file with `OTIO_LIMITS` (`maxBytes` 16 MiB, `maxDepth` 32, `maxString` 4096, `maxObjects`), refuses an invalid `yamakan_effects` or `yamakan_transition`, matches media by `yamakan:asset:<id>`, metadata asset id or content hash, and never opens an address in the file. An unread metadata key is not counted in `ignored`: the reader counts only an unread `global_start_time`, `source_range`, `effects`, `markers` and a false `enabled`, so counting a malformed `yamakan` dictionary is new behaviour.

`core/command/registry.ts` has three OTIO commands, all scope `project:read` and `mutation: false`: `yamakan.project.otioLosses`, `yamakan.project.exportOtio` (returns `{ timeline, report }`, the timeline as an object) and `yamakan.project.proposeOtio` (returns the proposal and changes nothing). No command turns the proposal into timeline operations.

The pieces an appliable import needs exist separately: `core/timeline/operations.ts` `OperationSchema` (`track.add`, `clip.add`, `clip.setEffects`, `clip.setTransition`, ids supplied by the caller as UUIDs) and `BatchSchema` (1 to 64 operations), applied by `yamakan.project.applyBatch` (scope `project:write`, with `expectedRevision` and a receipt). The only hash-bound proposal today is `core/takes.ts` `TakeProposalSchema`, applied by `yamakan.take.apply`; MPR-303 generalises it to operation batches.

`docs/evidence/ultimate/SS-015-interchange.md` states that the card stays open, lists what a proposal leaves out and what an export drops, and records that HTTP and MCP cap a request at 2 MiB, so `proposeOtio` reads less through them than the 16 MiB its reader allows.

CI job `otio-oracle` in `.github/workflows/qualify.yml` runs `scripts/write-otio-fixture.mjs` and then `scripts/otio-oracle.py` against `docs/evidence/qualification/otio-fixture.otio` with OpenTimelineIO installed from `scripts/ci/otio-requirements.txt`. The oracle checks the rate of every `source_range` and does not look at metadata.
`core/project.ts` limits a project to 16 tracks, 200 clips, 200 assets and a ten-minute timeline.

External behaviour: OpenTimelineIO is Apache-2.0 [DOC]. Whether third-party editors keep an unknown metadata dictionary through their own OTIO export is [UNKNOWN]; one user report says a DaVinci Resolve OTIO import keeps most metadata but leaves clips unlinked [IND]. Nobody in this project has run a round trip through a third-party editor.
interfaces: OTIO clip metadata gains one nested dictionary under the key `yamakan` (the type becomes `Record<string, string | OtioLineage>`): `{ lineage_version: '1', origin, asset_sha256, take_document_id, take_shot_id, take_id, record_hash, prompt_hash, model_id, model_manifest_hash, licence, consent_ids }`. Every value is a string of at most 128 characters except `consent_ids`, an array of at most 16 strings; a value the project does not hold is omitted, never written as empty. Existing flat `yamakan_*` keys are unchanged.

OTIO timeline metadata gains `yamakan: { lineage_version: '1', manifest_format: 'yamakan.export-manifest', manifest_format_version: '1', project_revision, snapshot_hash }`. The file does not contain the manifest's hash, because the manifest contains the file's hash.

`toOtio(project, lineage?)` and `otioJson(project, lineage?)` take an optional lineage lookup built by the resolver MPR-701 lands in `core/export-manifest.ts`; without it the output is byte-identical to today's.

`yamakan.project.exportOtio` (scope and input unchanged) returns `{ timeline, text, report, manifest }`: `text` is the exact `otioJson` output, and `manifest` is an `ExportManifestSchema` value with `subject.kind: 'otio'`, `subject.sha256` the SHA-256 of the UTF-8 bytes of `text`, and the same `media`, `clips`, `consents` and `notRecorded` a video export of that revision would state. Nothing is stored.

`otioLossReport` gains fixed entries: per carried clip that has lineage, `{ subject: 'clip', field: 'lineage', effect: 'yamakanOnly' }`; per project, `dropped` entries with fields `generationRequests`, `consentRecords` and `shotHistory` when the project holds any. `OtioLoss` keeps its shape.

`yamakan.project.proposeOtio` stays scope `project:read`, `mutation: false`; input gains optional `offset: z.number().int().min(0).max(200)`. The result gains `sourceSha256`, `lineage: { matched, absent, mismatched: [{ clip, field }] }` (at most 200 entries, where `clip` is the clip's index in the proposal) and `batch`.

`batch` is either the operation list to file with `yamakan.proposal.create` (`{ projectId, expectedRevision, operations, operationsHash }`, where `operationsHash` is MPR-303's hash of the operations; MPR-303's `proposalHash` exists only after filing, because it also covers the author, the filing time and the expiry), with `covers: { fromClip, toClip }` and `next: number | null`, or `null` with `reason` one of `unresolvedOnly`, `empty`, `trackLimit`, `clipLimit`, `durationLimit`. Its operations are only `track.add`, `clip.add`, `clip.setEffects` and `clip.setTransition`.

No new mutation command. The caller files the returned batch with `yamakan.proposal.create`, and it is applied with `yamakan.proposal.apply` (MPR-303) under that command's own scope, receipt and review rule. Until MPR-303 lands nothing in this card writes.
tasks.sourceDecision: ADAPT: extend the existing reader, writer and loss report in `core/interchange/otio.ts` and reuse the MPR-701 lineage resolver and the MPR-303 batch, rather than build a second importer or a new apply command. A nested dictionary under one application key was chosen over another flat `yamakan_lineage` JSON string because it stays readable in other tools [ASSUMED: one top-level key per application is the OpenTimelineIO convention; the oracle step checks that the library reads it back].
sourceReuse: `core/interchange/otio.ts` `toOtio`, `fromOtio`, `otioLossReport`, `otioJson` and `OTIO_LIMITS`.
The lineage resolver and `ExportManifestSchema` from MPR-701 (`core/export-manifest.ts`), so OTIO metadata and the manifest are two projections of one lookup and cannot disagree.
The proposal batch builder and apply command of MPR-303; `core/timeline/operations.ts` `OperationSchema` and `applyBatch` for the operations themselves.
`scripts/write-otio-fixture.mjs`, `scripts/otio-oracle.py` and the pinned `scripts/ci/otio-requirements.txt` (OpenTimelineIO, Apache-2.0 [DOC]) for the independent read; no new dependency.
`tests/otio.test.ts`, `tests/otio-commands.test.ts` and the restore path qualified by `tests/portable-closure.test.ts`.

Extend `yamakan.project.exportOtio`: resolve lineage for the current revision, build `text`, hash it, and build the manifest with `subject.kind: 'otio'`. Keep `timeline` in the result so existing callers do not break.

Part b, import. In `fromOtio`, read `metadata.yamakan` through a strict bounded schema. A malformed dictionary is counted in `ignored` under `Clip.metadata.yamakan` and the clip still imports, because nothing from the dictionary is ever applied. Compare each claimed value with the project's own lineage for the matched asset and fill `lineage.matched`, `absent` and `mismatched`.

Build the batch in the command, not in `fromOtio`: one `track.add` per file track that has at least one resolved clip (name cut to 80 characters, `Imported` when empty), one `clip.add` per resolved clip at its exact start, duration and source start, then `clip.setEffects` and `clip.setTransition` where the file carried Yamakan's validated values. A transition's `fromClipId` is rewritten from the outgoing clip's `yamakan_clip_id` in the file to that clip's new derived id; when the outgoing clip is unresolved, absent, or not the clip that ends where this one starts on the same new track, the transition is left out and counted in `ignored`, because `core/transitions.ts` refuses a batch whose transition names any other clip. A `lut` effect whose document id and content hash do not name a LUT document of this project is left out of the effect stack and counted in `ignored`, because `core/store.ts` refuses that commit. Unresolved clips are never added. Existing tracks and clips are never moved, replaced or removed.

Derive every new track and clip id as a UUID from SHA-256 over the literal `otio-import`, `sourceSha256`, the track index and the clip index, so the same file proposed twice at the same head gives the same operations and the same `operationsHash` (MPR-303's `proposalHash` also covers the author, the filing time and the expiry, so it differs between filings) and a page applied twice is refused. The derived value must set the UUID version and variant bits, because `Id` in `core/project.ts` is `z.uuid()`.

Page the batch: fill it in file order until either MPR-303 proposal limit would be passed (640 operations or 192 KiB of canonical bytes; `BatchSchema` itself holds 64, and MPR-303 applies a proposal in slices of 64 within one revision) and return `next` as the index of the first clip not covered, or null. Each page is proposed against the head at that moment, so a file larger than one batch is applied as several undo steps; the result states how many.
Refuse to build a batch that would exceed 16 tracks, 200 clips or the ten-minute timeline; return `batch: null` with the reason and leave the rest of the proposal readable.

Extend `scripts/write-otio-fixture.mjs` with one clip that has lineage, regenerate `docs/evidence/qualification/otio-fixture.otio`, and extend `scripts/otio-oracle.py` to assert that OpenTimelineIO reads `metadata['yamakan']` on that clip as a dictionary with the expected keys and that writing the timeline back through the `otio_json` adapter keeps it.

tasks.title: Run the supervised-agent measure M14 with a scripted agent, a budget and a forced restart
tasks.objective: The supervised-agent measure `M14` (hypothesis H-E) exists as evidence instead of only as a definition. A fixed scripted agent, acting over MCP with an agent token, produces the F4 brief (2 scenes, 6 shots, about 17 seconds) from imported media under a budget envelope, with approval points and one forced service restart, 20 times. For each run the record states whether the budget was overrun, whether any human-only operation ran without an approved request, whether any acknowledged work was lost and whether the export was delivered, each against the threshold fixed before the run. Nothing is compared with another product and no language model is involved.
currentBaseline: Facts read at main `7b1ca46`. No script, test or card runs `M14`: `10_BENCHMARK_AND_EVALUATION.md` defines the measure and hypothesis H-E, and every result there is `NOT TESTED`.

The frozen protocol 1.1.0 (`docs/evidence/ultimate/benchmark-protocol.json`) names category H, agentic production: 20 pilot briefs, imported assets first, generated later. Its pilot note says a pilot estimates variance only and establishes no superiority.

`scripts/qualify-agent-access.mjs` (npm script `qualify:agent-access`) starts the built service on a temporary workspace, creates a scoped token through the page and proves that it works and can be revoked. It runs no production. `scripts/measure-creative-recovery.ts` measures backup and restore latency on synthetic workspaces. `tests/interruption.test.ts` and `tests/creative-recovery.test.ts` cover recovery on small fixtures.
`mcp/main.ts` already takes an agent token from `YAMAKAN_AGENT_TOKEN_FILE` or `YAMAKAN_AGENT_TOKEN`, connects only to the loopback service and derives its tools from the service catalog.

Thirteen commands are human-only on main, among them `yamakan.generation.start` and `yamakan.generation.import`. An agent cannot call them, so an approval point exists only where the agent files a request and a person decides it; main has no such request.

What the measure needs and main lacks: a job wait and an event cursor (MPR-502); media import for an agent client (MPR-503); approval requests for human-only commands (MPR-504); budget envelopes (MPR-505, and through it the preflight of MPR-203, the gates of MPR-204 and the job attribution of MPR-507); the audit feed (MPR-506); and protocol v2, which carries the `M14` threshold (MPR-801).

`scripts/fixtures/fake-kaggle.mjs` is the existing stand-in for the Kaggle command-line tool, and `scripts/qualify-kaggle-screens.mjs` builds a launcher for it with the Windows C# compiler. The stand-in opens no connection and uses no quota.

Part a. Write `scripts/lib/scripted-agent.mjs` and `tests/scripted-agent.test.ts`. The agent's script for one run: create a project with `yamakan.project.create` at the protocol's deliverable frame rate, passed as `frameRate` (the default is 30 frames a second); import five pack clips through `yamakan_media_import`; ask `yamakan.generation.preflight` for three different stand-in requests; call `yamakan.generation.start` directly once (it must be refused); file the three start requests with `yamakan.approval.request`, each carrying its `preflightHash` (the third must be refused by the budget); poll `yamakan.approval.status`; after the approved start, poll `yamakan.generation.status`; file the `yamakan.generation.import` request for its own generation and wait for the decision; save the story with two scenes and six shots and assemble it; start `yamakan.export.video`; wait with `yamakan.job.wait`.

Give every mutation that keeps a receipt a request id derived from the seed and the step, and retry it with the same id after a failed or unanswered call. For a command that refuses request ids, read state first (`yamakan.approval.status`, `yamakan.events.read`, `yamakan.handoff.read`) and repeat the call only if its effect is absent. The agent stops on a declined request and never asks again for the same input.

Write `scripts/benchmark-agent.mjs` on the harness of `scripts/qualify-approvals.mjs`: a temporary workspace; the built service with the stand-in launcher; the MCP server process started with `YAMAKAN_MCP_IMPORT_DIR` pointing at a folder the script fills with five locally built clips; Edge driven by `playwright-core` as the approver. Before the agent starts, the approver records the egress and spend gate approvals for the stand-in route with the page button of MPR-204, then creates the agent token in the page with scopes `project:read`, `project:write`, `render:execute`, `job:read` and `job:control` and this envelope: `generations: 2`, `quotaSeconds` and `egressBytes` set to twice what one preflight of the stand-in request reports, `currencyMinor: 0` and a `wallSeconds` limit. During the run the approver approves one start request, declines the other and approves the import request, each in the inbox of MPR-504.

Forced restart: at the seam the seed picks, the script terminates the service by the process id it started, waits for the port to close, starts the service again on the same workspace and port, and lets the agent go on. The script never terminates a process by image name and never rewrites the agent's token file.

After the restart and before the agent continues, check and record: a request filed before the restart is still `pending` (a restart does not change the epoch); the gate approvals still read `approved`; the budget numbers are unchanged; a generation that was running is either still followed or has ended with a stated failure. The agent then continues from what it reads, not from what it remembers.

After each run, check and record five things. Completion: the export job succeeded and the file passes the export check of `M11` (from MPR-802 when merged; otherwise container, one H.264 video stream, one AAC stream and a duration within one frame of the timeline, read with the owned `ffprobe`). Budget: `yamakan.budget.read` shows spent plus reserved at or below the limit on every dimension, and the stand-in recorded exactly one push. Approvals: in `yamakan.audit.read`, read as the browser principal, every ended human-only operation that names the agent carries the id of an approved request with the same input hash, and the direct start appears only as a denied row. Acknowledged work: every revision the agent was given is in `yamakan.project.history`, and `yamakan.events.read` answers `reset: false` for the cursor saved before the restart. No duplicate effect: one project, one generation and one export job.

Part b. Counted run: `npm run benchmark:agent -- check`, then `measure`: 20 runs from clean workspaces with seeds drawn by `prng` seeded with the first 32 bits of the protocol hash read as an unsigned integer; the five seams get four runs each, in an order shuffled by the same `prng`, so the allocation is fixed before the first run and no seed is redrawn. While the protocol file is still a draft the runs are recorded with `pilot: true` and no PASS or FAIL is stated; the counted runs are made after the freeze.

Write `docs/evidence/ultimate/benchmark-v2-observations-agent.json`, the receipt and `docs/evidence/ultimate/MPR-805-supervised-agent.md` (what ran, what was a stand-in, every refusal seen, every deviation). Update the `M14` cell of `docs/evidence/ultimate/product-matrix.md` from the receipt only, and log deviations in `docs/evidence/ultimate/benchmark-v2-deviations.md`.
acceptance: `M14` passes only when all 20 counted runs complete with zero budget overruns, zero human-only operations without an approved request and zero lost acknowledged work. The 95% Wilson lower bound for 20 of 20 is 0.839, above the 0.8 floor [ASSUMED floor, from the protocol]; 19 of 20 gives 0.764 and fails.

In every run the agent's direct `yamakan.generation.start` is refused, the third filing is refused with `LIMIT_EXCEEDED` in the fixed budget wording, and the declined request starts nothing: the stand-in records exactly one push.
After the forced restart the agent finishes without repeating an acknowledged mutation, and a request that was pending before the restart is still pending after it.

Fewer than 20 counted runs, a failed host check, a missing tool or a missing dependency card makes the measure BLOCKED with the counts stated, never PASS. A run against a draft protocol is a pilot and states no verdict.
The receipt and the evidence file say in plain words that the agent was a fixed script, who or what approved, that the generation was a stand-in, and that nothing was compared with another product.
testPlan: New `tests/scripted-agent.test.ts`, without a browser: the script retries a receipt-keeping mutation with the same request id; for a command that refuses request ids it reads state before repeating; it stops on a declined request; it never calls a tool the server did not list; the seed fixes the seam and the order of requests.

Same file, the per-run checks on synthetic records: a budget row above its limit is an overrun; an ended human-only row without an approved request is a violation; a missing acknowledged revision is lost work; a refused filing is none of these.
Same file, the verdict rule: 20 of 20 passes, 19 of 20 fails, 19 runs is BLOCKED, and a draft protocol gives `pilot: true` and no verdict.
The measure is not part of `npm test`. `npm run benchmark:agent -- check` and one `run --seed 1` are made by hand on the founder host before the counted run.
negativeTests: The stand-in launcher cannot be built (no Windows C# compiler) or no browser channel is present: the result is BLOCKED and no run is counted.
The agent token is created without an envelope: every filing is refused with 'Agent budget: none set.' and the run is recorded as not completed, not as a pass of the budget check.
The approver is told to approve a request whose input hash differs from the one shown: the approval is refused and nothing starts.
An approved request replayed after the restart starts nothing a second time: the stand-in still records one push.
The script file contains no call that ends a process by image name; a test reads the file and asserts it.
`report` rejects a receipt whose head SHA differs from the checked-out head or whose protocol hash differs from the pinned one.
e2eQualification: `npm run benchmark:agent -- check`, then `measure`, on the founder host (Windows 11, Edge, the owned FFmpeg) on mains power, from a clean checkout at the recorded head. The run uses a real service process, the real MCP server, a real browser for the approver and a real hard kill of the service. The generation is the stand-in: no network connection, download or spend occurs.

Evidence: `docs/evidence/ultimate/MPR-805-supervised-agent-receipt.json`, the observations file and `docs/evidence/ultimate/MPR-805-supervised-agent.md` with the head SHA, the host, the protocol hash and state, the 20 per-run records and every refusal text. A step that could not run is recorded BLOCKED with its reason, never PASS.
performanceCriteria: The run stays inside the frozen `RESOURCE_POLICY` of `core/command/policy.ts`; no limit is raised for the measure.
One run at a time: one service, one MCP server, one browser. A run that has not delivered its export within 15 minutes is recorded as not completed [ASSUMED limit, fixed before the run].
The time from the kill to the first answered call is recorded for each run. It is reported, not judged, because no threshold for it was fixed in advance.
Temporary workspaces and exports are removed after each run, and free disk is checked before each run against the disk reserve of the resource policy.
compatibilityRequirements: The agent is a fixed script. `M14` therefore measures what the platform guarantees under supervision; it does not measure an agent's creative ability or a language model's reliability. A model-driven agent is a separate, later measure that needs founder-approved spend.
Runs approved by page automation are labelled `automation-stand-in`. They measure the mechanism a person would use, not a person's judgement; usability is `M12`.
The stand-in route is a test fixture. Its use says nothing about the real Kaggle route, which stays NOT TESTED in this card.

Models and providers stay off. No download and no spend happens in this card. Pack media, exports and workspaces stay outside the repository; no prompt text, credential, token or host path is committed.
No command, scope, schema, store or project format changes. SS-008 keeps its own scope and state; this card references it and does not close it.
The frozen protocol 1.1.0 file is not edited. Operator time in MPR-802 excludes agent productions; this card is where they are counted.
definitionOfDone: The runner, the scripted agent and their tests are merged and the common checks pass.
The receipt, the observations and the evidence file of the counted run exist at a recorded head, or the card is recorded BLOCKED with the reason and the counts.
`M14` in `docs/evidence/ultimate/product-matrix.md` reads PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED or NOT TESTED exactly as the receipt does. A FAIL is published as FAIL with its evidence.
Every deviation from the protocol is in the deviations log.
risks: A scripted agent can pass where a model-driven agent would not. The claim is limited in writing to the platform's guarantees, and the wording is fixed in the evidence file.
The harness needs the Windows C# compiler and Edge. On another host the measure is BLOCKED, as in `scripts/qualify-kaggle-screens.mjs`.

A hard kill while a remote generation is being followed may leave the stand-in run ended as lost. That run is recorded as not completed and counts against the floor: it is a finding, not a harness fault to be retried away.
The interfaces of MPR-502 to MPR-506 may land with different names. Step 0 records the real ones and the script uses those.
Twenty runs give a wide interval: 20 of 20 only bounds the completion rate above 0.839. The result must be quoted with n and the interval.
The envelope is sized from the stand-in's own estimate, so the quota and egress dimensions are exercised only at fixture scale.
The agent in M14 is a script that replays a fixed task over MCP; a model-driven agent is NOT TESTED and no card tests it.
blockingExternalRequirements: A counted verdict needs protocol v2 frozen (MPR-802 part a, which includes the founder's review of the pilot values). Until then the runs are a pilot and state no verdict.
A person-approved run is optional and needs a person the founder names; the counted runs do not wait for it.
tasks.rollback: Revert the pull request: the runner, the scripted agent, the test and the npm script go. Evidence files of a counted run stay as evidence; if one is wrong it is corrected by a new dated entry, not deleted. No project format, store or command changed, so no data needs migration.
